children.translated_text: Having saluted the Supreme Lord (Parameśa),
and then the sage <s>Bharadvāja</s>,
the knowledge that came in succession from <s>Hara</s> through <s>Indra</s> —
listen, O ones of excellent vows!
In the sacred hermitage of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,
<s>Bharadvāja</s> and other Brāhmaṇas
performed austerities, having installed <s>Śiva</s>,
with minds fixed solely on Him.
Then, having considered them devoted,
the lord of the thirty [gods] once
visited that hermitage,
himself assuming the guise of an ascetic.
He, honored by them, having inquired
after the well-being of all of them,
said: 'Why is the dharma of Vedic injunction
not being followed?'
They said: 'Is not this dharma
ordained by Vedic injunction, O sage —
the means of propitiation of the deity,
for the accomplishment of one's desired ends through tapas (austerity)?'
'In the Veda there is the Raudrī Saṃhitā,
the deity to be addressed is <s>Rudra</s>,
and for making Him present,
the prescribed ritual method is the Kālpika rite.'
Even when thus told, the Lord, wishing to know
their deeper conviction, laughingly
said to them: 'Your knowledge is false —
for the deity is merely a word.'
'If [the deity] is merely a word,
when sacrificers at different places [invoke] simultaneously,
she cannot come to be present [at all locations],
since she would be corporeal like us.'
'And no means of valid knowledge (pramāṇa)',
'that is uncontradicted, appears to establish that.'
'That [Vedic] statement is otherwise established,
and where are the good speakers among worldly discourses?'
Thus by the flood of atheistic words,
propelled like the ocean by the tide,
by <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) — their mountain-like intellect
did not move, due to the weight of its substance.
'The form of the deity is never
like our bodies;
she is endowed with supreme sovereignty —
therefore that is not an [appropriate] example.'
'If so, the [same] reasoning would apply to a pot —
like the word Indra, because of being a word.'
'But the word pot does not hold water,
the word moon does not shine.'
'Then let the [Vedic] statement have another referent,
being expressive of <s>Śakra</s> and the like.'
'How would words for action, form, and the like
have meaningfulness [in that case]?'
'All discourse too would be false.'
'Because it has a root, that is not reasonable.'
'If beings had no root [cause],
all activities would be destroyed.'
'<s>Upamanyu</s>, having seen <s>Hara</s>,
became free from anger, a sage.'
'How can his words be false,
he by whom the ocean is controlled?'
'Seized by the serpent-noose
emitting a garland of poison-flames,
he was freed by the Lord with a mere roar.'
'The White One (<s>Śiva</s>) has been seen by the wealthy ones.'
Thus through the continuation of debate,
seeing them delighted by praise of <s>Hara</s>,
with tears and choked voices,
<s>Hari</s> (<s>Indra</s>) became pleased.
The thunderbolt-bearing god <s>Śatakratu</s> (<s>Indra</s>)
showed his own form,
resembling the young sun,
being praised by the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>.
They praised him with Ṛg, Yajus,
and Sāman [verses], bowing down.
He said: 'State your wish,
even the highest in the worlds.'
They chose the knowledge of <s>Śiva</s>.
'Listen!' he said.
'But let there be one questioner among you,
approved by all the listeners.'
Then among them, the venerable <s>Bharadvāja</s>
became the leader.
Eloquent and bold, he questioned
the one honored by the gods, methodically.
'How did this supreme knowledge
come from <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord)?
And having established what in his mind,
did the Blessed One create this?'
'At the time of creation, <s>Maheśāna</s> (the Great Lord),
for the accomplishment of the aims of souls (<s>puruṣārtha</s>),
ordains pure knowledge
characterized by five streams.
'The multitude of words expressing what pertains to it,
the eight <s>Maheśvaras</s> who are the referents [of those words],
and the mantras numbering seven crores (seventy million),
on the supreme path (adhvan) —
'and eighteen additional
scriptures (śruta) for those presiding over <s>Māyā</s>,
the <s>Mantreśvaras</s> (lords of mantras) stationed
on the upper path, of radiance equal to the Lord's —
'among those, the Blessed One, manifest,
reveals [this knowledge] to the qualified ones for [their] accomplishment.'
'And the meaning that obtains
in others [too is from Him].'
'This knowledge, uttered by <s>Śiva</s>,
by the lords of mantras and lords of <s>Mantreśvaras</s>,
because it grants desires, is celebrated
as <s>Kāmika</s> in great detail.'
'Having learned from them, the Light of Vision,
with the tree of desire consumed by the garland of flames [of knowledge],
the Lord of <s>Umā</s> gave [it] to me,
over thousands of existences.'
'Leaving aside the elaboration therein,
by sūtras expressing the essential meaning,
I shall state the knowledge free from confusion,
mostly using those very [original] statements.'
'Now, <s>Śiva</s>, who is free from beginningless impurity,
the maker of all, the knower of all,
removes the web of bonds
of the soul (aṇu) previously bound.'
'The Lord of the world, having condensed
the great tantra of three topics and four sections
into a single sūtra,
then taught it in detail.'
'The creation, maintenance, destruction,
obscuration, and liberation of the world —
the function (kṛtya), with its instruments and fruits,
should be known: this alone is [the whole teaching].'
'By Him, established in His own nature,
who is the maker of the world, this must be so.'
'If [the maker were] established later [than creation], there would be infinite regress;
or liberation would be causeless.'
'Consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>), having the form of knowledge and action,
exists in the soul (<s>ātman</s>) always,
and in all directions — because in liberation
it is heard to be all-facing.'
'Though existent, because of not being manifest,
it appears to be obstructed.'
'It is under the control of Him whose power is unobscured;
that [soul] is thus [bound] precisely because of non-liberation.'
'The enveloping power and karma (action),
the product of <s>Māyā</s>, fourfold —
the web of bonds, in brief:'
'the [relevant] categories (dharma) have been stated only by name.'
'Thus, of these three categories of reality,
whose [theoretical] establishment was done in the first section,'
'the application through the sections on conduct (caryā), yoga, and ritual (kriyā)'
'will be stated.'
'The fruit of the application is liberation (mukti);
enjoyment (bhukti) too [comes] as a secondary result.'
'By the distinction of higher and lower,
these two are divided in many ways.'
'In the Vedānta, Sāṃkhya, [Jaina] existent-and-non-existent,
and <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> doctrines and others,
there is liberation together with its means.'
'What then is the distinction in the <s>Śaivāgama</s>?'
'Because the founders [of those systems] are not all-seeing,
the collection of realities is not clear [in them].'
'The means are fruitful accordingly.'
'In the <s>Śaiva</s> [system], all this is supreme.'
'In the Vedānta, there is one Ātman alone,
characterized by the manifestation of sentient and insentient.'
'This is merely an assertion —
on what basis is the conclusion established?'
'If the means of valid knowledge (pramāṇa) is there [in the Ātman],
the Ātman becomes an object of knowledge (prameya).'
'Where both of these are [present],
all four [pramāṇa categories] are established there.'
'Thus the non-duality would be lost;
otherwise, there would be no means of valid knowledge.'
'And [there would follow] equality of experience and non-liberation —
both of which are not desired by the proponents of Ātman.'
'In <s>Sāṃkhya</s> knowledge too, there is falsity,
because of cognizing cause in the effect.'
'And because the experiencer has no agency;
and also from [its] independence — because of being non-sentient.'
'In this [Jaina system] there would be seven categories:'
'jīva (soul), ajīva (non-soul), [and] three each of inflow and stoppage —'
'saṃvara (stoppage) and nirjarā (wearing away),
and also both bondage and liberation.'
'And all these are marked by <s>syādvāda</s> (conditional predication),
because of non-absoluteness.'
'That very thing is existent, that very thing is non-existent —
by whom is this ascertained?'
'Existent is something different, non-existent is something different —
if so, there is proving what is already proved.'
'Non-existent is inferior, existent is superior —
this too the wise say.'
'[If] both are not [present] in a single [locus], because of mutual dependence,'
'then both stand established [as different].'
'And if there is the state of being both existent and non-existent,
the existent is considered more fitting.'
'Because of the fear of confusion of actions thereby,'
'and they declared non-pervasiveness [of the soul] —
because of the absence of knowledge of the relation
between the universal and particular, [the soul being] non-sentient.'
'That which was non-pervasive before —
how would it become otherwise at the end?'
'If it has properties like expansion and the like,
then there follows a series of faults.'
'From the knowledge of the six categories [of <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>],
false knowledge ceases;
passion, aversion, and possessiveness,
and the particular qualities thereof —'
'they gradually cease,
since they arise from connection with the body.'
'That liberation has the form of inertness —
is not the liberated one then a corpse?'
'Of karma and the rest that manifest consciousness,
because of momentariness, again and again
[consciousness] is manifested even as it is born —
hence [consciousness] is considered momentary by others [the Buddhists].'
'That [is refuted] by experience of non-existent karma,
by memory of past experience.'
'Duration [of consciousness] in an annihilationist view —'
'there is no memory, nor karma.'
'[Consciousness] having the characteristic of destruction departs;
in liberation too there is no cessation of calamity.'
'And there is no experience whatsoever —
therefore the state of existence is preferable.'
'Thus, those of poor understanding who rely
on the views of those deluded by primordial ignorance,
seeking liberation,
are like those seeking fire from a firefly.'
'Whether the isolation (kaivalya) from the distinction of <s>Puruṣa</s> and <s>Prakṛti</s>,

children.translated_text: or the cessation from considering everything as <s>Brahman</s>,
or whatever liberations born from bonds —
all those undergo differentiation at [the next] creation.'
'One accomplished in the <s>Śaiva</s> [path] shines at the summit over all others;
liberated, he does not return again at creation.'
'Having supported all the world's misfortunes by his own radiance,
the lord of all lords abides forever, controlling [all].'
'Now, having perceived body and the rest —
entities that have the property of being effects —
we know the maker of this
as distinguished, through inference.'
'The distinction [of the maker is inferred] from the distinction of effects —
this is seen even in worldly affairs.'

children.translated_text: 'Whatever effect is of whatever kind and extent,
its cause is likewise.'
'[It is] eternal, because of no limitation by time;
not spatially located, because of the absence of duality.'
'Because of sequential and non-sequential production,
it has the power of producing sequentially and otherwise.'
'It has an instrument by which
action is seen to be [possible] — not [from] the absence of an instrument.'
'And it should be known as not derived [from anything else],
because of the beginningless establishment of the effect.'
'And the instrument is nothing other than power (śakti),
and power is not non-sentient, since it belongs to the sentient.'
'Because of non-restriction of objects — [it is] one;
in cognition and action, that is likewise.'
'The effect [such as] maintenance, birth, and the rest is not
from a seed, from <s>Prakṛti</s>, or from the atom.'
'By elimination, it belongs to <s>Maheśa</s> (the Great Lord) —'
'the liberated one: He is <s>Śiva</s> Himself.'
'If there is [objection of] non-apprehension of the relation,
the obstruction comes to some [particular] means of valid knowledge.'
'That [objection applies] to the opponent too — smoke is different
on a mountain than from a kitchen-fire.'
'In the world, action is seen to belong to an embodied [agent] —
and He too is like us [in that regard].'
'Because of the impossibility of [arising] from root-cause and the rest, the Lord's'
'body of power (śakti) is not like ours.'
'His body is [constituted] by the five mantras,
which serve the five functions (kṛtya):'
'<s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>, <s>Aghora</s>,
<s>Vāma</s>, and <s>Sadyojāta</s> — [corresponding to] head and the rest.'
'He rules the entire world
by a quality that revolves [in activity].'
'Because of being in the same position as the crown,
that [<s>Īśāna</s>] is the head — not a limb of the body.'
'Whichever body belongs to whichever [mantra],
by whichever [function] that [mantra] acts —'
'From protecting that, and also from expressing [it],
He has the face of <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>.'
'The heart is a synonym for awakening;
His <s>Aghora</s> [face is that] because He is <s>Śiva</s> (auspicious).'
'Because the thing possessed (parigraha) is terrible (ghora),
the designation Aghora is figurative.'
'<s>Vāma</s> [is so called] because of the leftness of the three goals of life;
and it is secret by nature.'
'The <s>Vāma</s> is the supreme, hidden abode
whose [face] is <s>Vāma-Guhyaka</s>.'
'The forms of the souls (aṇus) come into being instantly
by His mere will — hence He is called <s>Sadyojāta</s> (instantly born).'
'Or He instantly produces forms for yogins —'
'[He is] Sadyomūrti (of instant form) because of the swiftness of [His] action, not because of [having] a [material] form.'
'Thus [His] power (śakti), performing the body's function,
is called by the names of body because of the absence of a [material] body.'
'Those divisions such as <s>Vāma</s> and the rest'
'are also explained by the wise according to the division of functions.'
'He, having this form,
with this instrument of undiminished power,
always performs the function
that is appropriate at each time.'
'Therein, first, for the qualified souls alone,
He creates the eight [<s>Vidyeśvaras</s>],
endowed with powers such as <s>Vāmā</s> and the rest,
attended by seven crores [of mantras].'
'Among them are <s>Ananta</s> and <s>Sūkṣma</s>,
and also <s>Śivottama</s>,
<s>Ekanetra</s> and <s>Ekarudra</s>,
and <s>Trimūrti</s> of immeasurable splendor,'
'and <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> and <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>.'
'These are lords of lords, great kings.'
'Because of slightly unattained yoga,
they are appointable [as agents] by the Supreme One.'
'Even in their possession of omniscience and other yoga [powers],
their appointability is due to a trace of impurity (mala).'
'They are mutually distinguished [in rank],
and the mantras stationed below [are distinguished] likewise.'
'And they, prompted by the power of <s>Śiva</s>
manifest in the <s>Mantreśvaras</s>,
bestow grace upon souls
whenever and for whomever it is fitting.'
'That [grace], requiring the body of the performer,
having performed its function on the entire path —
at the end of [its] duration [the soul]
enters the state of <s>Śiva</s>, together with [its] lord.'
'Without an administering [agent], another [soul],
below the modification of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter),
having performed the function desired by the Lord,
departs when its own path-period is dissolved.'
'Then, manifest through <s>Ananta</s> and the rest,
truly [reaching] the knot (granthi) of the Lords,'
'for those whose bodies are begun from kalā and the rest,
He creates one hundred and eighteen [worlds].'
'Having entered those [worlds] too, the Blessed One
[enters] the rulers of worlds who are endowed with impurity (āñjana),
from whom all this [derives], and whose
power is bound to karma.'
'The founders of the scriptures for bound souls (paśu),
the bound souls who follow them,
those endowed with their own means and instruments,'
'stationed within the limits of the realm of time (kāla) —'
'In the [period of] maintenance, pervading all these
with His own radiance, along with [their] instruments,
He yokes [them] for the accomplishment of their own ends,
unperceived by beings.'
'Having withdrawn the means of experience,
having made [all] resort to the causal [state],
and having pervaded that [causal state] together with the souls,
He abides for rest.'
'Being well-disposed to all beings,
because beings are weary of existence,
having reached the end of the sleep [period],
He again proceeds as before.'
'Even in sleep He remains — awakening those fit for awakening,
obstructing those to be obstructed, ripening the karma of the doers,
making manifest the Māyā-powers fit for manifestation,
seeing everything — whatever category of being there is, as it is.'
'When the authority of the power of darkness
ceases, and upon its removal,'
'He manifests the infinity of knowledge and action'
'of the soul (aṇu), the friend of the world — [He is] <s>Śiva</s>.'
those whom he liberates in dissolution (<s>svāpa</s>),
they immediately become <s>Śivas</s>;
whether in dissolution or in creation,
whether atoms (<s>aṇu</s>) or lords (<s>pati</s>),
<s>Rudra</s>, <s>Mantra</s>, <s>Pati</s>, <s>Īśāna</s> —
they become sharers of those stations.
Those whom he graces during the [cosmic] maintenance (<s>sthiti</s>),
through a teacher (<s>guru</s>), [they attain] by the power of consciousness;
those embodied beings for whom the power (<s>śakti</s>)
descends even for cessation (<s>nivṛtti</s>) —
their sign of that is eagerness
for liberation and aversion to worldly existence;
devotion toward the devotees of <s>Śiva</s>,
and faith in the rites that teach that [path] —
by this, inference is possible, O learned one,
of the cause, even for those of coarse understanding.
For <s>paśus</s> (bound souls), seers (<s>dṛk</s>), <s>yogins</s>, and accomplished ones (<s>siddha</s>),
the two [types of] karmic manifestation are equal,
for those fit for the fruits beginning with the foremost (<s>jyeṣṭha</s>),
in the liberations that have [remaining] empowerment (<s>sādhikāra</s>).
Because of the distinction of means and [their] suitability,
that triad is further sought;
someone who manifests both [types],
distinguished by falling and accomplishment,
when the obstructive power of the lord of darkness
is slightly or half removed,
these signs arise
in embodied beings with some [mala] remaining.
Transcending even this triad of fitness,
<s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord)
graces [souls] repeatedly in dissolution (<s>svāpa</s>),
because this [grace] has [remaining] empowerment (<s>sādhikāra</s>).
At the root of creation, in the third [type],
in the dissolution of beings as in sleep,
that which he removes and [then] acts upon —
such a soul (<s>aṇu</s>) is spoken of.
Likewise, the seed of body and the like
he ripens through non-fixed placement;
it does not partake of fitness-limbs
immediately, like medicine and the like.
Even what is fit for ripening,
it cannot ripen itself by itself —
this is a common property (<s>dharma</s>)
of everything that undergoes transformation.
[<s>Śiva</s> is] omniscient because of being the maker of all,
together with means, instruments, and fruits;
that which one knows and does —
one is that very thing — this is well-established.
And because his [knowledge] is free from obstruction,
it does not depend on a revealer;
therefore it is not doubtful,
nor ever contrary [to reality].
Those [knowledges] that look to a revealer,
because they are covered by the powers of <s>mala</s> (impurity),
in accordance with the revealer,
they may be obstructed as well.
Neither perceptual, nor inferential,
nor verbal — the knowledge of <s>Śaṅkara</s>
shines forth, immaculate,
always, in all things.
That [knowledge], being one, because of the infinity of objects,
attains infinite divisions;
agency [too], because of non-difference from it,
is [spoken of] metaphorically as the same.
By [the cognitions of] existence, own-nature, instrument, purpose, what is to be accomplished, and sight,
partially arisen — those who know the reality of the Lord
liberate beings sunk in the mire of existence;
persons do not [need to know] at length the nature of the bonds of <s>paśus</s>.
Now, the characteristic of the Self (<s>ātman</s>),
the cause of the entire [universe], has been reached;
that is mostly covered in the teaching of the Lord,
yet an overview is stated [here].
The effect is earth and the rest; the maker is the Lord;
it is not useful for the maker [himself];
not for his own purpose, since [earth etc.] lack consciousness;
nor is it purposeless, because of the greatness of the maker.
By elimination, it is for the sake of another;
the knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>) is [that] other among those two;
the body is the other [i.e., the field], because it serves that [soul's] purpose;
earth and the rest too serve another's purpose, surely.
The body too, being unconscious, serves another's purpose
all the more evidently;
even if [one says it is] conscious — [no], because it is an object of enjoyment,
and because it is subject to change.
Objects of enjoyment and things subject to change are seen [to be]
devoid of consciousness, like cloth and the rest;
and where there is [a body], whether from existence [of consciousness] or not,
even in an existing corpse there is no consciousness.
If [one says consciousness comes] from a special transformation [of the body],
then there would be no memory [across states];
nor is this so, because [memory] is well-established;
therefore a rememberer other than the body exists.
Not non-pervading, not momentary,
not single, nor of inert nature,
not a non-agent, [but] conjoined with distinct consciousness —
at the end of bonds, <s>Śiva</s>-nature is heard [to arise].
Now, the bonds (<s>pāśa</s>) beginning with <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance)
are briefly described;
upon whose removal, the atoms (<s>aṇu</s>) [souls]
become lords of the world.
In the absence of bonds, the dependence [of the soul]
must be said — what is its basis?
If it is natural, then for the liberated,
the word 'liberated' becomes inapplicable.
Mastery is seen in one free from bondage;
subjection in one who is bound;
this much constitutes the bound-state
and the liberated-state of the bound and the liberated.
That dependence is bondage;
in that, if [bondage is] eternal, like consciousness and the rest,
the entire assemblage of means to liberation
is futile — enough with this notion!
Even the treasury of the eternal, pervading consciousness-power
for the accomplishment of [its] purpose
would not seek another power,
whether of <s>pāśa</s> or of <s>Śambhu</s>.
That covering (<s>āvaraṇa</s>) of this soul (<s>aṇu</s>)
has been sung in the fivefold stream of <s>Śaṅkara</s>'s [teaching]
by many synonyms,
[but it is] always unseen by <s>paśus</s> (bound souls).
By [the terms] animality (<s>paśutva</s>), animal-driving (<s>paśunīhāra</s>),
death (<s>mṛtyu</s>), delusion (<s>mūrcchā</s>), impurity (<s>mala</s>), collyrium (<s>añjana</s>),
ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), covering (<s>āvṛti</s>), disease (<s>ruj</s>), languor (<s>glāni</s>),
root of sin (<s>pāpamūla</s>), night (<s>kṣapā</s>), and the like.
That [<s>mala</s>] is one for all beings,
beginningless, dense, and great;
[its] ending is at its own time, abiding in each individual soul,
like a collection of digestive powers.
If that has existed beginninglessly — or [if] since some time,
then [state] its cause, [which must be] different from it;
if it obstructs even the liberated — then thus,
the effort for liberation would be false.
That is one, yet manifold in number,
because of such an origin [for each soul];
but its powers are many,
because simultaneous liberation [of all souls] is not observed.
The power of <s>Maheśvara</s> over those [malas],
gracious, benefiting all, is auspicious (<s>śivā</s>);
merely because it follows the [natural] law (<s>dharma</s>),
it is figuratively called a bond (<s>pāśa</s>).
It transforms these [malas]
until the end of obstruction, through the harsh activity [of existence];
when it effects the opening [of the soul],
then it is called gracious (<s>anugrāhikā</s>).
What <s>Śambhu</s> graces — consciousness and the rest —
because those [grace and mala] are mutually opposed,
simultaneously [they] are not possible; [then] how can the power
be benefiting all?
How is it fitting for the Lord of the world,
who has set forth for the benefit of beings,
to enter what is harmful
and [produce] pricking and piercing?
He does not grace the impurity (<s>mala</s>) of the soul (<s>aṇu</s>)
for the purpose of pricking;
rather, whatever is done,
is done through means, not otherwise.
In the darkness that has [remaining] empowerment (<s>sādhikāra</s>),
no one's liberation occurs;
the empowerment too ceases
through the transformation of that power [of <s>mala</s>].
That [transformation] too would not happen by itself
even for a suitable object;
because in every way and at all times
the unconscious is to be impelled by consciousness.
Just as a physician, though pricking
the patient with caustic and the like,
because he bestows the goal desired at the end,
is not regarded as a cause of suffering.
Because of the omnipresence of <s>Maheśa</s>,
his superintendence is not impeded;
nor where there is nothing to be done
does he assume indifference toward it.
The grace of a substance (<s>dharmin</s>) is [defined as]
conforming to the law (<s>dharma</s>) of that [substance];
there is never any [substance]
that is not conformed to by the Lord.
For the soul whose effort-energy of past empowerment
is [now] existing, [grace] increases;
for another <s>paśu</s>, there is grace
of action, because it serves that [soul's] purpose.
The conformity to the two properties (<s>dharma</s>)
of being a knower and being transformable
of the <s>mala</s> that has [remaining] empowerment (<s>sādhikāra</s>) —
[this occurs] at its cessation, upon its falling away.
Thus, both simultaneously
and sequentially, this is well-established indeed;
of <s>māyā</s> that has [remaining] empowerment (<s>sādhikāra</s>),
and of <s>karma</s> — this has been stated.
Now, the cause of the conjunction of consciousness
with sense-organs, body, and objects
is inferred from their coming-into-being,
because what has not come into being has no cause.
Because [<s>karma</s>] operates in a specific location,
because of variety, because of momentariness,
because of being fixed to each individual,
and because of continuity — it is a quality of that [soul].
Because it depends on the Lord, <s>avidyā</s>, and the like,
it is called a co-operative [cause];
<s>karma</s> (action), because it is produced by activity,
is <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen), because of its subtle nature.
It generates, sustains, and [produces] what is to be enjoyed;
it accomplishes three [purposes]: the personal (<s>adhyātma</s>) and the rest;
because it is the source of both truth and untruth,
it is of the nature of both <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.
In dissolution (<s>svāpa</s>), it undergoes maturation (<s>vipāka</s>);
upon its creation, it is utilized;
it operates in <s>māyā</s>, and at the end
what is not experienced does not dissolve.
Thus, operating from the time of <s>māyā</s>
until the end [of <s>kāla</s>], beginningless,
<s>karma</s> is also a revealer [of the soul's experiences],
[and] obstructive — [it is] not immediately for liberation.
Now, the characteristic of the bond called
'knot' (<s>granthi</s>), as understood through
the statement of the Omniscient One,
is described briefly, with some reasoning also.
That is the one inauspicious seed
of the world, possessing manifold powers,
co-operative-cause and empowerment ending,
obstructive, pervading, imperishable.
The property of the world by which an agent is inferred
as a cause — by that [same property]
a material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) too exists;
there is no cloth without threads.
That [material cause] must be unconscious,
because the effect is seen to be unconscious;
otherwise the defect of destroying everything is reached,
[and] there is no determination of cause [at all].
If this effect is impermanent,
why does it arise again?
If [the cause is] non-pervading, how could that be
all-facing for all?
Whatever is manifold, unconscious,
and seen to be subject to origination —
that does not [itself] have origination; therefore,
let a single [cause] be accepted.
A cloth is seen [to come] from a collection of threads;
everything [comes] from a single [source that is itself] from many;
that manifold too, from a single
seed, is born.
For those who hold that from a conscious cause
the unconscious too arises —
for them, why is water not inferred
by the sign of smoke?
For those for whom atoms are the cause
of the world from [its] beginning as elements —
for them, from the previously stated reason,
the subtlety of [those atoms'] knowledge is already known.
If body and the rest [come] from body and the rest,
then at the complete destruction [of all],
what talk [can there be]? Not total destruction [occurs] —
the Omniscient One would not speak falsely.
A property that is cognized
even in one part of a substance —
by whom is it prevented from arising
in that [substance] everywhere?
Having seen death millions of times
of composite embodied beings,
even that time is inferred
when the perishing of all beings [occurs].
Those effects that are its support,
in the form of powers at dissolution,
in the form of manifestation at creation —
they function for the accomplishment of purpose.
Taking up threads and such causes —
when cloth does not [yet] exist, for one desiring cloth;
when [cloth already] exists, even the word 'cause'
departs — thus the world is struck [with this problem].
Let the causal substance have its fruitfulness
in the arising of what was non-existent;
[then] let everything produce
everything desired from everything.
If [you say] what is impossible [comes] from what is possible —
what is your determining factor here?
I do not see any such [factor];
if [you say] it is power (<s>śakti</s>) — that is proving what is already proved.
Otherwise, because the activity
of the group of causes is unexplained;
scripture, [purposeful] taking up, and meaning
depart — thus that too is struck.
If there is a productive power,
[and] the effect is not of the nature of power —
the distinguishing mark between those two must be stated;
I do not see any such [mark].
Therefore, the determining power of a causal substance
that produces [its effect]
is ascertained by both positive and negative concomitance,
or by convention.
Its production from a different [form] is indeed
[possible] through resort to a [particular] set of causes;
by that [set], the form residing in the threads
obstructs the cloth-form.
When [the thread-form] is removed by a loom and the like,
then the cloth-manifestation is revealed;
just as [what was] hidden by a basket and the like —
by removing that, the cloth and the like [are revealed].
Manifestation is not made from non-being;
likewise, from the knotted state of <s>kalā</s> and the rest.
What is produced by the knot: <s>kalā</s>, <s>kāla</s> (time),
<s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>rāga</s> (attachment), the mothers of men (<s>nṛmātaraḥ</s>);
<s>guṇa</s> (quality), <s>dhī</s> (intellect), <s>garva</s> (ego), <s>citta</s> (mind), <s>akṣa</s> (senses),
<s>mātrā</s> (subtle elements), <s>bhūta</s> (gross elements) — in sequence.
What it brings about for the accomplishment of the body —
either directly or through an intermediate step,
how it connects and for what reason —
that is now explained as it truly is.
The agent-power of the soul (<s>aṇu</s>) is eternal
and all-pervading, like the power of the Lord;
[but] being concealed by darkness (<s>tamas</s>), in [relation to] objects
it does not shine — ungracious [i.e., without grace].
The reality (<s>tattva</s>) that graces that [agent-power]
is called <s>kalā</s>, luminous; <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>)
creates it by agitating <s>māyā</s>;
for it is the supreme limb of activity.
By that [<s>kalā</s>], which is like a lamp,
for the soul (<s>aṇu</s>) whose consciousness is unclear,
[<s>Śiva</s>] illuminates a portion [of its capacity],
piercing through the dense darkness.
This root '<s>kala</s>'
means both 'to count' and 'to impel';
that impelling, that driving forth —
that which does [this] to darkness is <s>kalā</s>.
Thus this pair, O Brahmin,
abiding together, inseparably,
in the procedure of enjoyment and action for beings,
they have been called agent and instrument.
Thus, [the soul], with the power of action made manifest,
desiring to see the domain of sight,
requires grace [for that],
being unable to see by itself.
For that purpose, the Lord, agitating
<s>kalā</s> itself which is capable of producing,
created the reality (<s>tattva</s>) called <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge),
the instrument of the supreme Self.
By that [<s>vidyā</s>], which is of the nature of illumination,
stimulating the knowledge-power,
[the soul], requiring the completion of all instruments,
perceives the supreme object.
With the consciousness-power thus manifested,
though it has seen the object, it still thirsts;
it does not attain that passion which generates [desire];
therefore the Lord created [<s>rāga</s>].
Colored by that [<s>rāga</s>], desiring
even impure objects of enjoyment,
it takes them up, but even while enjoying
does not attain dispassion.
Thus engaged, with instruments
established in [their] effects, along with [their] realms,
on the planes of enjoyment, it does not enjoy
the enjoyments that follow time.
The object of conditions such as <s>tuṭi</s> (moment) and the rest —
<s>kāla</s> (time) arises from <s>māyā</s>;
measuring from [the soul's] arising,
it regulates the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) through <s>niyati</s> (destiny).
Some have said that <s>karma</s>
is the regulator of enjoyment
together with its means, being dependent on <s>karma</s>;
what is beyond that is something else.
Enjoyment is the purpose of all <s>tattvas</s>,
and that too is dependent on <s>karma</s>;
let <s>karma</s> itself be body and the rest —
then everything becomes purposeless.
If [<s>karma</s>] depends on body and the like
for the accomplishment of the soul's purpose,
then, being dependent on <s>niyati</s> (destiny),
let <s>karma</s> be the regulator.
The <s>puṃs-tattva</s> (person-principle) arose from that very [<s>niyati</s>],
bound by the conditions of the individual (<s>puṃs</s>).
that which fills [the worlds] from <s>Pradhāna</s> (Prakṛti) onward,
depending on the <s>Rudras</s> of the cosmic worlds.
Then the principal (<s>prādhānika</s>) tattva,
from the <s>Kalā</s> tattva, produced [that which is] the cause
of the secondary [creation], arising from
the seven knots.
Then [from that arose] the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) of <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) and the rest —
the secondary [Prakṛti consisting of] <s>Sattva</s>, <s>Rajas</s>, and <s>Tamas</s>;
their functions — illumination and the rest —
are for the most part well-known.
Though the <s>guṇas</s> are three,
they constitute one tattva because of their inseparability.
The singular designation of each of them
is based on the predominance of [its] activity.
There is nothing in this world —
no insentient object whatsoever —
that is not pervaded by the <s>guṇas</s>, in which
one <s>guṇa</s> or a mixture [of <s>guṇas</s>] is not [present].
From that [arises] the <s>Buddhi</s> tattva (intellect-principle),
characterized by dispositions (<s>bhāvas</s>) and conditions (<s>pratyayas</s>),
which is the supreme object of enjoyment for the self,
fashioned for the purposes to be described.
The dispositions (<s>bhāvas</s>) are the qualities of <s>Buddhi</s>: <s>dharma</s> (virtue),
<s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), and <s>bhūti</s> (supernatural power) —
these are <s>sāttvika</s> (of <s>sattva</s> nature); their opposites,
abandoning attachment, are <s>tāmasa</s> (of <s>tamas</s> nature).
The conditions (<s>pratyayas</s>) are their material causes;
they are eight, nine, four-grouped,
seven, and five — well-known
as <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) and the rest, in classes, O sage.
The dispositions together with [their] conditions —
their characteristics are briefly stated:
they are innate (<s>sāṃsiddhika</s>), acquired through discipline (<s>vainayika</s>),
and natural (<s>prākṛta</s>) — [these pertain] to the soul.
For those whose minds are illuminated
by the cultivation of distinguished dharma,
the innate quality shines forth
even in the absence of the body, as before.
From worldly wisdom, teachers, and scriptures,
the disciplinary quality shines forth —
the disciplinary [quality] is acquired
through the exertion of mind, speech, and body.
The natural [quality] is manifest
in conjunction with the body — like awakening from dreams and the like.
Heaven and liberation [result] from the natural ones without obstruction;
entry into wombs, reaching hell, and bondage —
the purposes in [those of] the disciplinary and natural [types]
are accomplished with obstruction, in sequence.
Mastery, attainment, the yoga of complete knowledge,
enjoyments, desire, removal of the host of obstacles,
attachment to enjoyments, degradation, acquisition of a body,
and obstruction — these are the purposes in the innate ones.
Now, the general characteristic
of the classes of <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) and the rest
is briefly stated, lest there be confusion
from the condensed statement, by [giving] distinctions.
<s>Siddhi</s> (attainment) here is the understanding
whose object is <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s>, and the rest.
<s>Tuṣṭi</s> (contentment) is the thought 'I have accomplished my aim'
of one who has not [truly] accomplished his aim.
<s>Aśakti</s> (incapacity) is the inability to accomplish
what is beneficial when the instruments [of knowledge] fail.
Having some general [knowledge] elsewhere,
a different understanding — that is <s>viparyaya</s> (error).
<s>Siddhi</s> arises from the <s>sattva</s> nature
through the capacity for illumination of the manifest and the rest;
because of operating for the purpose of illumination,
it also arises from the <s>rajas</s> portion.
<s>Tuṣṭi</s> (contentment), because of having a false nature,
is grounded in the quality of <s>tamas</s>;
because of having the form of happiness, O <s>Brahman</s>,
it is also determined as <s>sāttvika</s>.
<s>Aśakti</s> (incapacity), because of non-activity,
is <s>tāmasa</s>; because of having the nature of suffering,
the <s>rājasa</s> quality is also seen [in it] —
the cause residing in the effect.
<s>Viparyaya</s> (error) has <s>tamas</s> as its source;
because of having a false form,
from the appearance of mere generality,
it is determined as [having] a <s>sattva</s> nature.
Thus this illumination of <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect),
characterized by dispositions and conditions,
is called <s>bodha</s> (cognition) — [it is] cognition
as the ground of manifestation for the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>).
If <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) is the cause of cognition,
[then] <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge-tattva) would be different from it.
If <s>Rāga</s> (attachment) [exists] when there is true dispassion,
what does [<s>Rāga</s>] whose source is <s>Kalā</s> accomplish?
If another manifester exists,
then the [first] manifester is purposeless.
When mind, senses, and objects exist,
<s>Buddhi</s> too would be purposeless.
Now some say this
with the intention of [<s>Buddhi</s> being] an instrument:
even that position, [shared with] the senses including mind as the sixth,
is held to be inconclusive.
If, when there is a single application,
one [instrument] is truly redundant —
[then] ear, eye, hand, foot, and the rest
should have different purposes for us.
And there is no single application whatsoever
of <s>Vidyā</s> and <s>Buddhi</s>;
through the door of different applications,
the fault of multiplicity of means [for one end] does not [arise].
<s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge) is the power of the manifest soul —
impelled, it takes the domains of the senses
as its own, and becomes the object
of the instrument conjoined with <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Through that, the other [faculty] — understanding — [arises]; <s>Rāga</s> (attachment)
is not secondary, because of being different in nature from that.
And this is the state of being an object of enjoyment; or rather,
the dispassionate one is liberated from that.
<s>Rāga</s> is the desire toward objects —
it does not exist for the two [types of] objects [when free].
<s>Karma</s> (action) should be conceived as pervading;
even when conceived, in another [context] what [of it]?
The fault of <s>karma</s> alone has been stated
only in the two fixed [forms].
The fault of co-existence and infinite regress
[does not apply] because of the dissimilarity of aversion and attachment.
All activity of everyone at all times
arises from the cognition of pleasure.
For one who has acted, pleasure, pain,
or delusion arises.
Aversion [arises] immediately after activity;
attachment [arises] prior to that [activity].
At the end of aversion, that [attachment arises] again — whereby
it is the cause of yoga, like energy (<s>vīrya</s>).
Now, from another [transformation] of the manifest, from <s>Buddhi</s>,
<s>Garva</s> (<s>Ahaṅkāra</s>, ego-principle) is considered — the false maker.
From whose activity
the five bodily winds move.
These are <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Apāna</s>, and the rest —
differentiated by function, not in substance.
As I briefly state their functions,
O <s>Bharadvāja</s>, understand me.
The function called 'conducting' (<s>praṇayana</s>) —
that is called 'enlivening' (<s>jīvana</s>).
That [function called] 'reasoning' (<s>ūha</s>) — the intelligence of beings —
wanders like a blind person seeking the path.
That which performs this is called <s>Prāṇa</s> —
or [it is called] <s>Prāṇa</s> because of connection with life-force.
The word <s>Prāṇa</s> [also applies] to the subtle body (<s>ātivāhika</s>),
to the power of consciousness (<s>citi</s>), and to the <s>Kalās</s>.
Similarly, the removal
of what is eaten, drunk, feces, urine, and semen —
that which performs this is sung
by the word <s>Apāna</s>, by those who see the truth.
The uniform distribution of food and drink
equally on all sides —
that which performs this is called <s>Samāna</s>;
<s>Vyāna</s> [is so called] from bending the body.
By the effort preceded by the desire to speak,
through the sound-quality in the space of the throat,
with the help of the organ of speech,
that by which articulation is produced —
that is <s>Udāna</s>. In this body,
whatever [results in] its maintenance is its station;
its mastery is the fruit. The remainder to be stated
has been set forth by the Lord in another section.
Now, for the accomplishment of the remaining purposes,
from this very [<s>Ahaṅkāra</s>], that [Lord]
extracted three [types] — <s>Sattva</s> and the rest —
predominantly imbued with the Lord's power.
The luminous (<s>taijasa</s>), the modified (<s>vaikṛta</s>),
and the other called <s>Bhūtādi</s> (source of elements) — thus it is remembered.
From these, the senses (<s>devas</s>) equal in number to the subtle elements (<s>mātras</s>);
from the subtle elements, the five gross elements.
Ear, skin, eyes, tongue,
and nose, together with mind —
by connection with illumination, [these are] <s>sāttvika</s>;
and the luminous (<s>taijasa</s>) [<s>ahaṅkāra</s>] is [also] <s>sāttvika</s>.
Speech, hands, the generative organ, the anus,
and feet — these arise from <s>rajas</s>;
because of connection with action, the group
predominating in <s>rajas</s> — that is the <s>vaikārika</s> (modified) here.
Sound, touch, form,
taste, and smell as the fifth —
these are the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), undifferentiated by qualities,
designated by the word '<s>tanmātra</s>.'
Because of being different from the groups of
illumination and action, they arise from <s>tamas</s>;
and because of being objects of illumination,
the <s>Bhūtādi</s> (element-source) among the <s>ahaṅkāras</s> is <s>tāmasa</s>.
That which impels the senses, is swift
in action, and has the nature of volition (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) —
[that is] <s>Manas</s> (mind). With regard to objects [like] sound and the rest,
hearing and the other [senses] are the graspers.
Speaking, grasping, joy-giving,
excretion, and locomotion — these are the actions
of speech and the other [organs]. [Their] otherness from the feet [etc.]
is [maintained] even when [residing in] the feet, because of not having those [physical] qualities.
In the absence of self, senses, and objects,
all senses do not operate.
The existence of a [separate] cause of activity
is determined even by reasoning.
Because of being different from the functions
stated for the other tattvas,
volition (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) approaches the seed [of all activity] —
[that is] <s>Manas</s>; by elimination.
Its knowledge [arises] from connection with the senses;
that [connection occurs] sequentially, because of [operating] in sequence.
Yet it appears [to operate] simultaneously —
due to nothing other than rapid movement.
The senses, being restricted to specific objects,
have different sources for each [person];
and because of manifesting smell and the rest,
they also have those [elements] as their basis.
The ear grasps sound alone;
and skin grasps touch alone.
Let it be so — if it does not grasp
another cause [i.e., element] possessing qualities.
The skin-sense grasps objects
not [directly] connected, turning away from the connected [element].
The eye grasps the substance of fire, water, and earth
that is of similar form [i.e., luminous].
Therefore, that [visual sense] would be born of three substances —
[but] it is not so held by others.
That by which an object is perceived —
that is the cause of [perceiving] that object.
Not even contact, action, and the like [are required] —
this is [the opponent's] chain of difficulties.
The space qualified by the ear-aperture
is what manifests the class of sounds.
The [space] qualified by the nasal aperture —
tell me, by what is [smell] prevented [from being grasped by the ear]?
If it is obstructed by the unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>),
what has that also accomplished elsewhere?
'What is in contact, it grasps' — not in a drum
cursed by some thief [?].
Even in what is inaccessible to reasoning, from authoritative statement,
understanding [arises] as consequential.
'Of what has limited meaning and unlimited meaning,
the latter is superior' — so say the wise.
Space, wind, fire, water,
and earth — these are the five elements.
Having one more quality [each] beginning with sound,
possessing functions beginning with giving space.
Shaking, burning, flooding,
and hardness — [these are] the qualities that make [them] known.
Sounds in space, wind, and the rest [reside] in space;
echo is [a sound] of the same class.
Arrangement, giving space,
cooking, cohesion, and supporting —
these are the functions
of wind, space, fire, water, and earth [respectively].
'Sound is a quality of space alone' —
because of its being perceived elsewhere,
some say, O Blessed One,
'[it is] a quality of all elements — how [can it be otherwise]?'
Where else but in the space of hearing [is sound perceived]?
How can it be a quality of another [element]?
Because of the basis accepted by others,
the experience of humans is the determiner there.
If you think that sometimes
perception [occurs] even at the root of the ear [without space] —
let there be a transformation of that too,
like the functioning of the ear — what harm [is there]?
Reasons contradicted by scripture and direct perception
do not establish [their] object,
because of being time-barred [i.e., overridden] —
so know the knowers of logic.
Even so, this [conclusion] stands:
let smell also be a quality of space,
since from <s>ketaka</s> flowers and the like
it is perceived even at a distance.
Thus, sound [resides] in the five [elements];
touch in the [lower] four elements;
neither cold nor hot in earth and wind;
cold in water, hot in fire.
Luminous in fire; white in water;
in earth — white and other colors in many ways.
Form in three [earth, fire, water]; taste in water —
sweet; sixfold in earth.
Smell in earth — unpleasant
and pleasant — so hold the wise.
In the body: bones, flesh, hair, skin,
nails, and teeth — [these are] earth.
Urine, blood, phlegm, sweat,
semen, and the rest — water is established [therein].
In the heart, in digestion, in the eyes, in bile —
fire [is present], because of observing its properties there.
In the differentiated functions of <s>Prāṇa</s> and the rest,
wind has already been stated to you.
By connection with the function of <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego),
space [is present] in all the channels (<s>nāḍīs</s>).
From the impeller (<s>Prayoktrī</s>, i.e., <s>Māyā</s>) down to earth —
this is the means of accomplishment for the soul (<s>aṇu</s>).
It is determined as restricted to each individual self,
because of the difference in enjoyments.
Because of the non-arising of simultaneous activity everywhere,
it is not all-pervading.
Even [things] of different classes [can produce] a single
fruit — like the parts of a lamp and [its] substance.
Thus this is the subtle body (<s>ātivāhika</s>) of this being —
revolving briefly in the womb of the dense forest of consciousness-contact;
'This much is not enough' — [therefore] the row of cosmic tattvas
I shall describe for the arising of the supporting body, objects, and [worlds].
Then, for the accomplishment of the purposes stated,
<s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord) fashioned
the worlds and the rest from the common sources —
<s>Kalā</s> and the other [tattvas].
Those [worlds] — <s>Kāla</s> (Time), <s>Anala</s> (Fire), and the rest —
extending to the boundary of <s>Kalā</s>, [constitute] the circle [of existence].
The knowers of truth call [this]
'<s>Saṃsāra</s>' — the abode of experience.
In the <s>Māyā</s> [level] also are recited
lords such as <s>Gahaneśa</s> and others.
And the purification of tattvas in <s>Dīkṣā</s> (initiation) —
all that [rests] upon His creation.
Eternality, pervasiveness, and the like
are determined from scripture.
The visible [world] — cities and the rest — which is the object of experience,
is embodied and subject to dissolution.
In the pure path (<s>śuddhādhvan</s>) also, the lords
of the higher <s>Māyā</s> are [placed] in the creation.
They are recited in that [<s>Māyā</s>] also;
they too [rest] upon His creation.
Dust is seen laterally
in the rays of the sun entering a lattice.
At the third stage, which is the location
of eight times eight [atoms], it would be the tip of a hair.
A nit, a louse, a grain of barley — likewise
a finger — by three times those [respectively].
Multiplied by those same [factors, one gets] a span (<s>pāṇi</s>);
a bow (<s>dhanus</s>) — that is marked by the [four] <s>Vedas</s>.
A staff (<s>daṇḍa</s>) should be known as two bows;
a <s>krośa</s> is two thousand of those.
They call two <s>krośas</s> a <s>gavyūti</s>;
and two <s>gavyūtis</s> a <s>yojana</s>.
The shell of <s>Brahmā's</s> egg, in thickness,
[measures some number of] <s>yojanas</s>.
Within it is the golden abode
of <s>Kālāgni</s> — of exactly that [extent].
Therein, with the radiance of ten million sharp rays
[like those] at the end of time,
surrounded by <s>Rudras</s> of that kind,
dwells the god known as <s>Kālāgni</s>.
Of all beings existing in all paths —
when his radiance is aroused,
fear arises through the power
of the Lord's destructive [energy] when impelled.
His flames, by their own nature,
extend ten million
<s>yojanas</s>; and by half that extent,
the smoke — dense and terrible.
Then there are thirty-three layers (<s>puṭas</s>),
[each of] ten million minus one hundred thousand [<s>yojanas</s>].
The thirty-two interstices between them
[each measure] one hundred thousand — [these are abodes] of wicked beings,
places created by the Lord of the path
for the purpose of punishment.
I shall tell you their names —
O best of twice-born, understand me.
<s>Raurava</s>, <s>Dhvānta</s> (Darkness), <s>Śītoṣṇa</s> (Cold-and-Hot),
<s>Saṃtāpa</s>, <s>Abja</s> (Lotus), <s>Mahāmbuja</s> (Great Lotus),
<s>Kālasūtra</s> as the eighth — these
are known as the hells.
[Named by their instruments:] <s>Sūcyāsya</s> (Needle-mouth), <s>Tāla</s> (Palm-tree), <s>Khaḍga</s> (Sword),
<s>Kṣuradhārā</s> (Razor-edge), and <s>Ambarīṣaka</s> (Frying-pan) —
burning coals, great burning,
and torments — these, O sage,
are the eight supremely loathsome [hells],
following the designation 'great sound' (<s>mahāśabda</s>);
lac-coating, flesh-eating,
suppression of exhalation and inhalation;
the paired mountains, the <s>śālmalī</s> tree of iron,
the blazing [hells of] hunger and thirst,
and the heap of worms —
these are declared as the rulers [of subsidiary hells].
The iron pillar, then the excrement and urine [hell],
and likewise the river <s>Vaitaraṇī</s>,
<s>Tāmisra</s> (darkness) and <s>Andhatāmisra</s> (blinding darkness),
<s>Kumbhīpāka</s> (pot-cooking) and <s>Raurava</s> (screaming),
<s>Avīci</s> (uninterrupted) which follows <s>Mahāpada</s>,
[and] <s>Rājarājeśvareśvara</s> —
of these compartments, together with the hells,
in number of <s>yojanas</s>,
there are thirty <s>koṭis</s> (crores),
and two <s>lakṣas</s> (hundred-thousands), O best of twice-born;
then, thirty thousand [yojanas]
beyond the earth of nine <s>lakṣas</s>,
the lower half is made of iron,
and the upper half is of gold;
the compartment that is below that —
half of earth and half of iron.
There, over these thirty-two
hells, the lord is stationed —
<s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> by name, renowned,
with the radiance of the fire of the sun at dissolution,
with a terrifying face, wrathful,
with round, bulging eyes,
holding a chisel in his hand, surrounded
by numerous beings of like nature.
Above the iron-and-gold compartment,
this is the eighth earth;
the higher [region] of six thousand [yojanas], the middle
of three <s>koṭis</s> minus one <s>lakṣa</s>,
the nine thousand abodes,
the higher of ten thousand —
the seven-fold [group] of these
is known by the wise as the seven <s>Pātālas</s> (netherworlds).
Hear from me their names
and their presiding lords, as I declare them:
<s>Ābhāsa</s>, that called <s>Paratāla</s>,
<s>Tritala</s>, and <s>Gabhastimān</s>,
<s>Mahātala</s>, <s>Rasāṅka</s>,
and the seventh, <s>Pātāla</s>, O sage;
in these seven [netherworlds], lords of <s>Daityas</s>,
serpents, and night-wanderers (<s>Rākṣasas</s>)
are declared seven by seven —
hear about them from me now;
the <s>Daityas</s>: <s>Śaṅkuśruti</s> in the first,
<s>Prahlāda</s>, <s>Śiśupālaka</s>,
<s>Karkandhaka</s>, <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>,
<s>Bṛhadgarbha</s>, and <s>Bali</s> likewise;
the <s>Kādraveyas</s> (serpents): <s>Kuṭilaka</s>,
<s>Vāsuki</s>, <s>Kambala</s> likewise,
<s>Kārkoṭaka</s>, then <s>Kālāṅga</s>,
<s>Durdarśa</s>, <s>Takṣaka</s> likewise;
<s>Vikaṭa</s>, <s>Lohitākṣa</s>,
<s>Yamākṣa</s>, <s>Vikaṭānana</s>,
<s>Karāla</s>, <s>Bhīmanirhrāda</s>,
and <s>Piṅgala</s> — these are the <s>Rākṣasas</s>;
above them all, the supreme
lord of the <s>Pātālas</s>,
in the golden realm of a thousand [yojanas],
<s>Hāṭaka</s> is stationed in the maṇḍala (circle);
whom, for the attainment of their desires,
the restrained ones, adorned with ascetic ornaments,
and the ladies of the lords of <s>Daityas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Asuras</s>
praise with charming verses;
then, the earth [extends] a hundred <s>koṭis</s>,
sheltering various peoples,
adorned with continents, mountains, rivers, waters,
and circles of treasures;
<s>Jambū</s>, <s>Śāka</s>, <s>Kuśa</s>, <s>Krauñca</s>,
<s>Śālmala</s>, <s>Gomeda</s>, <s>Puṣkara</s> —
these continents, each doubling from one <s>lakṣa</s>,
are surrounded by oceans beginning with the salt [ocean];
then the golden earth,
and the mountain <s>Lokāloka</s>,
darkness beyond, the cosmic waters (<s>garbhoda</s>),
and the shell (<s>kaṭāha</s>) — this is the earth-plane;
[with] mountains, rivers, and continents
adorned by fire and oceans —
this glorious earth, O <s>Śakra</s> (Indra),
I wish to hear about in detail;
with you as the speaker, O Lord of Gods,
who sees all things directly —
upon the fulfillment of instruction, my mind
runs eagerly toward hearing;
I shall narrate, O best of twice-born,
embodying the topic at hand;
listen with concentrated mind
about the continents, rivers, and forest-regions;
<s>Jambūdvīpa</s> is the navel of the earth,
its circumference is one <s>lakṣa yojanas</s>,
surrounded by the salt ocean,
which is of equal extent;
in its center stands the mountain —
the king of kings, golden,
outshining the sun's rays in brilliance —
<s>Meru</s>, frequented by the gods;
it is sixteen thousand [yojanas]
embedded in the earth; from the earth's surface,
it rises one <s>lakṣa</s> less than that [sixteen thousand],
sixteen [thousand] broad at the base;
at the three intervals of its [four] feet,
at the four increasing terraces,
rim-like ledges protrude,
most resplendent;
one [ledge] is of ten thousand [yojanas],
the other of a thousand plus [more];
the rim at the edge of the summit,
the abode of the world-guardians —
they call it <s>Cakravāṭa</s>,
radiant with all kinds of jewels;
<s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and great beings
dwell below on its terraces;
in the eastern and other [directions], headed by <s>Indra</s>,
learn their names:
adorned with circles of nets
of rays of various jewels, [the city] of <s>Hari</s> (Indra) —
frequented by <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Sādhyas</s>, and the <s>Maruts</s> —
<s>Amarāvatī</s>, with a golden ground,
with ramparts and gateways mostly of
red and yellow gems and gold —
<s>Tejovatī</s> of <s>Agni</s> (Fire), frequented by beings
resembling fire,
<s>Saṃyamanī</s> of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), lofty,
with a circle of iron ramparts,
frequented by <s>Kālapāśa</s> and ancestral spirits
and the army of ghosts,
dark, like the abode of the lord of <s>Daityas</s> and Death,
frequented by <s>Daityas</s>,
adorned with canopies of nets
of blue gem-radiance,
<s>Śuddhavatī</s> of the Lord of Waters,
constructed of crystal stones,
attended by aquatic beings
white like clouds, it shines with radiance,
<s>Gandhavatī</s> of <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind), lofty,
crowded with white and yellow banners,
attended by powerful beings,
constructed of all kinds of jewels,
<s>Mahodaya</s> of the Moon,
white, constructed of pearls and the like,
praised by hosts of twice-born,
it shines with cities bright as snowy mountains,
of Him whose blazing forehead-eye
burned <s>Smara</s> (Kāma) and Death, bearer of fame —
the city <s>Yaśovatī</s>, made
of all jewels, attended by <s>Rudra</s>,
thus, these [cities] bestow happiness in all seasons,
extending half the width of the <s>Cakravāṭa</s>,
these eight cities, reddened by the pollen
of the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree scattered by the wind,
were created by <s>Brahmā</s>
for those who attend upon the circle of world-guardians,
for their prosperity — these [cities], known as 'heaven,'
are celebrated by poets on earth;
fourteen thousand
<s>yojanas</s> [above], of the Self-born (<s>Brahmā</s>),
in the center, the city called <s>Manovatī</s>,
venerated by the lords of the worlds,
which made the reddish-hued lofty
lightning-paths [pale] by its great splendor,
as if rivaling the <s>Sāvitrī</s> (solar hymn),
surpassing [even] the desires of heaven,
in that [city], gods and sages
of great power worship
the great Lord of <s>Yogīs</s> for the attainment of perfection —
the Creator of beings, [worshipped] with <s>Yama</s> and others,
on the <s>Īśa</s> (Lord's) side of that mountain,
[there is] a peak resembling the sun,
which they call <s>Jyotiṣka</s>,
ever dear to <s>Paśupati</s> (Lord of Beings),
on its golden slopes,
variegated with jewels, are stationed
<s>Skanda</s>, <s>Nandin</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>,
<s>Gaṇeśa</s>, and other hosts of attendants;
on the summit, the abode of the God of gods,
the enemy of the three cities (<s>Tripuravidviṣ</s>),
attended by ten thousand hosts of <s>Rudras</s>
and by the best of gods beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>.
Thus, below <s>Meru</s> and at its end,
the mountains that stand in the directions,
the remaining [nine] regions (<s>varṣas</s>) in this nine-continent [land] —
learn about them from me:
<s>Niṣadha</s>, <s>Hemakūṭa</s>,
and <s>Himavān</s> — the best of mountains —
to the south of <s>Meru</s>; <s>Nīla</s>,
<s>Śveta</s>, and <s>Śṛṅgī</s> — to the left (north),
two thousand [yojanas] in breadth,
ten in height, nine in the intervals,
elongated toward the east, with excellent terraces,
with their tips extending into the ocean,
with half that breadth, [are]
<s>Mālyavad</s> and <s>Gandhamādana</s>,
[running] south and north, to the east and west
of <s>Meru</s>, equally distant,
west of <s>Mālyavat</s>, and to the east
of <s>Gandhamādana</s> mountain —
<s>Ilāvṛta</s> [lies]; south of <s>Nīla</s> mountain,
north of <s>Niṣadha</s> —
<s>Bhadrāśva</s>, to the east of <s>Mālyavat</s>,
a region filled with good people;
the well-bannered <s>Ketumāla</s>,
to the west of <s>Gandhamādana</s>,
from <s>Niṣadha</s>, <s>Harivarṣa</s>,
south of <s>Hemakūṭa</s>;
known by name as <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s>;
<s>Bhārata</s> [lies south] of the <s>Himavat</s> mountain;
that called <s>Ramyaka</s>, north of <s>Nīla</s>;
<s>Hiraṇya</s>, from <s>Śveta</s> mountain;
what is north of <s>Śṛṅgavat</s> —
that is called <s>Kuruvarṣa</s>;
four buttress-mountains
were fashioned by <s>Brahmā</s> for <s>Meru</s>'s stability,
half a <s>lakṣa</s> in height;
to the east of these is <s>Mandara</s>,
<s>Śveta</s>, having the hue of turmeric powder,
to the south, <s>Gandhamādana</s>;
to the west, <s>Vipula</s>, which is blue;
<s>Supārśva</s>, ruddy, to the north;
on them stand the wish-fulfilling trees
casting shade of a thousand <s>yojanas</s> —
<s>Kadamba</s>, <s>Jambū</s>, <s>Aśvattha</s>,
and <s>Nyagrodha</s> — up to the northern one;
the river born from the juice of the <s>Jambū</s> fruit,
flowing around <s>Meru</s>,
entered the very root of this [mountain],
turning that earth to gold;
having drunk [that juice], birds, serpents, mice,
deer, monkeys, and the like
became golden — as did those
beings who bathed in that [river];
the <s>Jambū</s> tree became the banner of the continent,
even though the wish-fulfilling trees exist;
because of its surpassing splendor,
this [continent] is known as <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>;
to the east, at the base of the buttress-mountain,
is the forest <s>Caitraratha</s>;
there is a lake called <s>Aruṇodaka</s>,
adorned with golden lotuses;
at the base of the southern mountain, surrounded by
<s>Gandharvas</s>, gods, <s>Siddhas</s>, and <s>Apsarases</s>,
[is] <s>Nandana</s> [garden]; there [is] <s>Mānasa</s>,
the lake that steals the mind;
<s>Vaibhrāja</s>, at the base of <s>Vipula</s>,
and the excellent lake <s>Sitoda</s>,
attended by gods, covered
with lotuses of sun-like radiance;
at [the base of] <s>Supārśva</s>, the forest called <s>Dhṛtimat</s>,
[and] the lake <s>Bhadraka</s>,
covered with <s>saugandhika</s> lotuses,
always frequented by the ancestral spirits;
in <s>Ilāvṛta</s>, the people live thirteen thousand years,
eating the juice of the <s>Jambū</s> fruit,
their needs fulfilled by the sight of <s>Meru</s>,
[they are] good-skinned;
in <s>Ketumāla</s>, the people live ten thousand years,
with the radiance of blue lotuses, eating the essence of jackfruit,
with divine bodily constitution,
happy and strong;
in <s>Bhadrāśva</s>, with the radiance of the moon's orb,
eating blue lotuses,
living ten thousand years,
free from suffering, sorrow, and fear;
in <s>Kuru</s>, the people live thirty thousand years,
eating the fruit of wish-fulfilling trees,
bearing twins,
with the radiance of dark-blue flowers;
two thousand and five [yojanas in extent],
marked at the juncture of one direction,
in the realms of <s>Soma</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, frequented by
<s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Munis</s>, and <s>Cāraṇas</s>,
the two continents <s>Candrabhādraka</s>,
whose people have the hue of moon-red lotuses;
their lifespan is the same as <s>Ilāvṛta</s>;
fruit and roots are their food;
though included within <s>Kuru</s> and the ocean,
they are mentioned because of proximity;
twelve thousand and fifteen hundred [years]
is the lifespan in <s>Hiraṇvatī</s>,
of the people with moon-like radiance,
who always eat the <s>lākuca</s> fruit;
in <s>Ramyaka</s>, beautiful with blue lotuses,
the people live twelve [thousand years];
thousands of years,
eating the fruit of the <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) tree;
with silver-like radiance, eating sugarcane —
in <s>Hari[varṣa]</s>, the people [live] the same lifespan;
golden-complexioned, in <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s>, eating
<s>plakṣa</s> (fig), living ten thousand years;
thus <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s> and the other
regions that have been described to you —
in them there is no division of stages
into <s>Kṛta</s> and the other [ages];
wisdom, lifespan, vigor,
strength, wealth, and progeny accord with the age;
in <s>Bhārata</s>, the people eat cultivated and uncultivated [food],
afflicted by the three kinds of suffering;
but the one virtue is that when one strives,
nothing desired remains unaccomplished;
since this land of action is the cause
of all fruit-bearing lands;
in the currents of the nine oceans, there are nine continents,
and here on the half-land,
beginning with <s>Indradvīpa</s> —
learn their names from me:
<s>Indradvīpa</s>, <s>Kaśeru</s>,
<s>Tāmraparṇa</s>, <s>Gabhastimān</s>,
<s>Nāgadvīpa</s>, <s>Cāndramasa</s>,
<s>Gāndharva</s>, <s>Vāruṇa</s> likewise,
and the ninth called <s>Kumārikā</s> —
[all] with various mountains and rivers,
teeming with various classes of people,
they are declared under the name of <s>Bhārata</s>;
<s>Āgnīdhra</s> was the name of the king,
the lord of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, in <s>Manu</s>'s lineage;
by the names of kings born of him,
<s>Bhārata</s> and the other [regions] are called;
by salt, milk, curd, ghee,
juice, honey, and ambrosia-water,
the continents, each doubling from one <s>lakṣa</s>,
are surrounded, beginning with <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>;
in <s>Śāka</s>, the <s>Śāka</s> tree is the defining feature,
the basis for the name <s>Śāka</s>;
in <s>Kuśa</s>, the golden <s>Kuśa</s> grass appeared
when the Self-born (<s>Brahmā</s>) wished to sacrifice;
in <s>Krauñca</s>, the <s>Daitya</s> called <s>Krauñca</s> was slain
at <s>Krauñca</s> mountain, in the golden cave,
by <s>Skanda</s>, having fought long
the very wondrous great illusionist;
that mountain, by the marvelous deed
of that <s>Daitya</s>,
acquired its banner-fame,
and by his name it is called <s>Krauñca</s>;
in <s>Śālmala</s>, the <s>Śālmalī</s> tree,
golden, a thousand [yojanas tall], sun-bright,
dear to the immortals — that is its banner,
the basis for its name;
in <s>Gomeda</s>, there was a king named <s>Gopati</s>,
who undertook the cow-sacrifice (<s>gosava</s>);
he was the patron of the fire-like
<s>Autathyas</s> in <s>Manu</s>'s lineage;
when they commenced the sacrifice
to <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu), he chose the <s>Bhṛgus</s> as priests;
<s>Gautama</s>, in anger, cursed him —
he went to the tenfold destruction;
in his sacrificial enclosure, those cows
were burned by the fire of the sage's anger;
the earth was covered by their fat,
and hence it became <s>Gomeda</s>;
there is a river called <s>Puṣkariṇī</s>,
adorned with golden lotuses —
by her, that <s>Puṣkara</s> continent
is made famous, frequented by gods;
just as in <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s> and the other [regions],
the people always dwell [happily],
so too in <s>Śāka</s> continent and the rest,
eating milk and the like;
with the radiance of snow, moon, ice, blue lotuses,
grain, and crystal,
living ten thousand years,
with suffering and thorns destroyed;
before the seventh ocean,
two <s>koṭis</s> and three [additional],
and fifty thousand [yojanas]
from the tip to the interior of the golden mountain
Then [there is] the golden earth,
with mountains and trees of various gems,
created by <s>Brahma</s> for the sport
of the gods — ten <s>koṭis</s> [in extent].
<s>Lokāloka</s> [is] outside of it,
the determiner of the illuminated and unilluminated [regions],
ten thousand <s>yojanas</s> in diameter,
furnished with lofty peaks.
On its peaks, the rays of the sharp-rayed [sun]
are like the light of the moon,
the radiance of the direction-supporting [mountains] does not scorch, O sage,
because of [their] remoteness.
Beyond that, dense darkness [extends]
nineteen <s>lakṣas</s> [of yojanas],
forty thousand,
thirty-five <s>koṭis</s>,
twenty-seven <s>lakṣas</s>,
and one <s>koṭi</s> [from] the ocean.
The golden shell [of the cosmic egg extends] one <s>koṭi</s>
from the interior, on all sides.
<s>Bhuvarloka</s> [is] fifteen <s>lakṣas</s> [of yojanas],
extending from the earth's surface to the Pole Star.
