children.translated_text: <s>Maharloka</s> is two <s>koṭis</s>, where dwell
the hosts of sages beginning with <s>Marīci</s>.
<s>Janaloka</s>, delimited at eight <s>koṭis</s>,
is the abode of the <s>Pitṛs</s> and <s>Jahnu</s>'s people.
<s>Tapoloka</s> is one <s>koṭi</s> of suns [in height], where dwells
the great yogin <s>Sanandana</s>,
<s>Ṛbhu</s>, <s>Sanatkumāra</s>,
and <s>Sanaka</s>, the great ascetics.
Above that, the abode of truth —
<s>Satyaloka</s> of the Self-born [<s>Brahmā</s>],
endowed with the greatest pleasures,
sixteen <s>koṭis</s> [in extent].
<s>Sāvitrī</s> dwells there in embodied form,
together with the <s>Vedas</s> and their appendages.
Then four and six [<s>koṭis</s>] respectively [are]
the abodes of the slayer of <s>Madhu</s> and of the enemy of <s>Tripura</s> —
<s>Jyotiṣmatī</s> and <s>Citrā</s> [respectively].
One <s>koṭi</s> [is] the shell of the [cosmic] egg.
Extending over a hundred <s>koṭis</s> —
such is the sphere of <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> (the Cosmic Egg).
This is largely equal
in measure in all the streams [of tradition].
<s>Śakra</s> (Indra) guards its eastern direction;
<s>Agni</s> (Fire) guards the southeast.
The destroyer of beings [<s>Yama</s>] guards the south;
the <s>Rākṣasa</s> [<s>Nirṛti</s>] guards the southwest.
The god <s>Varuṇa</s> [guards] the west;
<s>Vāyu</s> (Wind) [guards] the northwest.
<s>Soma</s> and the lord of <s>Yakṣas</s> [guard] the north;
<s>Īśa</s> (Śiva) [guards] the northeast direction.
<s>Brahmā</s> [is] above; <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu) below —
always devoted to all purposes.
As controllers of these [guardians] also,
ten groups of ten <s>Rudras</s> are stationed.
These powerful ones, from whose station
even the mighty ones do not transgress out of fear,
[are] of various forms, of great valor,
with radiance like the rising sun,
attended by bearers of various weapons.
Learn their names from me:
<s>Budhna</s>, <s>Vajra</s>, <s>Śarīrāja</s>,
<s>Kapālī</s>, <s>Śa</s>, <s>Pramardana</s>,
<s>Prāgvibhūti</s>, <s>Avyaya</s>, <s>Śāstā</s>,
<s>Pinākī</s>, <s>Tridaśādhipa</s>.
<s>Bhasma</s>, <s>Kṣaya</s>, <s>Antaka</s>, <s>Hara</s>,
<s>Jvalana</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Hutāśana</s>,
<s>Piṅgala</s>, <s>Khādaka</s>, <s>Babhru</s>,
<s>Dahana</s> — these are the [<s>Rudras</s>] of the fire-direction.
<s>Vidhātṛ</s>, <s>Dhātṛ</s>, <s>Kartṛ</s>, <s>Īśa</s>,
<s>Kāla</s>, <s>Mṛtyu</s>, <s>Viyojaka</s>,
<s>Yāmya</s>, <s>Dharmeśa</s>, <s>Saṃyoktṛ</s>,
<s>Hara</s> — these are the [<s>Rudras</s>] under <s>Yama</s>'s command.
<s>Nirṛti</s>, <s>Māraṇa</s>, <s>Krodha</s>,
<s>Hantṛ</s>, <s>Dhūmra</s>, <s>Vilohita</s>,
<s>Ūrdhvaliṅga</s>, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>,
<s>Daṃṣṭrin</s>, <s>Bhīma</s> — these are the [<s>Rudras</s>] of the <s>Rākṣasa</s>-direction.
<s>Bala</s>, <s>Atibala</s>, <s>Pāśāṅga</s>,
<s>Śveta</s>, <s>Bhūta</s>, <s>Jalāntaka</s>,
<s>Mahābala</s>, <s>Mahābāhu</s>,
<s>Sunāda</s>, <s>Abdarava</s> — these are the [<s>Rudras</s>] of <s>Varuṇa</s>'s [direction].
<s>Laghu</s>, <s>Śīghra</s>, <s>Mahadvega</s>,
<s>Sūkṣma</s>, <s>Tīkṣṇa</s>, <s>Kṣayāntaka</s>,
<s>Kapardin</s>, <s>Abdeśa</s>, <s>Pañcānta</s>,
<s>Pañcacūḍa</s> — these are the [<s>Rudras</s>] of the wind-direction.
<s>Nidhīśa</s>, <s>Rūpavān</s>, <s>Dhanya</s>,
<s>Saumya</s>, <s>Śānta</s>, <s>Jaṭādhara</s>,
<s>Kāma</s>, <s>Prasāda</s>, <s>Lakṣmīśa</s>,
<s>Prakāśa</s> — these are the [<s>Rudras</s>] of the <s>Soma</s>-<s>Yakṣa</s> direction.
<s>Vidyeśa</s>, <s>Sarvavit</s>, <s>Jñāna</s>,
<s>Vedavit</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, <s>Vedaga</s>,
<s>Vidyā</s>, <s>Vidhātṛ</s>, <s>Bhūteśa</s>,
<s>Balipriya</s>, <s>Sukhādhipa</s> —
<s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Gaṇādhyakṣa</s>, <s>Vibhu</s>,
<s>Tryakṣa</s>, <s>Caṇḍa</s>, <s>Amarastuta</s>,
<s>Vicakṣaṇa</s>, <s>Nabha</s>, <s>Ulipsu</s>,
<s>Saṃvivāha</s> — these are of the zenith.
<s>Krodha</s>, <s>Anila</s>, <s>Bhugbhogin</s>,
<s>Grasana</s>, <s>Udumbareśvara</s>,
<s>Vṛṣa</s>, <s>Viṣadhara</s>, <s>Ananta</s>,
<s>Vajra</s>, <s>Daṃṣṭrin</s> — these are the [<s>Rudras</s>] of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s [direction, below].
Then [there are] the realms of enjoyment beginning with the waters,
the [various] grounds established in them,
forty [in number] for the controllers —
endowed with the glory of fruits obtained in [their] domains.
<s>Bhāra</s>, <s>Bhūti</s>, <s>Āṣāḍhi</s>, <s>Ḍiṇḍi</s>,
<s>Lākulya</s>, <s>Amara</s>, <s>Puṣkara</s>,
<s>Prabhāsa</s>, <s>Naimiṣa</s> — this
is the secret group of eight [sacred sites] in water.
<s>Śrīśāla</s>, <s>Jalpa</s>, <s>Kedāra</s>,
<s>Bhairava</s>, <s>Āmrātakeśvara</s>,
<s>Hariścandra</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s> —
those beginning with [these] in the radiance [domain], together with <s>Atipada</s>.
<s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Vimala</s>,
<s>Kurukṣetra</s>, <s>Gayā</s>, <s>Khala</s>,
together with <s>Nāpada</s> and <s>Uttara</s> — with
<s>Hāsa</s>, together with <s>Nākhala</s> — these [are] in the sky [domain].
<s>Sthāṇu</s>, <s>Svarṇākṣa</s>, <s>Gokarṇa</s>,
<s>Bhadrakarṇa</s>, <s>Mahālaya</s>,
<s>Vastrapada</s>, <s>Avimukha</s> —
[these] <s>Rudrakoṭis</s> [are] in the space [domain].
These are called the group of eight holy [sites].
In the [domain of] pride, [they relate to] the senses' range.
The group of eight <s>Sthāṇu</s> [sites], O best of twice-born,
I shall tell you by name:
<s>Mākoṭa</s>, <s>Maṇḍaleśāna</s>,
<s>Dviraṇḍa</s>, <s>Chagalāṇḍaka</s>,
<s>Sthūla</s>, <s>Sthūleśvara</s>, <s>Śaṅku</s>,
<s>Karṇa</s>, and <s>Kālañjara</s>.
The eight subtle divine cities —
in the intellect [domain] — beginning with the <s>Paiśāca</s> [city],
[then] the <s>Rākṣasa</s>, <s>Yākṣa</s>, <s>Gāndharva</s>,
<s>Māhendra</s> — endowed with great supernatural power,
<s>Saumya</s>, <s>Prājeśvara</s>, <s>Brāhma</s> —
brilliant with supreme splendor.
In the secondary [category are] the abodes of the lord of yogins:
the uncreated, the created-elephant [realm],
the <s>Brāhma</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, <s>Kaumāra</s>,
the <s>Auma</s> (pertaining to <s>Umā</s>), and the <s>Śraikaṇṭha</s> — at the end.
The radiant abode of <s>Vīrabhadra</s>,
praised by the best of yogins,
[is] below its own station, [where he is] established in [his] domain,
with glory surpassing all <s>Rudras</s>.
<s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Ananta</s>,
<s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Umāpatya</s>, <s>Jeśvara</s>,
<s>Sarveśāna</s>, <s>Īśvara</s> —
called <s>Ekavīra</s> and <s>Ekaśiva</s>,
<s>Ugra</s>, <s>Pracaṇḍadṛk</s>, and <s>Īśa</s> —
these are stationed at the summit of [all] qualities.
Having worshipped through great austerity,
[they] are considered eminent because of [their dominion over] <s>Krodha</s> and the other [powers].
Sharp in [executing] the duties of their own jurisdiction,
the <s>Rudras</s> are all-seeing in purpose and action.
Now hear of the chief overlords
who possess ten times their glory.
<s>Krodheśa</s>, <s>Caṇḍa</s>, <s>Saṃvarta</s>,
<s>Jyotis</s>, <s>Piṅgala</s>, <s>Sūraga</s>,
<s>Pañcāntaka</s>, <s>Ekavīra</s>,
and <s>Śikheda</s> — these are remembered [as the chief overlords].
[<s>Śiva</s>], possessing all faculties, all bodies,
the abode of all inner organs,
the controller established in the individual soul (<s>puruṣa</s>),
possessing the power of reckoning at [the proper] time,
<s>Bhuvaneśa</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>,
<s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Bhavodbhava</s>,
<s>Ekapiṅga</s>, <s>Ekṣaṇa</s>, <s>Īśāna</s> —
thumb-sized and radiant,
comparable to the Supreme Lord, [stationed] in the wombs
of passion, knowledge, and the parts (<s>kalā</s>);
in the great cities, the sixty-four
<s>maṇḍala</s>-lords of the <s>maṇḍalas</s>.
<s>Ananta</s>, <s>Trikāla</s>, <s>Goptā</s>,
<s>Kṣemīśa</s>, the lord of <s>Brahmā</s>,
<s>Dhruva</s>, <s>Tejas</s>, <s>Adhiṣa</s> — [these] <s>Rudras</s>,
and <s>Gahaneśa</s> and <s>Viśvarāṭ</s>,
the <s>Rudras</s> who are the superintendents of <s>Māyā</s>,
the sovereign lords of the <s>maṇḍalas</s>,
mounted upon the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
causing the evolution of the hosts of beings.
This much alone is this terrible
earth of the existence of all beings,
in which the ignorant sink
like cows [stuck] in mud, unmoving.
<s>Bhṛguṇī</s>, <s>Brahmavetālī</s>,
<s>Sthāṇumatī</s>, the supreme <s>Ambikā</s>,
<s>Rūpiṇī</s>, <s>Nandinī</s>, <s>Jvālā</s> —
the seven lords of the seven <s>arbuda</s>-[realms].
The queens of knowledge (<s>Vidyārājñī</s>) have been stated
in the [section on] knowledge, praised by the <s>Rudras</s>.
Above them, with radiant glory,
the god, the lord of knowledge, is stationed.
Entered by the consciousness of the Lord of <s>Mantras</s> and <s>Īśa</s>,
attended by the eight arrays of <s>Rudras</s> —
the <s>Ucchuṣmas</s>, <s>Śambaras</s>, <s>Caṇḍas</s>,
of great valor, hostile to [those who violate their] station,
[these] <s>Rudras</s> [are] the hosts, together with the direction-guardians.
The treatises [and] the lords [proceed] from that.
Those beginning with <s>Ananta</s>
have already been stated by name.
Their own forms, O brahmin,
[have been described] previously, in connection with your question.
In the <s>Sadāśiva</s> [level], O pure-limbed one,
[there is] the array of <s>Sakala</s> and the like.
The god <s>Sadāśiva</s> [abides] in the <s>Bindu</s>;
the lords of the <s>kalās</s> beginning with <s>Nivṛtti</s> [are there].
In the <s>Nāda</s>, the lord of sound; in the <s>Śakti</s>,
the best of all who possess power.
The womb of the universe; the lords of speech (<s>Vāgīśas</s>)
are the lords beyond [that]; <s>Śiva</s> [is the ultimate].
The path conceived as having the form of atoms
[extends] from <s>Sadāśiva</s> down to <s>Śiva</s>,
the resting place of all that is supreme.
How [can there be] lords above that?
Having transcended <s>Īśāna</s>, the <s>tattva</s> extending up to
the Peaceful (<s>Śānta</s>) is remembered as <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
The worlds too, beginning with the <s>Nāda</s>,
the <s>kalās</s> — there is no lord other than <s>Śiva</s>.
But whatever differentiation of lords [exists] herein,
that, in the treatise, is like the differentiation of powers (<s>śakti</s>) —
through the figurative usage of the differentiation of functions;
that differentiation arises from the differentiation of stations.
By those powers through which [<s>Śiva</s>]
brings about the awakening of the soul's radiance —
those are the sovereigns of the worlds
designated by the names <s>Nivṛtti</s> and the rest.
That by which he turns back beings
is his turning-back [power] —
<s>Nivṛtti</s> (Cessation) — and that station [is so named];
there, the lord too is called 'possessing <s>Nivṛtti</s>.'
That by which the further course of one who has ceased [worldly existence]
is characterized as directed eastward [i.e., upward] —
being arrested — that is <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s> (Foundation);
that station [is so named] and its lord [likewise].
That by which, having abandoned the domain of the attainable,
[<s>Śiva</s>] gives knowledge to the soul —
that is <s>Vidyā</s> (Knowledge); its station also [is so named],
and <s>Vidyeśa</s> (Lord of Knowledge) is its lord.
That by which <s>Hara</s> brings about
the pacification of all suffering for the soul —
that is <s>Śānti</s> (Peace), and that is its station;
he who effects that is also called 'possessing <s>Śānti</s>.'
The illumination of the domains above and below
is made great, greater,
and greatest
for the soul (<s>cit</s>) that is being liberated, by those [powers].
Those, [called] <s>Indhikā</s> and the rest, and that station [is theirs];
that lord [presides] over all three [of those powers].
Even in the state of omniscience and the like,
[there remains] subjection due to a portion of impurity (<s>mala</s>).
That by which [<s>Śiva</s>] wipes that away — that is his
liberating [power]; and that station [is named accordingly].
The liberator and the performer of that act;
that by which [<s>Śiva</s>] makes one an <s>Īśāna</s> (Lord) —
that is the upward-going [power]; that is its station;
and that lord is the master of the upward-going.
Those who have attained that station
through the practice of <s>Śaiva</s> disciplines,
having enjoyed bliss until the end of that [cosmic] duration,
proceed to the supreme station.
They do not perform creation and the like,
because they are established in their own purpose.
Thus the <s>Sadāśiva</s> <s>tattva</s>
has been explained to you in brief.
In [the] <s>Śakti</s> [tattva] also it is likewise — this [lord]
is <s>Sakala</s> (with parts) through connection with function;
his function pertains to that [<s>Sadāśiva</s>] domain and above;
[he is] <s>Niṣkala</s> (without parts) elsewhere, at all times.
In earth, <s>Pradhāna</s>, the knots (<s>granthi</s>),
knowledge, <s>Bindu</s>, <s>Kalā</s>, and the like —
the multipliers, beginning with ten,
exist below the tip of the <s>Nāda</s>, O sage.
Above the <s>Kalā</s> and below <s>Vidyā</s>
are heard [of] the lords of the dense [realms].
This much is the intermediate [region] —
such is the definition, as known from [each] domain.
Of both paths thus,
which are characterized by sequential emanation,
the dissolution [proceeds] in reverse order,
up to the two <s>tattvas</s> of <s>Śakti</s> [and <s>Śiva</s>].
Of the differentiated and of the aggregate —
how and to what extent is that dissolution
of the path of <s>tattvas</s>, O Lord?
Tell us, you who reveal all meanings.
In the great sleep, the dissolution of the aggregate [occurs];
the dissolution of the differentiated is intermediate.
Creation is likewise; the [duration of] stability —
listen as it is now stated.
A day of the one born from the Golden Egg [<s>Brahmā</s>]
ends after a thousand sets of four <s>yugas</s>;
the night is of equal [duration]; in the measure of day-and-night,
[his life lasts] a <s>parārdha</s> of years.
This dissolution [proceeds] in reverse order;
[the elements] beginning with <s>Prakṛti</s> are [then] restrained.
At that time, O hero, a hundred <s>Rudras</s>
and both <s>Śrīkaṇṭhas</s> are the lords of <s>Pradhāna</s>.
Having absorbed the subtle universe
and the subtle bodies of the conscious [souls] through [his] power,
those whose dispositions are established in <s>Prakṛti</s>
rest for the duration of that sleep.
Impelled by the <s>Maṇḍala</s>-lords
who bear the <s>mantras</s> beloved of <s>Śiva</s>,
at the [proper] time, having produced the universe,
they carry out their own jurisdiction.
<s>Karma</s>, <s>dharma</s>, and the like — that [<s>karma</s>]
exists in the intellect as a quality.
A quality does not depart from the qualified —
how then is it said [to exist] in <s>Prakṛti</s>?
True — <s>karma</s> is a quality of the intellect;
a quality does not depart from the qualified.
Because of its presence in body, senses, fruits, and levels [of existence],
it is figuratively attributed to those [other locations].
In the substratum, in the cause, in the effect,
in what is proximate, and in what is helpful —
in accordance with [the pattern of] <s>dharma</s> and the like —
this is [the] definition, the wise have declared.
Thus, at the [time of] <s>parārdha</s>
of the creations of qualities and the like, the cause of the qualities,
the <s>Kalā</s> absorbs the <s>Kalā</s>; <s>Māyā</s>
[is] turned away from [her] jurisdiction.
When that ceases, the gods
who are its administrators also cease.
Because the jurisdiction of creation, maintenance, and the like
depends on that [<s>Māyā</s>].
Thus, when the <s>Mantreśas</s> and the chief [lords]
enter their desired station,
the <s>Vidyā</s> [level] absorbs the <s>Sadā</s> tattva;
that [is absorbed by] <s>Bindu</s>; the <s>Baindava</s> by <s>Dhvani</s> (Sound);
the <s>Nāda</s> is absorbed by the supreme <s>Śakti</s>;
<s>Śakti</s> is governed by <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) himself.
Thus, for the repose of beings
and of <s>Māyā</s>, the supreme <s>Śiva</s>,
having surveyed [all] through the power of his own vision,
[brings about] the sleep, [and then] sets forth creation [again].
Thus the <s>tattvas</s>, the entities,
the worlds, and the bodies —
of the pure and impure paths, O brahmin,
have been explained in summary.
Knowledge, the five atomic bodies,
<s>Bindu</s>, <s>Nāda</s>, and the cause —
the five aggregates [constitute] the supreme path.
Where are the entities [and] the conditions established?
The <s>Nāda</s> is subtle — in <s>Kalā</s>, <s>Kāla</s>,
and the pair of <s>Rāgas</s>, together with <s>Puruṣa</s>;
the gross <s>Nāda</s> is of five <s>kalās</s>,
resting on five <s>tattvas</s>, O sage.
The knot of four [tattvas] beginning with <s>Pradhāna</s> —
the repository, [which is] <s>Bindu</s>, is of four <s>kalās</s>.
In pride [<s>ahaṃkāra</s>], the mind-presiding deities;
in the intellect, the entities beginning with <s>Bhāva</s> are established.
The god of five-<s>mantra</s> body
is established in the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements);
the <s>Mantreśas</s> [are] in the subtle elements;
the <s>Mantras</s> are established in the gross [elements].
Thus, that net of bonds — invisible, seeded by darkness and the like,
obstructing the soul, [experienced] by those whose vision is bound by the <s>paśu</s>-doctrine — [that net] in great abundance;
for the purpose of its pacification, through the ritual actions to be described,
the <s>Śāmbhavī</s> [power], whose potency is unobstructed, [shines forth —] the wealth of <s>mantras</s>.
Injunctions regarding Observances
That pure essence of the souls — of the nature of vision and action — which has been stolen,
whose real existence [causes] the fall of the born creatures into the ocean of worldly existence —
That grace of the Lord which destroys the irresistible darkness —
bowing to him, we undertake the exposition of the <s>caryāpāda</s> (section on conduct).

children.translated_text: Here indeed, at the commencement of the treatise: 'Of this triad of categories, having attained [knowledge of] their established nature through the [previous] sections, the application through the sections on conduct (<s>caryā</s>), yoga, and ritual (<s>kriyā</s>) will be taught.'

children.translated_text: That which was previously stated in summary — therein, even for teachers and others who have understood knowledge, action, and yoga, without conduct (<s>caryā</s>) — which consists in observing what is prescribed and avoiding what is forbidden — the desired fruit is not obtained without obstruction. Thus, having arrived in due order at the completion of the <s>yogapāda</s>, to introduce the <s>caryāpāda</s> whose connection has been indicated, he says:

children.text: This indicates that the \CP\ is the last of the text

children.translated_text: Now, therefore, of teachers (<s>deśika</s>) and the rest,
a compendium of general conduct,
having arrived at its proper occasion,
is taught in brief.

<s>Vṛtti</s>: '[Of teachers and the rest]' — of <s>ācāryas</s>, <s>sādhakas</s>, <s>putrakas</s>, and <s>samayins</s>. '[A compendium of general conduct]' — a collection of common and special observances. '[Having arrived at its proper occasion]' — having come in due order. '[In brief]' — in summary — it is now taught, that is, expounded.

children.text: ācāryasādhakaputrakasamayināṃ [sāmānyācārasaṃgrahaḥ] sādhāraṇāsādhāraṇācārasamuccayaḥ [avasaraprāptaḥ] kramāyātaḥ [samāsena] saṃkṣepād idānīm upadiśyate 'bhidhīyata iti|

children.translated_text: The word '<s>atha</s>' indicates a new topic. The word '<s>ataḥ</s>' indicates [that this follows] immediately after the <s>yogapāda</s>.
The divisions of <s>Śaivas</s>
The teacher (<s>deśika</s>), the <s>mantra</s>-practitioner (<s>mantravṛtti</s>),
the <s>putraka</s>, and the <s>samayī</s> —
these four are the <s>Śaivas</s>,
whether observing vows or not observing vows.
<s>Vṛtti</s>:

children.text:
deśika ityācāryaḥ| [mantravṛttiḥ] mantra evānanyaniṣṭhā vṛttiḥ yasya sa sādhakaḥ|
śaivānāmeva deśikādīnāmiha lakṣaṇam|
śāktādayastu te anyādṛśā eveti vijñāpayituṃ śaivapadopādānam|
dvividhāstu te śaivāḥ| vratino [avratino 'pi] vratavarjitāśca|
children.translated_text: '<s>Deśika</s>' means <s>ācārya</s> (teacher). '[<s>Mantravṛtti</s>]' — one whose livelihood (<s>vṛtti</s>) is solely in <s>mantras</s>, devoted to nothing else — that is the <s>sādhaka</s>. Here, the characterization pertains to <s>Śaivas</s> alone — teachers and the like. The word '<s>Śaiva</s>' is used to indicate that the <s>Śāktas</s> and others are of a different kind. And those <s>Śaivas</s> are of two kinds: those observing vows (<s>vratin</s>) and those without vows (<s>avratin</s>).
<s>Śaivas</s> who observe vows
Now, regarding those who observe vows, he says:
The vow-observers are [either] matted-haired (<s>jaṭila</s>) or shaven (<s>muṇḍa</s>);
among them, the foremost are ash-whitened;
adorned with <s>tilakas</s>, <s>puṇḍrakas</s>, or bands (<s>paṭṭa</s>),
from [the lowest] level upward.
<s>Vṛtti</s>:
'[Vow-observers are matted-haired or shaven]

children.text:
vratināmapi dvau bhedau jaṭitvaṃ muṇḍitā ca|jaṭilo 'pi vakṣyamāṇabhautikanaiṣṭhikabhedād dvividhaḥ|
[teṣu] sarveṣu caiteṣu madhyād [agryāḥ] brāhmaṇāḥ [bhasmapāṇḍarāḥ] bhasmoddhūlitasarvāṅgāḥ|
[bhūmipādayaḥ tilakaiḥ puṇḍrakaiḥ paṭṭaiḥ bhūṣitāḥ] kṣatriyāstilakālaṃkṛtatanavaḥ| vaiśyāstripuṇḍrakamaṇḍitāḥ| śūdrāstu paṭṭākṛtinā bhasmoddhūlanena bhūṣitāḥ syuriti śeṣaḥ||
children.translated_text: ' — of vow-observers too there are two divisions: having matted hair and being shaven. The matted-haired one too is of two kinds, by the distinction of 'elemental' (<s>bhautika</s>) and 'final' (<s>naiṣṭhika</s>) [vows]. '[Among them]' — among all of these, from the middle, '[the foremost]' are <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, '[ash-whitened]' — with all limbs dusted with ash. '[From (the lowest) level upward, adorned with <s>tilakas</s>, <s>puṇḍrakas</s>, or bands]': <s>Kṣatriyas</s> have bodies adorned with <s>tilakas</s>; <s>Vaiśyas</s> are decorated with three-line marks (<s>tripuṇḍraka</s>); and <s>Śūdras</s> are adorned with ash-dusting in the form of a band (<s>paṭṭa</s>) — this is the remainder.
Those unfit for wearing matted hair
A <s>Śūdra</s> should not wear matted hair,
nor an ignorant person, nor one who is negligent,
nor a woman, nor one advanced in age,
nor one who is sick or physically impaired.
<s>Vṛtti</s>:

children.text:
śūdramūrkhapramattastrīvṛddhāmayāvivikalāṅgairvā jaṭā na dhāraṇīyāḥ|
bahuvacananiṣedhād ekajaṭā ete syuriti kecit||
[jaṭābandhanavidhiḥ]
atha tadvidhānam---
children.translated_text: Matted hair should not be worn by <s>Śūdras</s>, the ignorant, the negligent, women, the aged, the sick, or the physically impaired. Because of the prohibition using the plural, some [say] these may wear a single matted lock.
[The procedure for tying matted hair] Now, the procedure for that:
Dividing the hair by the number of <s>kalā</s>-<s>tattvas</s>,
<s>pavitras</s> (purifiers), <s>aṇu-śaktis</s>, <s>mantras</s>, or <s>īśas</s> (lords),
and having performed the <s>sampāta</s> [offering] for each portion,
with the collected <s>aṇu</s>-[mantras],
one should tie [the matted locks] before the lord of the vow,
with the fire of <s>Śiva</s>;
for the <s>mantrin</s> (sādhaka), with the <s>mantra</s> to be accomplished;
for the <s>putraka</s> and the qualified, with the heart [<s>mantra</s>].
<s>Vṛtti</s>: '[By the number of <s>kalā</s>-<s>tattvas</s>, <s>pavitras</s>, <s>aṇu-śaktis</s>, <s>mantras</s>, or <s>īśas</s>]

children.text:
kalāḥ `tārā sutārā taraṇiḥ' ityādyā aṣṭatriṃśat|
tattvāni ṣaṭtriṃśat|
pavitrāṇavaḥ sadyojātādimantrāḥ pañca|
śaktayo vāmādyā nava|
mantreśā anantādividyeśā aṣṭau|
ābhyaḥ saṃkhyābhyo madhyādanyatamayā saṃkhyayā keśān vibhajya [pratyaṃśaṃ] ekaikasminnaṃśe [saṃhitāṇubhiḥ] śivaikādaśikayā saṃhitayā [sampātya] sampātahomaṃ kṛtvābhyarcitasya vrateśvarasya śivasya purataḥ [śivatejasā] tanmūlenācāryasya jaṭāṃ badhnīyāt|
[mantriṇaḥ] sādhakasya sādhyamantreṇa [putrayogyayoḥ] putrakasamasthayostu hṛdeti bhedaḥ||
children.translated_text: ': The <s>kalās</s> — '<s>Tārā</s>, <s>Sutārā</s>, <s>Taraṇi</s>' and so forth — are thirty-eight. The <s>tattvas</s> are thirty-six. The <s>pavitras</s> (purifying <s>mantras</s>) — '<s>Sadyojāta</s>' and the rest — are five. The <s>śaktis</s> — <s>Vāmā</s> and the rest — are nine. The <s>mantreśas</s> (lords of <s>mantras</s>) — <s>Ananta</s> and the other <s>vidyeśas</s> — are eight. Having divided the hair by any one of these numbers, '[for each portion]' — in each portion, '[with the collected aṇu-mantras]' — with the <s>Śiva-ekādaśikā</s> collection (<s>saṃhitā</s>), '[having performed the sampāta]' — having performed the <s>sampāta-homa</s> (offering), before the worshipped lord of the vow, <s>Śiva</s>, '[with the fire of Śiva]' — with that as the basis, the <s>ācārya</s> should tie the matted locks. '[For the mantrin]' — for the <s>sādhaka</s>, with the <s>mantra</s> to be accomplished. '[For the putraka and the qualified]' — for the <s>putraka</s> and those of equal standing, with the heart [<s>mantra</s>] — this is the distinction.
He states the particular method of growth of the matted hair:
With ash mixed with vermin-destroying substances,
and with <s>triphala</s> [ash],
or with powder [mixed] at evening,
the elemental vow-observer (<s>bhautikavratin</s>) should nourish them.

children.text:
Vṛtti:
[kṛmighnadravyamiśreṇa] kaṭutailaviḍaṅgapāradādidravyasaṃyuktena [traiphalena bhasmanā] harītakyāmalakavibhītakabhasmanā [sāyacūrṇena] niśācūrṇamiśreṇa vā bhautikavratī tāḥ puṣṭiṃ [nayet] prāpayet||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: '[With vermin-destroying substance-mixed]' — combined with substances such as pungent oil, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, mercury, and the like. '[With <s>triphala</s> ash]' — with ash of <s>harītakī</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, and <s>vibhītaka</s>. '[With evening powder]' — or mixed with turmeric powder — the elemental vow-observer should '[nourish]' — bring — them to growth.
Elemental and final vow-observers
He states the characteristics of the two types of vow — elemental (<s>bhautika</s>) and final (<s>naiṣṭhika</s>):
Those whose vow has a fixed term
are the elemental vow-observers;
those whose [vow] lasts until the fall of the body —
they are known as final vow-observers (<s>niṣṭhāvratin</s>).
<s>Vṛtti</s>:

children.text:
iyatā kālenaitadvrataṃ saṃnyastavyamiti sāvadhikaṃ yeṣāṃ vrataṃ te bhautikavratinaḥ|
yeṣāṃ [dehapātāntakaṃ] śarīrapātāntaṃ nirvāhaḥ te [niṣṭhāvratinaḥ] naiṣṭhikāḥ||
children.translated_text: Those whose vow is with a fixed term — 'for this much time this vow is to be laid down' — they are elemental vow-observers. Those whose observance '[lasts until the fall of the body]' — until the fall of the physical body — they are '[final vow-observers]' — <s>naiṣṭhikas</s>.
Now, who are those final vow-observers? He says:
Teachers (<s>guru</s>) and <s>putrakas</s>,
but not primary <s>sādhakas</s>.
<s>Vṛtti</s>:
'[Teachers]

children.text: ācāryāḥ putrakāḥ tathā [na prāthamikasādhakāḥ] dehapātāvadhimantrasādhakāśceti niṣṭhāvratino jñeyāḥ|
children.translated_text: ' — <s>ācāryas</s>, and <s>putrakas</s> likewise. '[Not primary sādhakas]' — but <s>mantra</s>-practitioners whose [vow-]term is until the fall of the body — these should be known as final vow-observers.
The <s>sāntānika</s> (householder who has completed his vow)
He speaks of the release from the elemental vow:
One whose vow-term is completed, who has properly
offered his vow to the lord of the vow,
who has laid aside the accoutrements of the vow, who has a virtuous wife
and possesses household prosperity —
the elemental [vow-observer] is called '<s>kāmya</s>' (desire-based),
or indeed a true '<s>sāntānika</s>' (householder).
<s>Vṛtti</s>:

children.text:
samyag iti aviplutavratasya sataḥ [pūrṇavratāvadhiḥ] pūrṇo vratāvadhiryasya saḥ|
tathā nirvyūḍhayathāmnātavrata ityarthaḥ|
tatastu [vrateśāya] vrateśvarāya [arpitavrataḥ] vratasamarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā [nyastavratāṅgaḥ] vratāṅgāni ajinakamaṇḍalvādīni saṃnyasya| yathoktaṃ śrīmatkiraṇe---
children.translated_text: 'Properly' — for one whose vow is unbroken. '[Whose vow-term is completed]' — one whose vow-term has been fulfilled. That is, one who has completed the vow as prescribed. Then, '[having offered his vow to the lord of the vow]' — having performed the offering of the vow to the lord of the vow (<s>vrateśvara</s>), '[having laid aside the accoutrements of the vow]' — having laid aside the vow-accessories such as the deer-skin, water-vessel, and the like. As stated in the glorious <s>Kiraṇāgama</s>:

children.text:
tarpayitvā praṇamyeśaṃ vratameṣāṃ samarpayet|
jaṭāstadbhasmadaṇḍaṃ ca kaupīnaṃ saṃyamaṃ kramāt||
samarpya brahmaṇe dhyātvā puṣpavāryakṣataistridhā|
vrataṃ samarpya mantrāṇāṃ hṛnmantreṇa visarjanam||
jaṭāvataraṇaṃ tasya kāryam iti
children.translated_text: 'Having satisfied and bowed to the Lord, one should offer the vow of these: the matted hair, the ash, the staff, the loincloth, and the restraint, in order. Having offered [them] to <s>Brahman</s>, having meditated, with flowers, water, and unbroken rice grains, three times. Having offered the vow, dismissal of the <s>mantras</s> with the heart-<s>mantra</s>. The lowering of the matted hair should be performed for him' — thus.

children.text:
evaṃ kṛte sati [sapatnīparigrahavibhūtimān] śobhanadāraparigrahabhūtiyuktaḥ san bhautikaḥ kāmya ityuktaḥ satsāntānika iti vā|
yadvā vibhūtiyogino 'syaiva kāmya ityākhyā| tadvirahiṇastu sadā śobhanena sāntānikākhyena bhaikṣeṇa vartanātsāntānikatvam|
yaduktaṃ śrīmatpauṣkare---
children.translated_text: When this is done, '[possessing a virtuous wife, household, and prosperity]' — endowed with an excellent wife, household, and wealth — he is called 'elemental, desire-based' or '<s>sāntānika</s>.' Alternatively, the name '<s>kāmya</s>' belongs to one who is a practitioner of <s>vibhūti</s> (sacred ash) [rites]. But for one without that, because of subsisting always on excellent alms called '<s>sāntānika</s>' — [he has] the status of <s>sāntānika</s>. As stated in the glorious <s>Pauṣkara</s>:

children.text:
uttamaṃ dvijabhaikṣaṃ tu grāhyametattvayā sadā|
taddhi sāntānikaṃ nāma bhaikṣaṃ hi parikalpitam|| iti|
children.translated_text: 'The supreme alms of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should always be accepted by you; for that is called <s>sāntānika</s> alms, so it is designated.'
<s>Śaivas</s> without vows
A <s>sādhaka</s> who follows worldly customs,
a <s>putraka</s>, a graduate (<s>snātaka</s>) who is a householder,
a <s>samayī</s>, and a former householder —
these are <s>Śaivas</s> without vows.

children.text:
Vṛtti:
sādhakasya śivadharmilaukikadharmibhedād dvaividhye sati lokadharmī yaḥ sādhakaḥ, putrakaḥ, tathā [snātako gṛhī] gṛhasthatve sati snātaḥ, samayī, [prāggṛhasthaḥ] pūrvaṃ gṛhasthaścetyete vratavarjitā jñeyāḥ|
prāggṛhasthasśca ityuttarakālaṃ gārhasthyatyāgāpekṣayā|
yataḥ sambhavanti kecana ājīvanamujjhitagṛhāvasthitayaḥ| tadvailakṣaṇyārthaṃ prāggṛhasthagrahaṇam||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: Since the <s>sādhaka</s> is of two kinds — a follower of <s>Śiva</s>-<s>dharma</s> and a follower of worldly <s>dharma</s> — the <s>sādhaka</s> who follows worldly customs, the <s>putraka</s>, likewise '[a graduate who is a householder]' — one who is a <s>snātaka</s> while being a householder, a <s>samayī</s>, '[a former householder]' — and one who was previously a householder — these should be known as without vows. 'And a former householder' — with reference to a later time, in view of the abandonment of the householder state. Because there arise some who, having abandoned the householder state, subsist [as renunciants] for a livelihood. To distinguish [from them], the term 'former householder' is used.
Common conduct of <s>Śaivas</s>
Their common duty
is twilight worship (<s>sandhyopāsana</s>) and ritual worship (<s>arcana</s>);
bathing and the like are its auxiliaries;
on <s>parvan</s> days, the observance is doubled.
<s>Vṛtti</s>:

children.text:
teṣāṃ vratināmidamavratibhiḥ sādhāraṇaṃ karma ityagrasthiteṣu ślokeṣvapi sambandhanīyam| kiṃ tadityāha---[sandhyopāsanamarcanam] sandhyopāsanārcanādi|
[tadaṅgāni] tasya karmaṇo yānyaṅgāni snānādīni tānyapi sādhāraṇānyeva| parvasu cāṣṭamīcaturdaśyayanaviṣuvādiṣu [dviguṇakriyā] pūjājapādikriyādvaiguṇyam||
children.translated_text: 'Their' — of those with vows — 'this [duty is] common with those without vows' — this should be connected with the verses that follow as well. What is that? He says: '[Twilight worship and ritual worship]' — <s>sandhyā</s>-worship, <s>arcana</s>, and the like. '[Its auxiliaries]' — the auxiliaries of that duty, such as bathing and the like, are also common. And on <s>parvan</s> days — the eighth, fourteenth, solstice, equinox, and the like — '[doubling of observance]' — doubling of worship, <s>japa</s>, and other practices.
Leaves to be avoided at meals; and the taking of alms
On leaves of the banyan (<s>nyagrodha</s>) and the sacred fig (<s>aśvattha</s>),
and on leaves of the castor plant (<s>vātaghna</s>) and the <s>akṣa</s> (vibhītaka),
and on bronze [vessels] — no eating; alms
[may be taken] from the four <s>varṇas</s>, [if] unblemished.
<s>Vṛtti</s>:
'[On leaves of the banyan and sacred fig]

children.text:
nyagrodhasya vaṭasya, aśvatthasya cordhvodgatamūlastadviśeṣasya patreṣu, [vātaghnākṣadaleṣu] vātaghnasya cairaṇḍādeḥ akṣasya vibhītakasya sambandhiṣu patreṣu, kāṃsye pātre abhojanaṃ,
[cāturvarṇyam akutsitaṃ bhaikṣaṃ] brāhmaṇādivarṇacatuṣṭayādaninditādbhaikṣagrahaṇaṃ ca sarvasādhāraṇam||
children.translated_text: ' — on the leaves of the <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan tree) and of the <s>aśvattha</s> (the special variety with roots going upward), '[on leaves of the castor plant and the akṣa]' — on leaves related to the <s>vātaghna</s> (castor plant and the like) and the <s>akṣa</s> (<s>vibhītaka</s> tree), and on bronze vessels — no eating. '[From the four varṇas, unblemished alms]' — the taking of alms from the four <s>varṇas</s> beginning with <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, from those who are blameless — this is common to all.
Avoidance of food (at certain ceremonies)
At all consecrations of deities,
at the construction of bridges and the like,
at <s>saṃskāras</s> (life-cycle rituals) such as the <s>sīmantonnayana</s>
(hair-parting ceremony) and the like — avoidance of food.
<s>Vṛtti</s>:
'[At all deity-consecrations]

children.text: sarvadevapratiṣṭhāsu [setvādīnāṃ niveśane] setuprapāvihārādipratipādane [sīmantonnayanādyeṣu saṃskāreṣu] sīmantonnayanādiṣu saṃskāreṣu ca annavarjanam annādivarjanaṃ sarveṣāṃ sādhāraṇam||
children.translated_text: ' — at all installations of deities. '[At the construction of bridges and the like]' — at the establishment of bridges, water-stations, monasteries, and the like. '[At saṃskāras such as the sīmantonnayana and the like]' — at life-cycle rituals such as the <s>sīmantonnayana</s> and the like — avoidance of food, that is, abstention from food and the like, is common to all.
Dietary rules on parvan days
With <s>caru</s> (sacrificial porridge), or with fruits and roots,
or with other <s>haviṣya</s> (sacrificial food) —
on the fourteenth, the eighth,
and the fifteenth [of the lunar month] — [this is] one's sustenance.
<s>Vṛtti</s>:
'[On the fourteenth, eighth, and fifteenth]

children.text:
caturdaśyaṣṭamīpañcadaśīṣu [caruṇā phalamūlairvā]
carvādibhiḥ vartanaṃ prāṇayātrā|
haviṣyeṇāpareṇa vā ityanena ājyapayoyavādinā havirarheṇa vastunā phalamūlādivyatiriktena vartanaṃ sādhāraṇamiti prāguktena sambandhaḥ||
children.translated_text: ' — on the fourteenth, eighth, and fifteenth days, '[with caru, or fruits and roots]' — sustenance, that is, maintenance of life, with <s>caru</s> and the like. 'Or with other <s>haviṣya</s>' — by this, sustenance with substances worthy of oblation, such as clarified butter, milk, barley, and the like, other than fruits and roots — this is common [to all], in connection with what was stated earlier.
Special observances at auspicious times
On the <s>vyatīpāta</s>, the day of [solar/lunar] destruction,
the month-increase, the solstice, and the like,
special restraint should be observed,
and the gratification (<s>pratarpaṇa</s>) of <s>Śaivas</s>.
<s>Vṛtti</s>:

children.text:
vyatīpātaḥ puṇyakālaviśeṣo jyotiḥśāstrāmnāto bṛhadvaidhṛtyādyupalakṣitaḥ|
ayane dakṣiṇottare| ādigrahaṇādviṣuvadarkendugrahaṇakālāḥ|
eṣu kāleṣu viśeṣasaṃyamaḥ [śaivānāṃ ca pratarpaṇaṃ] śaivajanatarpaṇaṃ ca sarveṣāmeva sādhāraṇam||
children.translated_text: The <s>vyatīpāta</s> is a special auspicious time taught in the science of astronomy (<s>jyotiḥśāstra</s>), indicated by <s>Bṛhadvaidhṛti</s> and the like. The solstices are the southern and northern [solstices]. By the word 'and the like,' the equinox, and the times of solar and lunar eclipses [are included]. At these times, special restraint, '[and the gratification of Śaivas]' — and the nourishing of <s>Śaiva</s> devotees — is common to all.
Protection of Śaivas in distress
When [a Śaiva] is lost on the road, seized by enemies,
afflicted by disease, or oppressed by hunger,
a complete rescue
should be undertaken for the <s>Śiva</s>-practitioner.
<s>Vṛtti</s>:
'[Of the Śiva-practitioner]

children.text:
śivaśāsane yuktasya sarvasyaiva mārgakṣīṇādiviṣaye samuddhāraḥ sarvātmanā [kartavyaḥ] karaṇīyaḥ|
[mārgakṣīṇe] mārgasya adhvanaḥ kṣīṇe paricyutau, naṣṭo mārge adhvani yaḥ kṣīṇapātheyaḥ kṣīṇadeho vā tasmin|
ripugraste śatrubhirvaśīkṛte| rogārte vyādhyutkrānte|
[kṣutprapīḍite] kṣudhā ca prakarṣeṇa pīḍite| [sarvātmanā samuddhāraḥ] sarvaprakāramuddhāraṇaṃ tasmāttasyā āpado mocanamavaśyaṃ kāryam||
children.translated_text: ' — for anyone engaged in the teaching of <s>Śiva</s>, in matters concerning one lost on the road and the like, rescue should be undertaken '[with all one's means]' — completely. '[Lost on the road]' — when the road, the path, is lost — one who has lost his way, or one whose provisions or body are exhausted on the road. '[Seized by enemies]' — subjugated by foes. '[Afflicted by disease]' — overcome by illness. '[Oppressed by hunger]' — and one who is exceedingly tormented by hunger. '[With all one's means, a complete rescue]' — rescue by all means, that is, deliverance from that distress, must certainly be performed.
What is to be avoided by vow-observers
He states the general rules of conduct for the vow-observer, both elemental and final:
Abstention from meat, women, and honey
[is enjoined for] the vow-observer; sleeping on the ground,
guarding the senses,
the water-vessel (<s>kamaṇḍalu</s>) as companion,
disregard of women's singing, dancing, conversation,
and coquetry,
not being alone in private with a woman,
avoidance of garlands, ointments, and the like.
<s>Vṛtti</s>:

children.text:
vratina idamavaśyamanuṣṭheyam| māṃsayoṣinmadhutyāgaḥ māṃsasya yoṣito madhunaśca varjanam|
māṃsatyāgastvatra śūdrasyaiva| anyeṣāmavratitve 'pi tanniṣedhāsiddheḥ|
kṣitiśāyitā iti sthalaśāyitvam|
[mātrārakṣaṇam] ajinākṣasūtradaṇḍakamaṇḍalvādimātrāyāḥ svopayoginaḥ parikarasya rakṣaṇam apramādaḥ|
[ekasya kamaṇḍalusahāyatā] ekasyaiva kamaṇḍaludvitīyasyāvasthānam|
[strīgītanartitālāpavilāsānāṃ] srīsambandhino gītanṛtyasalāpavilāsādeḥ [upekṣaṇaṃ] pariharaṇam|
[striyā raho 'vyavasthānam] striyā ca sahaikānte 'vasthitivarjanamiti sahāvasthitimātrasyeha niṣedhaḥ, pūrvaṃ tu tatsambhogasyeti na paunaruktyam|
[sragabhyaṅgādivarjanaṃ] sragvilepanābhyaṅgādivarjanaṃ ca||
children.translated_text: This must necessarily be performed by the observant one. Abstention from meat, women, and honey — the avoidance of meat, women, and honey. But therein, the abstention from meat is only for the <s>Śūdra</s>, since for the others the prohibition is already established even without a vow. 'Sleeping on the ground' means sleeping on a bare surface. [Guarding of accoutrements] — guarding, i.e. carefulness regarding one's own implements such as the antelope skin, rosary, staff, water-pot, and the like. [Being accompanied only by a water-pot] — remaining alone with only a water-pot as companion. [Disregarding women's singing, dancing, conversation, and coquetry] — avoiding singing, dancing, conversation, coquetry, and the like connected with women. [Not remaining alone with a woman] — avoiding staying together with a woman in seclusion — here what is prohibited is merely staying together, whereas previously it was sexual intercourse with them; so there is no redundancy. [Avoidance of garlands, unguents, and the like] — avoiding garlands, ointments, massage-oils, and the like.
Times for <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites)
Furthermore —
on the fourteenth of the dark fortnight,
on the eighth, at the <s>Siddhadarśana</s>,
<s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites) [should be performed] at all <s>parvan</s> (juncture) days,
at the equinoxes, and on the <s>aṣṭakā</s> days and the like.
Those to be honored
The honoring of the <s>guru</s> and those equal to him, relatives,
and of elder brothers too,
with <s>madhuparka</s> (honey-mixture) and the like.

children.text: full line: pūjanaṃ madhuparkādyaiḥ svakāle strīniveṣaṇam (MrgT_3.21)

children.translated_text: Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
On the fourteenth and eighth of the dark fortnight

children.text: kṛṣṇāṣṭamīcaturdaśyoḥ [siddhadarśane] siddhasandarśane [viṣuve] viṣuvaduttarāyaṇārkendugrahaṇādiṣu [sarveṣu parvasu] sarvaparvakāleṣu ca śrāddhaṃ viśeṣataśca aṣṭakādiṣu iti, kanyāgate 'rke māghatryodaśīprabhṛtiṣu ca kuryāt|
children.translated_text: — on the eighth and fourteenth of the dark half; [at <s>Siddhadarśana</s>] — at the conjunction with <s>Siddha</s>; [at the equinox] — at the equinox, the northern solstice, solar and lunar eclipses, and the like; [at all <s>parvan</s> days] — at all juncture-times, the <s>śrāddha</s> should be performed; and especially at the <s>aṣṭakā</s> days and the like — and one should perform it from the thirteenth of <s>Māgha</s> onward when the sun is in <s>Kanyā</s> (Virgo).
Of the <s>guru</s> and those equal to him, relatives

children.text: guroḥ guruputrādīnāṃ ca tattulyānāmanyeṣāṃ ca vayovidyādharmādivṛddhānāṃ ca [jyāyasāṃ bhrātṝṇāṃ] janmādinā dīkṣādyanugrahataśca jyeṣṭhānāṃ bhrātṝṇāṃ ca [madhuparkādyaiḥ] madhuparkavastrālaṃkārādyaiḥ pūjanaṃ kāryam||
children.translated_text: — of the <s>guru</s>, the <s>guru</s>'s sons and the like, and of others equal to them who are senior in age, learning, dharma, and the like; [of elder brothers] — of brothers who are elder by birth, initiation, and other [forms of] grace — [with <s>madhuparka</s> and the like] — with <s>madhuparka</s>, cloth, ornaments, and the like, honoring should be done.
Conduct of the <s>bhautika</s> (worldly) observant after completion of the vow
To specify what was stated — that the <s>bhautika</s> (worldly practitioner) has a good wife, household, and prosperity — he says:
(continued)
Enjoyment of women at the proper time;
engagement in auspicious conduct,
wearing of fragrance, garlands, and the like.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
Enjoyment of women at the proper time

children.text:
vratasamāpterūrdhvaṃ dārasaṃgrahakālaḥ strīṇāṃ svakālaḥ, tasminniṣevaṇam|
[maṅgalācārayogitvaṃ gandhamālyādidhāraṇam] maṅgalācaraṇayogaṃ prakaṭaṃ sragādidhāraṇaṃ ca kuryāt||
children.translated_text: — after the completion of the vow, the time for taking a wife — that is the 'proper time' for women; at that time, enjoyment [is permitted]. [Engagement in auspicious conduct, wearing of fragrance, garlands, and the like] — one should engage in auspicious practices and openly wear garlands and the like.
Non-common conduct specific to <s>Śaivas</s>
Now, the non-common conduct previously commenced with 'and the other, when the occasion has arrived' is formulated in sūtra form:
For each of these separately,
conduct too is prescribed.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):

children.text: eteṣāṃ deśikādīnāṃ pṛthakpṛthag vidhiniṣedhātmaka ācāro vidhīyate anuśāsyate|
children.translated_text: For these — the <s>Deśika</s> (preceptor) and the others — conduct, consisting of injunctions and prohibitions, is separately prescribed, i.e. taught.
Rules of conduct for the <s>Deśika</s> (preceptor)
Here, for the <s>Deśika</s> first, he says:
The <s>guru</s> should bestow grace
upon those impelled by the power of <s>Maheśa</s> (Great Lord),
having ascertained [their fitness] through tests
prescribed by the elders, with diligence.
Because, by not [initiating] devotees of <s>Śiva</s>
and by [initiating] those who are wayward,
one incurs the need for expiation —
therefore, one should exercise the utmost care.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
'That primal power descends upon a person in his last birth' —
thus, for the souls (<s>aṇus</s>) who have been touched by the grace-power of the Supreme Lord, the <s>guru</s> should bestow grace in the form of <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation).

children.text:
kīdṛśaṃ kiṃ ca kṛtvetyāha---
vṛddhoktābhiḥ parīkṣābhiḥ prayatnavān parijñāya vidyāvṛddhā āgamoktaparīkṣākuśalā atra vṛddhaśabdenoktāḥ|
tadabhihitābhiḥ parīkṣābhiḥ saprayatnaḥ san parijñāya saṃsāravaitṛṣṇyamanugrahārthināṃ ca buddhvā|
yasmādevaṃvidhāṃ parīkṣāṃ vinā śivabhaktānāṃ kadācidakaraṇaṃ vyabhicāriṇāṃ ca karaṇaṃ syāt|
tadānīṃ prāyaścittī gururbhavet| ataḥ [param] prakṛṣṭaṃ yatnaṃ tadāśayaparīkṣaṇe kuryāt||
children.translated_text: What kind [of testing], and having done what, he says: 'Having ascertained through tests prescribed by the elders, with diligence' — those who are senior in learning, skilled in tests prescribed by the <s>Āgamas</s>, are called 'elders' (<s>vṛddha</s>) by this word. Having ascertained through the tests stated by them, being diligent — having understood [the candidates'] disenchantment with <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) and their desire for grace. Because, without such a test, there may be non-initiation of <s>Śiva</s>-devotees and initiation of the wayward. Then the <s>guru</s> would incur the need for expiation. Therefore, one should exercise supreme care in examining their disposition.
The rite called <s>saṃjīvana</s> (revival)

children.text: prasaṅgād vyabhicāriṇi dīkṣite saṃjīvanākhyaṃ karma vaktumāha---
children.translated_text: Incidentally, to state the rite called <s>saṃjīvana</s> when a wayward person has been initiated, he says:
One should perform the <s>saṃjīvana</s> (revival) rite
when a wayward person has been initiated,
by the order of creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>), through the <s>saṃhitā</s>-oblation,
accompanied by a full [oblation] at the end.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):

children.text: kṛtrimasaṃsāravaitṛṣṇyagurudevādibhaktiprakarṣāsṃdarśanādaparipakvve jane vyabhicāriṇi dīkṣite sati [sṛṣṭitaḥ] sṛṣṭikrameṇa pratitattvasaṃhitāhomāt sarvasamāptau [adhaḥ] adhastāt [pūrṇāsamanvitaṃ] pūrṇāhutidānataḥ [saṃjīvanaṃ] saṃjīvanākhyaṃ karma dīkṣāphalapratibandhakaṃ bhavati|
children.translated_text: When a person who has not matured — through displaying false disenchantment with <s>saṃsāra</s> and false intense devotion to the <s>guru</s>, the deity, and the like — a wayward person, has been initiated, [one should perform the <s>saṃjīvana</s> rite] by the order of creation, through the <s>saṃhitā</s>-oblation at each <s>tattva</s> (principle), at the conclusion of all; 'below' — at the end; 'accompanied by a full [oblation]' — by the offering of a full oblation — the rite called <s>saṃjīvana</s> (revival), which obstructs the fruit of the [invalid] initiation, comes into being.

children.text: nanu dīkṣāyāṃ karmadāhasya vṛttatvāt punaḥ saṃjīvanam kathamupapadyata ityetadāha---
children.translated_text: Now, since the burning of <s>karma</s> has already occurred in the initiation, how is a revival possible? To that he says:
There is no revival of <s>karma</s>
that has been burned — that conception is false;
it is [merely] the pacification of the harm and misfortune
[that would befall] the <s>guru</s> — indeed, that is the expiation.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):

children.text:
dīkṣitasya tāvadanarhatvādeva dīkṣāphalaṃ na siddham| ataḥ kiṃ tasya saṃjīvanoktyā| na ca dagdhasya karmaṇaḥ [saṃjīvanamasti] saṃjīvanopapattiḥ|
[khedanāpāyaśamanam] api tu asthāne vṛthaiva mantrāḥ kheditāḥ, tataḥ pratyavāyo mā bhūditi tacchāntaye gurostatprāyaścittam||
children.translated_text: For the initiated person, because of his very unworthiness, the fruit of initiation has not been accomplished. So what is the point of speaking of revival for him? Nor is there the possibility of revival of <s>karma</s> that has been burned. Rather, [the rite serves for] the pacification of [the consequence that] the <s>mantras</s> were labored over in vain, in an inappropriate case, lest there be a negative consequence from that — for the pacification of that, this is the <s>guru</s>'s expiation.
Initiation for those from other traditions
For those who have fallen from the positions
of other philosophical systems and follow [Śaivism],
having performed [the rite] thus up to their own birth-class,
one should perform the initiation in reverse order.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
From the positions of other philosophical systems

children.text:
yāḥ kāpilasaugatādiparadarśanoditāḥ saṃsthā uktayastābhyaḥ cyutānāṃ bhāvanādivaśād bhraṣṭānām [anuvartināṃ] kālāntarataḥ śaktipātamāhātmyād andhatvanivṛttyā śaivamārgānuvartināṃ satāṃ prāyaścittārtham evam iti prāgvatsṛṣṭikramātsāmānyamantrasaṃhitāhomaṃ svajātyantaṃ kuryāt|
svajātiśabdena caturdaśavidhabhūtasargamadhyasthabrāhmaṇādijātisamāśrayo bhūloke lakṣyate|
children.translated_text: — those positions taught in other systems such as <s>Kāpila</s> (Sāṃkhya), <s>Saugata</s> (Buddhist), and the like; of those who have fallen from them — who have turned away through the power of contemplation and the like; [who follow] — who, by the force of the descent of [Śiva's] power at a later time, follow the <s>Śaiva</s> path through the removal of blindness — for such persons, for the purpose of expiation, one should perform the <s>saṃhitā</s>-oblation with the general <s>mantra</s> in the order of creation, as before, up to their own birth-class. By the word 'own class' (<s>svajāti</s>), the birth-class of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the like situated within the fourteen-fold category of created beings on the earth-plane is indicated.

children.text: tadantaṃ yāvat| tatastu vilomataḥ saṃhārakramāt prāguktavat svādhaḥparyantaṃ yāvad [dīkṣāṃ kuryād] dīkṣayā yojanikāṃ kuryāt||
children.translated_text: Up to that extent. Then in reverse order — by the order of dissolution (<s>saṃhāra</s>), as previously stated, down to one's own [level], one should perform, i.e. yoke [the candidate] through initiation.
Concealing of <s>mantras</s>
They are not regarded as qualified
to employ <s>mantras</s>, due to [their propensity for] rebirth;
because of [the risk to] the accomplishment of <s>mantra</s>-practice,
one should perform other [rites] for them separately.

children.text: The text of this verse is awkward if it really means

children.translated_text: Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):

children.text:
te caiva dīkṣitā api punarbhavatayā [mantraprayoktāraḥ na matāḥ] mantraprayogārhā na bhavanti|
nānyasyānugrahādivyāpārayogyāḥ|
nāpyātmano [mantrasādhanasaṃsiddheḥ] mantrasādhanajanitāyāḥ siddheḥ prayoktāraḥ prayojakāḥ syuḥ|
mantrasiddhyarthamāmnātasya kriyākāṇḍasya prayoge teṣāmanarhakatvaṃ bhavatīti yāvat|
ataḥ ebhyaḥ sakāśād [itarāṇi kuryād] mantrasādhanānyanyāni sampādayet pṛthak kuryāt| na tveṣāṃ tāni prakaṭayedityarthaḥ||
children.translated_text: Those who have been thus initiated, because of [their propensity for] rebirth, are not regarded as qualified to employ <s>mantras</s>. They are not suitable for activities such as bestowing grace upon others. Nor can they be agents, i.e. effectuators, of the accomplishment (<s>siddhi</s>) born of <s>mantra</s>-practice for themselves. That is to say, they lack qualification for the employment of the ritual procedure (<s>kriyākāṇḍa</s>) prescribed for the accomplishment of <s>mantras</s>. Therefore, from them one should accomplish other <s>mantra</s>-practices separately — that is, one should not reveal those [mantras] to them.
Those worthy of <s>mantra</s>-explanation

children.text: na ca sarvatra tadgopanīyam| api tu---
children.translated_text: Nor should it be concealed everywhere. Rather —
One should expound the meaning of the <s>Tantras</s>
to devotees of <s>Śiva</s>, free from jealousy,
properly, to those who follow the proper path,
preserving the lineage of the <s>guru</s>.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
Preserving the lineage of the <s>guru</s>

children.text: gurvāmnāyakramaṃ rakṣan [nyāyavartibhyaḥ] śāstrānuṣṭhānaparebhyaḥ śivabhaktebhyaḥ tantrārthaṃ [gatamatsaraḥ] anviṣṭaḥ san [nyāyataḥ] vakṣyamāṇanyāyena vyākuryāt||
children.translated_text: — protecting the succession of the <s>guru</s>'s tradition; [to those who follow the proper path] — to those devoted to the practice of the scriptures, to devotees of <s>Śiva</s>; the meaning of the <s>Tantras</s>; [free from jealousy] — being free from envy; [properly] — by the method to be stated, one should expound.
Times to be avoided in exposition
Not during indigestion or sour belching,
nor when troubled by feces or urine,
not during vomiting or diarrhea,
nor when unbathed after intercourse.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
During indigestion or sour belching

children.text:
ajīrṇatvādāmlāmburasodgāre [viṇmūtrabādhane] mūtrapurīṣottambhane [chardyāṃ] vāntau na vṛttāyāṃ atisāre ca na vyākhyānaṃ kuryāt|
[nāsnātaḥ kṛtamaithunaḥ] na cāpyupabhogānantaramakṛtasnānaḥ san||
children.translated_text: — when there is belching of sour liquid due to indigestion; [troubled by feces or urine] — when there is retention of urine or feces; [during vomiting] — when vomiting has occurred, or during diarrhea, one should not give exposition. [Nor unbathed after intercourse] — nor after sexual enjoyment without having bathed.
Method of exposition
He states the method of exposition:
Standing on a purified ground,
protected from the hearing of the uninitiated (<s>paśu</s>),
having worshipped [<s>Śiva</s>] stationed within the boundary-circle,
<s>Śiva</s>, whose form is <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ),
and the Lord of <s>Gaṇas</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>), and the <s>guru</s>,
and the implements that are the support of the rite,
having placed the manuscript with its well-guarded sūtras
upon some [support],
one should say 'Come, recite' to the accomplished [disciple],
facing east or north;
the <s>guru</s> should commence the exposition,
preceded by a statement of the connection and the meaning.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
On purified

children.text: upalepanādinā pavitrite [paśuśravaṇavarjite] adīkṣitaśravaṇarakṣite [mahītale] bhūtale [paridhyantaḥsthitaṃ] sūtroccāṭanakṛtamaryādātmakaparidhyantarasthaṃ [śivaṃ praṇavavigrahaṃ] praṇavākāraṃ parameśvaraṃ [gaṇādhyakṣaṃ] gaṇeśvaraṃ guruṃ ca [iṣṭvā] abhyarcya [kriyāśrayaṃ kārakaṃ ca] vyākhyākriyopayogikaraṇīsūtrādikārakamiṣṭvā
children.translated_text: — on ground purified by smearing and the like; [protected from the hearing of the uninitiated] — guarded against the hearing of the uninitiated; [on the ground] — on the earth; [stationed within the boundary-circle] — stationed within the boundary established by the rite of unfastening the sūtra; [<s>Śiva</s>, whose form is <s>Praṇava</s>] — the Supreme Lord in the form of <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ); [the Lord of <s>Gaṇas</s>] — <s>Gaṇeśvara</s>, and the <s>guru</s>; [having worshipped] — having honored; [the implements that are the support of the rite] — the instruments such as the stylus, thread, and the like that are useful for the exposition-rite, having worshipped [them],

children.text: \Bhatt's reading would indeed give what seems a strange gloss here,
making a reference to three of the śāstrasambandhas out of
the word kāraka; but \Brunner's too is not smooth. She suggests
(1985:362, fn.5) that the karaṇīsūtra is used to trace the box
to enclose the praṇava just mentioned in verse 31 and that the
teacher would use it while explaining maṇḍalas.

children.translated_text: The manuscript with well-guarded sūtras

— the manuscript with its well-preserved, beautifully strung sūtras; having placed it upon some pedestal, mechanical support, or the like; addressing the accomplished disciple with 'Come' and [saying] 'Recite'; one should instruct. And the <s>guru</s> himself, [facing east or north] — facing east or facing north, should commence the exposition. 'Preceded by a statement of the connection and the meaning' — what kind of connection? It is sixfold: supreme, great, intermediate, divine, divine-and-non-divine, and non-divine.

children.text: arthaḥ prayojanam| uktistātparyakathanam| abhidheyamityarthaḥ| tatpurassaraṃ sambandhābhidheyaprayojanavarṇanaṃ prathamaṃ kuryāditi bhāvaḥ|
children.translated_text: The meaning is the purpose. The statement is the declaration of the purport — that is the meaning of <s>abhidheya</s> (subject-matter). One should first describe the connection, subject-matter, and purpose — this is the import.
Furthermore,
one should state the stream (<s>srotas</s>), the sub-stream (<s>anusrotas</s>),
their divisions, and their enumeration,
and one's own <s>guru</s>, for the sake of the [scripture's] propagation;
one would be a thief by not declaring that.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
The stream, sub-stream, their divisions, and enumeration

children.text:
sroto 'nusrotastadbhedasaṃkhyānaṃ [svaṃ guruṃ ca] sva gurukramaṃ ca [pravṛttaye brūyād] śāstrapravṛttihetuṃ vadet|
[tadakīrtanāt steyī bhavet] gurorakīrtanāddhi steyaṃ bhavati|
children.translated_text: — the enumeration of the stream, sub-stream, and their divisions; [one's own <s>guru</s>] — one's own <s>guru</s>'s lineage; [should state for the sake of propagation] — one should declare the reason for the scripture's propagation. [By not declaring the <s>guru</s>, one would be a thief] — indeed, by not declaring the <s>guru</s>, theft occurs.
The streams (<s>srotas</s>)
Now, what are the streams and what are the sub-streams? He says:
The streams are: <s>Kāmika</s> and the rest as the upper (<s>ūrdhva</s>);
<s>Asitāṅga</s> and the rest as the southern (<s>dakṣiṇa</s>);
<s>Sammoha</s> and the rest as the northern (<s>uttara</s>); the eastern (<s>prācya</s>)
is <s>Trotala</s> and the rest, in extensive [detail];
the western (<s>āpya</s>) is <s>Caṇḍāsidhāra</s> and the rest,
under the dominion of <s>Caṇḍanātha</s> (<s>Caṇḍeśvara</s>).
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):

children.text:
kāmikādi kāmikādīni jñānāni [ūrdhvaṃ srotāṃsi] ūrdhvasrotaḥ|
[asitāṅgādi] asitāṅgādīni dakṣiṇam| sammohādi sammohādīni uttaram|
trotalādijñānāni [prācyaṃ] prācyāni| [caṇḍāsidhārādi] caṇḍāsidhārādīni [āpyaṃ] paścimam| tacca [caṇḍanāthaparigrahaṃ] caṇḍeśvaraparigrahatayā jñeyamiti pañcasrotaḥkathanam||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāmika</s> and the rest — the <s>Kāmika</s> and other [Āgamas] constitute the upper stream. <s>Asitāṅga</s> and the rest — the southern. <s>Sammoha</s> and the rest — the northern. The <s>Trotala</s> and other [Āgamas are] the eastern. <s>Caṇḍāsidhāra</s> and the rest are the western. And that is to be understood as under the dominion of <s>Caṇḍeśvara</s> — thus the statement of the five streams.
The sub-streams (<s>anusrotas</s>)
Now the sub-streams are stated:
<s>Śaiva</s>, <s>Māntreśvara</s>, <s>Gāṇa</s>,
<s>Divya</s>, <s>Ārṣa</s>, and <s>Gauhyaka</s>,
<s>Yoginī</s>, <s>Siddhakaulā</s> —
the wise know these eight as streams;
they follow along with each stream —
one should state them separately.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):

children.text: śaivādīni aṣṭau srotāṃsi [pratisroto 'nuyāyīni] pratisroto 'nuvidhāyinīti, etānyekaikasminnūrdhvādau srotasyanusrotastvena sthitānītyarthaḥ| [tāni] etāni ca vibhāgaśaḥ [brūyāt] kathayet||
children.translated_text: The <s>Śaiva</s> and the other eight are streams; 'they follow along with each stream' — they are subsidiary streams (<s>anusrotas</s>), meaning that these are established as sub-streams within each of the upper and other [main] streams. And one should state them separately.
The <s>Śaiva</s> stream
Now, he explains the <s>Śaiva</s>, which was mentioned first among these:
The <s>Śaiva</s> is the original <s>tantra</s>-composition,
accomplished by [divine] command, without doubt.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
Previously

children.text: prāthamye sargaprārambha eva yacchivabhaṭṭārakāpāditatantranirmāṇam [ājñāsiddham] ājñāmātrasiddham [asaṃśayam] asandehamativīryavat tajjñānaṃ śaivam|
children.translated_text: at the very commencement of the first creation, the tantra-composition produced by the Blessed <s>Śiva</s> [is called <s>ājñāsiddha</s>] — accomplished by mere command — [without doubt] undoubted, possessing extraordinary power; that knowledge is <s>Śaiva</s>.
The <s>Māntreśvara</s>, <s>Gāṇa</s>, <s>Divya</s>, and <s>Ārṣa</s> streams
He states the tetrad beginning with <s>Māntreśvara</s>:
That [knowledge], by the Lords (<s>Īśānas</s>), the <s>Gaṇas</s>, the gods,
and the sages, by His will,
having understood [it], compiled in their own words,
has come to bear those [respective] names.
[Vṛtti:]
That

children.text: taccaivaṃ jñānaṃ [īśānaiḥ] mantreśvaraiḥ gaṇaiḥ devaiḥ munibhiśca vijñāya [tadicchayā] śivecchayaiva [svoktyā] svavācā sampraṇītaṃ sat krameṇa [tādākhyaṃ samupāgatam] māntreśvaraṃ gāṇeśvaraṃ divyamārṣaṃ ca saṃjñayā sampannam||
children.translated_text: — that very knowledge — [by the <s>Īśānas</s>] by the <s>Mantreśvaras</s>, the <s>Gaṇas</s>, the gods, and the sages, having understood [it], [by His will] by <s>Śiva's</s> will alone, [in their own words] composed in their own speech, has sequentially [come to bear those names] attained the designations <s>Māntreśvara</s>, <s>Gāṇeśvara</s>, <s>Divya</s>, and <s>Ārṣa</s>.
The <s>Gauhyaka</s> stream
He explains the <s>Gauhyaka</s>:
<s>Guhyakas</s>, serpents, <s>Yakṣas</s>,
and <s>Dānavas</s>, impelled by <s>Śiva</s> —
what they said in condensed form,
that stream is known as <s>Gauhyaka</s>.
[Vṛtti:]

children.text: guhyakākhyayā bhujagayakṣadānavā ucyante| [śiveritāḥ yadūcurupasaṃhṛtya] taiḥ śivabhaṭṭārakapreritaiḥ yatsaṃkṣipyoktaṃ tad gauhyakaṃ srotaḥ||
children.translated_text: By the designation <s>Guhyaka</s>, serpents, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Dānavas</s> are meant. [Impelled by <s>Śiva</s>, what they said in condensed form] — what was stated in condensed form by those impelled by the Blessed <s>Śiva</s>, that is the <s>Gauhyaka</s> stream.
The <s>Yoginīkaula</s>
He states the <s>Yoginīkaula</s>:
The <s>Yoginīs</s> obtained the knowledge
that immediately illuminates yoga.
That is the <s>Yoginīkaula</s> —
it has not passed beyond them; it [remains] from them alone.
[Vṛtti:]

children.text: sadyaḥ tatkṣaṇameva [yogāvabhāsakaṃ] yogamavabhāsayati yattathāvidhaṃ jñānaṃ śivabhaṭṭārakād yoginyaḥ [lebhire] prāpuḥ| tacca tābhya eva sakāśād nottīrṇaṃ nānyatra prasṛtam āsveva sampradāyatayā sthitamityarthaḥ||
children.translated_text: [Immediately] at that very moment, [illuminating yoga] — the <s>Yoginīs</s> [obtained] received from the Blessed <s>Śiva</s> such knowledge that illuminates yoga. And that has not passed beyond from them to others — it has not spread elsewhere; the meaning is that it has remained within them alone as a tradition.
The <s>Siddhakaula</s>
Now the one called <s>Siddhakaula</s> is stated:
Similarly, another [stream] — the condensation
that is mixed (<s>miśra</s>) is indeed [called] 'mixed.'
[Vṛtti:]

children.text:
yadanyat siddhakaulākhyaṃ jñānaṃ tat tathā iti yoginīkaulavat| yathā na tad yoginībhya uttīrṇaṃ tathedaṃ siddhebhyasteṣveva pāramparyeṇa sthitamiti yāvat|
[yaḥ] yastu [miśraḥ] vyāmiśraḥ saṃhāraḥ saṃgraho yathā māntreśvaramapi munibhiḥ āṛṣaṃ vā guhyakaiḥ saṃkṣipyoktaṃ sa miśra eva saṃkṣepaḥ etatsaṃjñayā yukto jñeyaḥ||
children.translated_text:
That other knowledge called <s>Siddhakaula</s> is 'similarly' — like the <s>Yoginīkaula</s>. Just as that did not pass beyond the <s>Yoginīs</s>, so this [has remained] among the <s>Siddhas</s> alone in succession — that is the meaning.
[That] which is a 'mixed' (<s>vyāmiśra</s>) condensation — such as when the <s>Māntreśvara</s> [stream] is condensed by sages, or when the <s>Ārṣa</s> [is condensed] by <s>Guhyakas</s> — that 'mixed' condensation should be known as bearing this designation.
And these divisions of the downstream [traditions]:
Because of being divided by differences among teachers,
their number cannot be determined.
[Vṛtti:]

Being differentiated by differences among speakers, these are indeed innumerable.
Now he states the division into ten and eighteen in the upstream [tradition]:
The <s>Śaiva</s> and <s>Raudra</s> — the great divisions —
are ten and eighteen in the upper [stream].
The <s>Raudra</s> [tantras] were uttered by <s>Rudras</s>
possessed by <s>Śiva</s>, not from their own intellect.
[Vṛtti:]

children.text:
śaivāḥ kāmikādayo vakṣyamāṇā daśa bhedāḥ| raudrā vijayādayo 'ṣṭādaśa|
ete [ūrdhvake] ūrdhvasrotasi [mahābhedāḥ] bhedāḥ|
tatra śaivāḥ śivabhaṭṭārakeṇa upadiṣṭāḥ|
raudrāstu [śivāviṣṭaiḥ] śivādhiṣṭhai rudraiḥ [udgīrṇāḥ| na svabuddhitaḥ] na svamanīṣikayā||
children.translated_text:
The <s>Śaiva</s> [tantras] are ten divisions, beginning with <s>Kāmika</s>, to be stated. The <s>Raudra</s> are eighteen, beginning with <s>Vijaya</s>.
These are [in the upper stream] — the great divisions of the upper stream.
Therein, the <s>Śaiva</s> [tantras] were taught by the Blessed <s>Śiva</s> [himself].
But the <s>Raudra</s> [were] uttered by <s>Rudras</s> [possessed by <s>Śiva</s>] presided over by <s>Śiva</s>. [Not from their own intellect] — not from their own thought.
The twenty-eight <s>Śaivāgamas</s>
He recites those very divisions:
Of the <s>Śaiva</s> [tantras], <s>Kāmika</s> is first,
<s>Yogaja</s>, <s>Cintyaka</s>,
<s>Kāraṇa</s>, <s>Ajita</s>,
the one called <s>Dīpta</s>, <s>Sūkṣmaka</s>, the supreme
<s>Sāhasra</s>, the one named <s>Aṃśumat</s>,
and <s>Suprabheda</s> — [these] ten, they know.
Of the <s>Raudra</s> [tantras], <s>Vijaya</s> is first,
<s>Niḥśvāsa</s>, <s>Pārameśvara</s>,
<s>Svāyambhuva</s>, then <s>Āgneya</s>,
<s>Vīrabhadra</s>, and <s>Raurava</s>,
<s>Makuṭa</s>, the one called <s>Vimala</s>,
and the one called <s>Candrajñāna</s>,
<s>Mukhabimba</s>, <s>Udgīta</s>,
<s>Lalita</s>, the one named <s>Siddha</s>,
<s>Santāna</s>, and <s>Śarvokta</s>,
<s>Kiraṇa</s>, and the supreme <s>Vātula</s>.
[Vṛtti:]

Clear.
[The rule for commencing exposition]
Having commenced that [tantra], one should not expound for too long
on the first day.
Even at the beginning, not merely excessive
questions and counter-questions —
having taught three root <s>sūtras</s>,
or two, or even one,
one should stop. [One who continues] speaking beyond that
is obstructed by obstacles.
[Vṛtti:]
Having commenced that

children.text:
tat śaivaṃ raudraṃ tantramārabhya nāticiraṃ prathame 'hani prathame 'hni [vyākuryād] vyācakṣīta|
nāpi śiṣyaḥ prārambhe [sampraśnapratipraśnātimātrakaṃ] sampraśnapratipraśnairatimātraṃ prārambhaṃ kaluṣīkuryādityadhyāhāraḥ|
kīdṛśastarhi prārambhaḥ syādityāha---trīṇīti, vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇāni mūlāni sūtrāṇi mūlasūtrāṇi trīṇi [tathā dve] yadvā dve sūtre, [athāpi vā ekam] yadvā ekameva sūtram|
vidhāya iti vyākhyāya [uparamed] viramed| [ūrdhvaṃ vadan vighnaiḥ viruddhyate] tadadhikaṃ vyākurvantaṃ hi vighnā rundhantītyarthaḥ||
children.translated_text:
— having commenced that <s>Śaiva</s> or <s>Raudra</s> tantra, one should [expound] explain not for too long on the first day.
Nor should the student at the beginning [through excessive questions and counter-questions] make the beginning turbid through excessive questions and counter-questions — this is to be supplied.
What kind of beginning should there be? He says: 'Three' and so forth — three root <s>sūtras</s> of the characteristics to be described; [or two] alternatively two <s>sūtras</s>; [or even one] alternatively one <s>sūtra</s> alone.
'Having taught' — having explained, [one should stop] should cease. [One who speaks beyond that is obstructed by obstacles] — for obstacles obstruct one who expounds more than that — that is the meaning.
Definition of root <s>sūtra</s>
It was said 'three root <s>sūtras</s>.' He shows those:
That in which, as in a seed,
the tree of the great tantra's meaning
appears — that is the root <s>sūtra</s>,
adorned with the word 'atha' and the like.
[Vṛtti:]
In which

children.text:
yasmin sūtre [mahātantrārthapādapaḥ bīja iva] sakalatantrārtho bīja iva mahāvṛkṣa ārūḍhaḥ ābhāti śaktyātmanāvasthitaḥ pratibhāti [tad athaśabdādyalaṃkṛtaṃ] tadathaśabdaśivasiddhādimaṅgalyaśabdālaṃkṛtaṃ mūlasūtraṃ mūlaṃ sūtraṃ jñeyam|
yathā---`athānādimalāpeta' ityādi||%
\quote{athānādimalāpetaḥ
${\rm \Mrg\VP\ 2:1a.}$}
children.translated_text:
— in which <s>sūtra</s>, [the tree of the great tantra's meaning], like a [great tree in a] seed, the entire meaning of the tantra appears — abides in the form of potency — [that, adorned with the word 'atha' and the like] — that which is adorned with auspicious words such as 'atha,' '<s>Śiva</s>,' '<s>Siddha</s>,' and the like — is to be known as the root <s>sūtra</s> (root aphorism).
For example: 'Now, freed from beginningless impurity...' and so forth.
Of that [meaning], the enumeration (<s>uddeśa</s>) would be another [root <s>sūtra</s>],
expressing number, designation, and the like.
Its definition — the statement of its own nature —
and different from that is the collection of commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>).
[Vṛtti:]

children.text: tasya mūlasūtropakṣiptasya tantrārthasya [uddeśakam] uddeśaḥ [anyad] dvitīyamūlasūtram [syāt] yat saṃkhyāsaṃjñādivācakaṃ saṃkhyāsaṃjñādikaṃ vakti| yathehaiva---
children.translated_text: Of that tantra-meaning introduced by the root <s>sūtra</s>, the [enumeration] is the second root <s>sūtra</s> [which would be] that which states number, designation, and the like. As here [in this very text]:

children.text:
tripadārthaṃ catuṣpādaṃ mahātantraṃ jagatpatiḥ|
sūtreṇaikena saṃgṛhya prāha vistaraśaḥ punaḥ|| iti|%
\quote{tripadārthaṃ catuṣpādaṃ \devdot\ prāha vistaraśaḥ punaḥ
${\rm \Mrg\VP\ 2:2.}$}
children.translated_text: 'The great tantra of three topics and four sections — the Lord of the world, having condensed it in one <s>sūtra</s>, then spoke it in detail.'

children.text: tṛtīyamapi mūlasūtratvena jñeyaṃ yatra tallakṣaṇaṃ svarūpoktiścāsti| yathā---
children.translated_text: The third also is to be known as a root <s>sūtra</s> — that in which there is its definition and statement of its own nature. For example:
'Creation, maintenance, destruction, concealment, and liberation of the world.'

children.text:
atra hi śivaḥ pāśajālamapohatīti mūlasūtropakṣiptamapohanaṃ lakṣyate|
pañcavidhakṛtyātmakamapohanasvarūpamuktam| [tadanyaḥ] tatastvanyāni yāni sūtrāṇi tadvyākhyānāya pravṛttatvād [bhāṣyasaṃgrahaḥ]
bhāṣyasaṃgrahatvena jñeyāni|
yadvā tallakṣaṇaṃ svarūpoktiriti tairmūlasūtroddeśasūtrādibhiḥ sūtrairyadabhidheyasya lakṣaṇaṃ sā svarūpoktirjñeyā|
mūlasūtradvayapramukhasūtrasaṅgrahaḥ svarūpākhyayā boddhavya ityarthaḥ|
children.translated_text:
For here, 'removal' (<s>apohana</s>) — introduced in the root <s>sūtra</s> [as] '<s>Śiva</s> removes the network of bonds' — is characterized [through its definition].
The fivefold nature of removal as [constituting] the five acts is stated. [Different from that] — the other <s>sūtras</s>, being engaged in explaining that, [are a collection of commentary] — are to be known as a collection of commentary.
Or: 'its definition, the statement of its own nature' — by those <s>sūtras</s> — root <s>sūtras</s>, enumeration <s>sūtras</s>, and the like — whatever is the definition of what is to be expressed, that is the 'statement of its own nature.'
The collection of <s>sūtras</s> headed by the pair of root <s>sūtras</s> is to be understood by the designation 'own nature' — that is the meaning.

children.text:
tadanyastu tadvyaktibhedagrantho bhāṣyasaṃgraha iti mantavyaḥ|
asmiṃśca pakṣe svarūpagranthasya sarvasyaiva mūlasūtratvam| tena ca `trīṇi mūlāni sūtrāṇi dve tathaikamathāpi vā} vidhāyoparamed' ityaviruddham||
children.translated_text:
Different from that is the text that [gives] elaboration of distinctions — that should be considered as the 'collection of commentary.'
And in this interpretation, the entire 'own nature' text has the character of a root <s>sūtra</s>. Therefore, the statement 'having taught three root <s>sūtras</s>, or two, or even one, one should stop' — is not contradicted.
The fruit of exposition
He who teaches thus, and he who studies —
both of them, with sins destroyed,
having attained brilliant fame in the world,
may they enter the abode of <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva).
[Vṛtti:]
Thus

children.text: ityuktakrameṇa yo brūte vyākurute| [yaḥ] yaśca adhīte śṛṇoti tau [ubhau] dvāvapi guruśiṣyau [hatakalmaṣau] nirastapāpau [loke] jagati [dīptaṃ] śubhraṃ yaśaḥ prāpya uttarakālaṃ [śāṃkaraṃ dhāma] parameśvaratejo viśetāṃ tatsāyujyaṃ gacchetām||
children.translated_text: — in the manner stated, he who [teaches] expounds; [and] he who studies, who listens — [both] those two, teacher and student, [with sins destroyed] with evils removed, [in the world] in the world, having attained [brilliant] radiant fame, at a subsequent time [may enter the abode of <s>Śaṅkara</s>] the radiance of the Supreme Lord — may they attain union with Him (<s>sāyujya</s>).
The fault of teaching on prohibited days
But otherwise:
On a prohibited day, [teaching] to one who listens
in a manner not prescribed by one's own tantra,
in vain — one who speaks the <s>Śaiva</s> [teaching] here [on such a day]
becomes short-lived; after death, attains the state of a ghost (<s>preta</s>).
[Vṛtti:]

children.text:
svatantroktavidhinā [anadhyāye] ye anadhyāyāsteṣu [śṛṇvate] yaḥ śṛṇoti tasya [mṛṣā] vyarthaṃ tacchrutam|
atha tathāvidhaṃ mṛṣā vyarthaṃ śṛṇvate śaivaṃ śāstraṃ [vadan] kathayan iha loke tāvad alpāyuḥ bhavati|
mṛtaḥ jīvitādūrdhvaṃ [pretatvaṃ] pretabhāvamājñāvilaṅghanataḥ kravyādayonim [aśnute] prāpnoti||
children.translated_text:
According to the rule stated in one's own tantra, [on a prohibited day] — on those days that are prohibited — [for one who listens] for the one who listens, [in vain] that hearing is fruitless.
Furthermore, to one who thus listens fruitlessly, one who [speaks] teaches the <s>Śaiva</s> scripture — first in this world becomes short-lived.
After death — after [the end of] life — [attains ghosthood] attains the state of a ghost, because of transgressing the command, [reaches] a flesh-eating birth.
Prohibited days

children.text: athe ke te anadhyāyā yadvilaṅganādīdṛkphalāvāptirityata āha---
children.translated_text: Now, what are those prohibited days, from the transgression of which such fruit is obtained? He says:
One should not teach on the fourteenth,
on the eighth of both fortnights,
on the first and fifteenth,
on the fourth, and on the day of the sun's transit.

[Vṛtti:]
The sun's transit is the day of <s>saṃkrānti</s> (solstice/transit). The rest is clear.
On [the day of] a thunderclap, meteor, earthquake,
and rainbow in the west — one day.
At the twilights when there is thunder, when there is a burning [glow] in the quarters,
when there is a halo [around the sun], and when there is hail —
[Vṛtti:]
Thunderclap, meteor, earthquake, rainbow in the west

children.text:
nirghātaḥ āntarikṣaḥ śabdaḥ| ulkā daṇḍākāratejorūpā| mahīkampaḥ bhūmikampaḥ| paścāccāpaḥ vāruṇyāṃ diśīndradhanuḥ|
eteṣu [vāsaraḥ] ekavāsaro 'nadhyāyaḥ|
sandhyāstanitadigdāhapariveṣopaleṣu ca] sandhyayormeghagarjitaśrutau, digdāhe, sūryapariveṣadarśane, antarikṣād upalavarṣe caśabdādekāhameva||
children.translated_text:
— a thunderclap is a sound from the atmosphere. A meteor is a fiery form in the shape of a rod. Earthquake is a shaking of the earth. A rainbow in the west is <s>Indra's</s> bow in the western quarter.
On these [occasions], one day is a prohibited [day for study].
[At the twilights when there is thunder, burning glow in the quarters, halo around the sun, hail] — when thunder is heard at the two twilights, when there is a burning glow in the quarters, when a halo around the sun is seen, and when there is a rain of stones from the sky — by the word 'and,' for one day only.
When fog, a rainbow in the east, or a city in the sky
[is seen] — for [the duration of] seeing these —
[Vṛtti:]
Fog, rainbow in the east, city in the sky

children.text:
nīhāre himākhyayā prasiddhe| prāgdhanuṣi ca pūrvadiksthendradhanurdarśane| vyomapure gandharvanagare ca dṛṣṭe|
[eteṣu darśanāt] taddarśanaṃ yāvadanadhyāyaḥ kāryaḥ||
children.translated_text:
— when fog (known as mist) [is present]; when a rainbow in the east — <s>Indra's</s> bow standing in the eastern quarter — is seen; and when a city in the sky — a mirage city — is seen.
[For the duration of seeing these] — one should observe the prohibition from study for as long as that is seen.
And when there is a spike-like [appearance] on the sun or moon,
three days; and when <s>Svarbhānu</s> (Rāhu, eclipse) is seen —
[Vṛtti:]
When there is a spike-like appearance on the sun or moon

children.text: candrārkabimbasthakīlakākṛtyutpātadarśane svarbhānudarśane] rāhudṛṣṭau ca tryaham anadhyāyaḥ||
children.translated_text: — when the sight of a spike-shaped portent on the disc of the moon or sun [occurs]; [when <s>Svarbhānu</s> is seen] — when <s>Rāhu</s> is seen (i.e., during an eclipse) — three days is the prohibition from study.
Five days during the festival of <s>Hari</s> (Indra/Viṣṇu),
and during the sacred thread [ceremony] of the Enemy of sacrifices (<s>Parameśvara</s>).
[Vṛtti:]
During the festival of <s>Hari</s>

children.text: indrotsave hariprabodhādau vā [makhadviṣaḥ pavitre ca] parameśvarapavitrārohaṇe [pañcarātraṃ] pañcāham||
children.translated_text: — during <s>Indra's</s> festival, or the awakening of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) and the like; [during the sacred thread of the Enemy of sacrifices] — during the mounting of the sacred thread of <s>Parameśvara</s> — [five days] five days.
When a cat, serpent, or frog
passes between [teacher and student] — one day.
[Vṛtti:]
Cat, serpent, frog
— when a cat, snake, or frog [passes between] between the expounder and the listener — [one day] for one day.
Three days when a three-hooded serpent is seen;
two days when a two-hooded one [is seen].
[Vṛtti:]

children.text: triphaṇini vyāle sarpe dṛṣṭe tryaham| dviphaṇini tu dvyaham anadhyāyaḥ||\newverse
children.translated_text: When a three-hooded serpent is seen — three days. When a two-hooded one — two days is the prohibition from study.
When a corpse is heard [of] within [the teaching area], at a cremation,
when the smell of a corpse [wafts in], during a harsh wind —
[one should stop] until that ceases; and when a well-known
creature dies — one day.
[Vṛtti:]
Within

children.text:
vyākhyānakālamadhye [śavaśrutau] śavapaṭaharodanādiśrutau [dāhe] gṛhadāhādiśravaṇe [śavagandhe] śavanikaṭadhūmāghrāṇe [kharānile] paruṣatare vāyau ca vahati tadvirāmaṃ vinā vyākhyānaṃ na kuryāt|
[khyātajantumṛtyau] prakhyāte kasmiṃścijjantau mṛte [vāsaram] naikāhaṃ vyācakṣīta||
children.translated_text:
— in the middle of the time of exposition — [when a corpse is heard] when the drum-sounds and wailing associated with a corpse are heard; [at a cremation] when the burning of a house and the like is heard; [when the smell of a corpse] when the smoke near a corpse is smelled; [during a harsh wind] when a very harsh wind blows — one should not conduct the exposition until that ceases.
[When a well-known creature dies] — when some well-known creature dies — [one day] one should not expound for one day.
When the teacher has become <s>Śiva</s> (died) — one month;
when a brother, student, or the like — three days;
when a <s>Śaiva</s> king [dies] — seven days;
when [a king] of the <s>paśu</s>-dharma (non-Śaiva) [dies] — three nights.
[Vṛtti:]

children.text:
gurau śivībhūte māsam anadhyāyaḥ| [bhrātṛśiṣyādike] bhrātari śiṣye ca śivībhūte tryaham| [saptāhaṃ] saptarātraṃ śaive [rājani] rājñi|
paśudharmiṇi rājanyuparate trirātraṃ vyākhyāniṣedhaḥ||
children.translated_text:
When the teacher has become <s>Śiva</s> — one month is the prohibition from study. [When a brother, student, or the like] — when a brother or student has become <s>Śiva</s> — three days. [Seven days] for a <s>Śaiva</s> [king] — when a <s>Śaiva</s> king [dies].
When a king of the <s>paśu</s>-dharma (non-<s>Śaiva</s>) passes away — three nights is the prohibition of exposition.
With respect to those accomplished in one's own tradition and lineage —
likewise in the case of others, the teacher [observes the same].
Commentary:
