children.text: atha anyeṣvapi [svakalpānvayasiddheṣu] svakalpopāyena svaśāstrasādhāraṇyenānviṣṭeṣu śivībhūteṣu [deśikaḥ] ācāryaḥ [tathā] tryahamanadhyāyaṃ kuryāt||
children.translated_text: Now, regarding others also — [those established through their own lineage-tradition] — those sought out through one's own traditional method, by the commonality of one's own scripture, who have become <s>Śiva</s>-realized — [the teacher], the <s>ācārya</s>, should likewise observe a three-day cessation of study.
Rules for Exposition
When expounding —
he should, upon reviewing a previous exposition,
effect reconciliation and the desired [conclusion].
Commentary:
By reviewing the previous exposition, whatever might be contradictory to it should be reconciled.

children.text: kvacicca prastutavyākhyāvasarāgatapāścātyavisaṃvāde itthaṃ tatreṣṭavyamiti pūrvavyākhyāne iṣṭim ativyāptyavyāptiparihāraṃ vadet||
children.translated_text: And wherever, in the course of the present exposition, a subsequent [statement] that was introduced conflicts [with the earlier teaching], he should state in the earlier exposition the desired [correction] — removing over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>) and under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>) — [saying] 'thus it should be understood there.'
A <s>samayī</s> (basic initiate) or a <s>putraka</s> (son-disciple),
having learned something unprecedented,
should, when permitted,
report it to the teacher who occupies the seat (<s>pīṭha</s>).
Commentary:

children.text:
gurugṛhanivāsinā samayinā putrakeṇa vā [kiṃcidapūrvakaṃ] kimapyapūrvaṃ vastu jñātvā tadanujñātena [gurave pīṭhavartine] pīṭhasthagurave nivedanīyam|
gṛhītācāryābhiṣeke kimapyapūrvamanyato 'dhigataṃ putrakasamayinordattānujñayoḥ sakāśāt pīṭhasthena guruṇāvagantavyam||
children.translated_text:
By a <s>samayī</s> or <s>putraka</s> dwelling in the teacher's house, having learned [something] unprecedented — some novel matter — when permitted by him, it should be reported to the teacher occupying the seat (<s>pīṭha</s>).
One who has received the consecration of a teacher (<s>ācāryābhiṣeka</s>), having obtained something unprecedented from elsewhere, should learn it from a <s>putraka</s> or <s>samayī</s> who has been given permission, through the teacher occupying the seat.
Or alternatively,
he may learn from one consecrated by himself, or
[from one] honored by <s>Śaṃkara</s> at the <s>yogapīṭha</s> (seat of yoga),
or, while staying outside, from one who is outside,
even from one consecrated by another who is not on the seat.

children.text:
Vṛtti:
[svābhiṣiktāt] svayamabhiṣiktācāryād yogapīṭhe śrīmatkiraṇādāvāmnātalakṣaṇe viśiṣṭe devaguruśāstrapūjādhāre [iṣṭaśaṃkaraḥ śṛṇuyāt] pūjitaparameśvareṇādhigantavyam| yadi tu bahiḥ sthitaḥ deśāntareṣvaṭan granthānadhigantumicchet tadā bahiḥsaṃsthāt bahiḥsthitāt parasiktād anyābhiṣiktād apīṭhagāt apīṭhasthādapyadhigantavyam||
children.translated_text:
Commentary:
[From one consecrated by himself] — from a teacher consecrated by oneself, at the <s>yogapīṭha</s>, the distinguished support of worship of god, teacher, and scripture, characterized by what is taught in the glorious <s>Kiraṇāgama</s> and others — [one honored by Śaṃkara should learn] — one who has worshipped the Supreme Lord should learn. But if, while staying outside, wandering in other regions, one wishes to learn texts, then one may learn from one staying outside — from one consecrated by another, even from one not occupying the seat.

children.text: NOTE reference to yogapīṭhalakṣaṇa in Kiraṇa,
which may be a reference to the description in \Kir\ 31

children.translated_text: Injunctions for the Teacher
He should not go without footwear,
nor anywhere without a companion,
not too early, nor too late in the day,
not at night, nor in fierce sunlight.
Commentary:

children.text: upānadgrahaṇaṃ pādukādyupalakṣaṇam| [anupānatkaḥ] nagnapādaḥ [asahāyavān] ekākī [nātiprāk] aprabhāte [ativelāyāṃ] sāyaṃ [rātrau] niśāyāṃ [kharātape] tīvrātape vā na gururgacchet||
children.translated_text: The mention of footwear is indicative of wooden sandals and the like. [Without footwear] means barefoot. [Without a companion] means alone. [Not too early] means before dawn. [Too late] means in the evening. [At night] means during the night. [In fierce sunlight] means in intense heat — the teacher should not go [at such times].
He should not associate with lowly persons, nor
should he wander aimlessly from house to house.
Likewise, he should not ridicule anyone,
nor mock, nor torment [anyone].
Commentary:
He should not associate with lowly persons

children.text:
na nikṛṣṭairjanaiḥ sahavāsaṃ kuryāt| vṛthā [gṛhādgṛhamapi gṛhād gṛhāntaraṃ ca [na yāyāt] na paryaṭet|
[kaṃcinnopahased nānukuryāt] na ca kasyāpyupahāsamanukaraṇaṃ ca kuryāt| [na kaṃcit pīḍayet] na ca kaṃcinmarmodghāṭanadehatāḍanadhanāpaharaṇairhiṃsyāt||
children.translated_text:
— he should not cohabit with base people. He should not wander aimlessly from house to house — he should not roam about.
[He should not ridicule or mock anyone] — he should neither ridicule nor imitate anyone. [He should not torment anyone] — he should not harm anyone by exposing vulnerabilities, striking the body, or seizing property.
He should not practice any conduct
practiced by the wicked, for that teacher —
if such conduct leads to loss of respect,
it cannot be prevented [from spreading] among the <s>mantrins</s> and others.

children.text: Brunner has followed the reading of 2 IFP transcripts

children.translated_text: Commentary:
Bad conduct

children.text:
asadbhirācaritaṃ na kiṃcidācaret| [yataḥ sa guruḥ] yasmātsarveṣu sādhakaputrakasamayiṣvasyaiva garīyastvam|
[tadāpannam amānyatvam] ācārye 'pūjyatvamāpādyamānaṃ [mantryādiṣu na vāryate] tatsādhakādiṣu durnivāram|
tadanugṛhītānāmapyeṣāṃ tattatpadāvāpteḥ||
children.translated_text:
— conduct practiced by the wicked should not be practiced at all. [For that teacher] — because among all <s>sādhakas</s>, <s>putrakas</s>, and <s>samayīs</s>, his alone is the preeminence.
[The resulting loss of respect] — the dishonor that would befall the teacher [cannot be prevented among the mantrins and others] — it is impossible to prevent among those <s>sādhakas</s> and others.
Because even those who have been graced by him would [lose respect] upon attaining their respective stations.
Conduct of the Putraka and Samayī
Having thus described the conduct of the teacher, he now speaks to describe [the conduct] of the <s>putraka</s> and <s>samayī</s> —
The <s>putraka</s>, rising at dawn,
and the <s>samayī</s>, having completed the daily rites,
having made obeisance, and permitted
by the teacher, should perform [his] duties.
Commentary:

children.text: putrakaḥ samayī ca [prātaḥ] brāhme muhūrte utthāya kṛtāhnikaḥ kṛtapraṇāmo [guruṇā anujñātaḥ] gurvanujñātaḥ [kṛtyam] karaṇīyam [ācaret] kuryāt||
children.translated_text: The <s>putraka</s> and the <s>samayī</s>, rising at dawn, at the <s>brāhma muhūrta</s> (the hour of Brahmā), having completed the daily rites and made obeisance, [permitted by the teacher] — with the teacher's permission — should perform what is to be done.
Rules for Hearing Scripture
What is that duty? He says —
Having studied, one should hear the scripture,
dwelling with the teacher, devoted to the teacher,
having abandoned pride, jealousy,
and the succession of ostentation and vice.
Commentary:

children.text: samayinā putrakeṇa [śāstramadhītya] śāstrapāṭhānantaraṃ [gurau vasan gurutantraḥ] gurugṛhādhivāsinā tatpāratantryeṇa ca [abhimānamātsaryaḍambhasantatim] abhimānam ahaṃkāraṃ mātsaryaṃ dveṣaṃ ḍambhaṃ kṛtrimaṃ vyasanasantatiṃ kleśahelāparamparāṃ tyaktvā vihāya [śṛṇuyāt] tacchravaṇaṃ kāryam||
children.translated_text: By the <s>samayī</s> or <s>putraka</s> — [having studied the scripture] — after the recitation of the scripture, [dwelling with the teacher, devoted to the teacher] — one who resides in the teacher's house, with dependence upon him, [having abandoned pride, jealousy, ostentation, and the succession of vice] — having abandoned pride, the sense of 'I,' jealousy, hatred, ostentation, artificiality, and the succession of vice — the chain of affliction and carelessness — having abandoned [all these], [one should hear] — the hearing of that [scripture] should be performed.
Things to be Avoided in the Teacher's Presence
Wrapping the throat, spitting,
coughing, laughing, and the like — in the presence
of the teacher one should not do; nor should one debate
with anyone, nor wear ostentatious attire.
Anointing the body, bodily adornment,
yawning, remaining seated,
familiar conversation, sitting cross-legged,
meditation, worship, and the like —
Commentary:

children.text:
uttarīyaiḥ kaṇṭhaveṣṭanaṃ kaṇṭhaprāvṛtiḥ| niṣṭhīvo mukhapānīyanirasanam| kāsahāsau prasiddhau| ādigrahaṇād aślīlabhāṣaṇakrīḍādi guroḥ sannidhau na kuryāt|
[kaiścid no vādaṃ kuryāt] na ca kenacitsaha vivadet| na ca sannihite gurau [utkṛṣṭaveṣavā] utkṛṣṭaveṣaḥ syāt| udvaranādikaṃ na kuryādityabhisambadhyate| tatra udvartanaṃ prasiddham|
aṅgasaṃskāraḥ snānodvapanasamālambhanādi| jṛmbhaṇaṃ vidāritāsyagātravinamanam| āsanasaṃsthitiḥ āsane 'vasthānam| samānālāpaḥ sāmyenāpihitavaktrasyānamrasya saṃkathanam|
etacca paryaṅgabandhadhyānādi ca na kuryāt| ādigrahaṇād anyasyāpyavinayasya lokaprasiddhasya niṣedhaḥ||
[gurau vartanam]
children.translated_text:
Wrapping the throat means covering the neck with upper garments. Spitting means expelling water from the mouth. Coughing and laughing are well known. By the word 'and the like,' obscene speech, play, and such things should not be done in the teacher's presence.
[One should not debate with anyone] — one should not argue with anyone. Nor, when the teacher is present, should one be [ostentatiously attired] — wearing fine clothes. Anointing and the rest should not be done — this is to be connected. There, anointing is well known.
Bodily adornment means bathing, sprinkling, anointing, and the like. Yawning means opening the mouth with the body bending. Remaining seated means staying on a seat. Familiar conversation means speaking with covered mouth and bowed head on equal terms.
These, and sitting cross-legged, meditation, and so forth should not be done. By the word 'and the like,' any other disrespectful [behavior] well known in the world is prohibited.
One who is wise should not salute [the teacher]
when he is eating, in meditation,
walking about, engaged in ritual work,
or standing near [his own] teacher.
Commentary:
When eating, in meditation, walking about

children.text: bhojanasamādhānacaṅkramaṇavyagramācāryaṃ [kriyodyataṃ] kāryeṣvāsaktaṃ [gurusamīpe sthitam] gurusaṃnikarṣasthaṃ ca [matimān] prājño nābhivādayet||
children.translated_text: — when the teacher is occupied with eating, meditation, or walking, [when engaged in ritual work] — when occupied with duties, [when standing near the teacher] — when standing in the proximity of [his own] teacher — a wise person should not salute [him at such times].
When [the teacher] walks, one should follow behind;
when he enters, one should enter after him.
One should not question his words;
one should not awaken him when he sleeps.
Permitted [by the teacher], one should go for alms;
having obtained [food], one should report and then eat.
One should sleep when he has slept, and so forth —
one should do whatever is enjoined by the rules.
Commentary:
When walking

children.text:
vrajantaṃ gurum [pṛṣṭhato yāyād] anuvrajet| viśantaṃ [anusaṃviśed] anupraviśet| [tadvaco nānuyuñjīta] tadājñāparyanuyogaṃ na kuryāt| na cainaṃ [śayānaṃ] suptaṃ prabodhayet|
[anujñātaḥ] tadājñayā bhaikṣaṃ caret| [prāptam] āhṛtya [niveditaṃ] tasmai nivedya tadājñayaiva adyāt|
tasmiṃśca supte [śayīta] supyāt| [yacca] ityevamādyanyadapi [vidhyuditaṃ] sāmānyaśāstravihitaṃ karaṇīyaṃ [kuryād] anutiṣṭhet||
children.translated_text:
— when the teacher is going, [one should follow behind] — one should follow. When he enters, [one should enter after] — one should follow in. [One should not question his words] — one should not dispute his commands. Nor should one awaken him [when sleeping] — when he is asleep.
[Permitted] — by his command, one should go for alms. [Having obtained] — having brought [food back], [having reported] — having informed him, by his command alone one should eat.
And when he has slept, [one should sleep]. [And whatever else] and other things also [enjoined by the rules] — whatever is prescribed by the general scriptures as duty, [one should do] — one should observe.
Special Conduct of the Putraka and Samayī

children.text: itthaṃ samayinaḥ putrakasya ca sādhāraṇacaryopadeśaḥ kṛtaḥ| iyāṃsu viśeṣaḥ| yaduta---
children.translated_text: Thus the common instruction of conduct for the <s>samayī</s> and the <s>putraka</s> has been stated. The distinction [between them] is as follows —
The <s>putraka</s>, when permitted, may wander at will,
or may reside in the abode.
The <s>samayī</s>, as described before, and the householder
should serve the teacher with effort.
Commentary:

children.text: putrako dhāmni vased, anujñātaḥ kāmaṃ caredvā
children.translated_text: The putraka may reside in the abode; permitted, he may wander at will

children.text:
putrakasya gurugṛhanivasanaṃ tadājñayā deśāntarāṭanamiti kāmacāraḥ|
[samayī prāggṛhasthaśca yatnena gurumupacaret] samayinaḥ prāguktasya prāggṛhasthasya ca yatnato guruparicaryādyabhijñā||
children.translated_text:
— for the <s>putraka</s>, there is dwelling in the teacher's house, or, by the teacher's permission, wandering to other regions — this is his freedom of movement.
[The samayī as described before and the householder should serve the teacher with effort] — the <s>samayī</s> described earlier and the householder should assiduously apply themselves to serving the teacher and the like.
Why? He says —
Because the goal to be accomplished has not been attained,
and even its attainment depends on that [teacher].
And for one devoted to other occupations
[there is no attainment]; therefore, one should be a servant of that [teacher].
Commentary:
Of the goal

children.text: sādhyasyābhipretasya koṭeḥ sampatteḥ alabdhatvāt [tallābho 'pi tadāśrayaḥ] tallābhasya ca gurvāśrayatvāt samayinaḥ prāggṛhasthasya ca gurūpasadanamavaśyaṃ kāryam| yasmād anyavṛttiniṣṭhasya sato [na ca] na tallābhaḥ| tasmāt [tatsādhako bhavet] ācāryaparicaryāsādhanaparau syātām||
children.translated_text: — because the culmination of what is desired has not been attained, [and even its attainment depends on that (teacher)] — because the attainment of that also depends on the teacher, the <s>samayī</s> and the householder must necessarily approach the teacher. Since for one devoted to other occupations [there is no attainment of that]; therefore [one should be a servant of that (teacher)] — both should be devoted to serving the teacher.
Conduct of the Sādhaka
Now, the conduct of the <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner) —
The <s>sādhaka</s>, permitted by the teacher,
having resorted to a sacred site (<s>puṇyakṣetra</s>),
wearing the guise of the deity to be propitiated, silent,
subsisting on oblation-food (<s>haviṣya</s>), sacrificial porridge (<s>caru</s>), or vegetables —
accompanied [by companions], vigilant,
or subsisting on fruits and roots alone,
having worshipped <s>Śiva</s>, he should worship the deity to be propitiated,
and should perform <s>japa</s> (repetition) as taught in three ways.
Having offered a tenth part as oblation, [and completing] the sacrificial
concluding bath (<s>kumbhasnāna</s>), on an auspicious day,
stationed at the [sacred] site, he should commence the rite,
or, while wandering, [should pursue] the attainment of <s>siddhi</s>.
Commentary:

children.text:
vakṣyamāṇavanniyatakṣetraṃ parigṛhya tiṣṭhato vividhasiddhikṣetracāriṇo vā sādhakasya sādhāraṇī ceyaṃ caryā|
yad [gurvanujñātaḥ] guroḥ prāptānujñaḥ [puṇyakṣetraṃ samāśritaḥ]
pavitrasthānasthitaḥ [sādhyaveṣadharaḥ] sādhyadevatāviśeṣaveṣadhārī [maunī] saṃyatavāg [haviṣyacaruśākabhuk] haviṣyeṇa ghṛtakṣīrayavādinā caruṇā vā mantritena pāyasena śākena vā kṛtavṛttiḥ [phalamūlabhugeva vā] phalamūlāśī vā [sahāyavān] sasahāyaḥ [apramattaḥ] tyaktapramādaḥ [śivamiṣṭvā] śivamabhyarcya [sādhyaṃ yajet] sādhyamantraṃ pūjāprakaraṇoktavadyajet| japaṃ ca---
children.translated_text:
This is the common conduct of the <s>sādhaka</s>, whether stationed at a designated site or wandering through various <s>siddhi</s>-sites.
Namely, [permitted by the teacher] — having obtained the teacher's permission, [having resorted to a sacred site] —
stationed at a holy place, [wearing the guise of the deity to be propitiated] — wearing the distinctive appearance of the particular deity to be propitiated, [silent] — with speech restrained, [subsisting on oblation-food, sacrificial porridge, or vegetables] — sustaining oneself with <s>haviṣya</s> (ghee, milk, barley, etc.), or with <s>caru</s> (consecrated rice-porridge), or with vegetables, [or subsisting on fruits and roots alone], [accompanied] — with companions, [vigilant] — having abandoned heedlessness, [having worshipped Śiva] — having worshipped <s>Śiva</s>, [he should worship the deity-mantra] — he should worship the <s>mantra</s> to be propitiated as described in the section on worship. And regarding <s>japa</s> —

'For minor <s>siddhis</s>, the <s>japa</s> should be performed audibly (<s>bhāṣya</s>), consisting of [the recitation] for another's benefit.
For middling <s>siddhis</s> and above, [it should be] whispered (<s>upāṃśu</s>)' —

children.text: iti śrīmatparākhyādāvuktatvādvaśīkaraṇavidveṣādyadhamasiddhyapekṣayā bhāṣyarūpaṃ khaḍgāñjanādi madhyamasiddhyānuguṇyenopāṃśusaṃjñaṃ cakravartitvādyuttamasiddhyapekṣayā ca mānasaṃ kuryāt| yadi vā---
children.translated_text: thus, as stated in the glorious <s>Parākhyāgama</s> and others, for the purpose of inferior <s>siddhis</s> such as subjugation (<s>vaśīkaraṇa</s>) and creating enmity (<s>vidveṣa</s>), the <s>japa</s> should be in audible form; for middling <s>siddhis</s> such as [obtaining] a sword (<s>khaḍga</s>) or eye-ointment (<s>añjana</s>), it should be of the type called whispered (<s>upāṃśu</s>); and for supreme <s>siddhis</s> such as universal sovereignty (<s>cakravartitva</s>), it should be mental (<s>mānasa</s>). Or alternatively —

children.text:
uttamāḥ śivamantrādyā mantreśādyāstu madhyamāḥ|
gaṇāśca rudramantrāśca bhaginyo mātarastathā|
adhamāḥ kīrtitāḥ mantrāḥ iti|
children.translated_text:
'The supreme [mantras] are <s>Śiva-mantras</s> and the like; the <s>Mantreśa</s> [mantras] and such are middling.
The <s>Gaṇa</s> [mantras], <s>Rudra-mantras</s>, the <s>Bhaginīs</s> (Sisters), and the <s>Mātṛs</s> (Mothers) —
these are declared to be inferior <s>mantras</s>.'
Likewise —

children.text:
utamānmanasā mantrānmadhyamānapyupāṃśunā|
adhamānapi mantrāṃstu bhāṣyeṇeha japedbudhaḥ||
children.translated_text:
'The supreme <s>mantras</s> one should recite mentally; the middling ones in a whisper;
and the inferior <s>mantras</s> one should recite audibly — thus [should do] the wise one.'

children.text: iti śrīmatpauṣkaroktarītyā sādhyamantrasyaiva adhamamadhyamottamatvena bhāṣyopāṃśumānasabhedena [tridhoditaṃ japaṃ kuryād] triprakāratayā japaṃ vidadhyāt|
children.translated_text: Thus, according to the method taught in the glorious <s>Pauṣkarāgama</s>, [the japa] of the deity-<s>mantra</s> itself, distinguished as inferior, middling, and supreme, with the division into audible, whispered, and mental — [the three-fold japa should be performed] — one should perform the <s>japa</s> in three modes.
'Having recited with the division into mental and the rest, at the end, with a view to <s>siddhi</s>' —

children.text: iti sādhyamantrārcanaprakaraṇe 'bhihitaṃ yataḥ| [daśāṃśaṃ hutvā] japācca daśāṃśena homaṃ kṛtvā [tadyāgakumbhasnātaḥ] tadyāgāvabhṛthasnātaḥ [śubhe dine] śubhe 'hani [kṣetrasthaḥ] niyatakṣetre [siddhisaṃśrayaṃ caranvā] kṣetrāṇi vā caran [karma prārabhet] karmārambhaṃ kuryāt||
children.translated_text: thus it is stated in the section on worship of the deity-<s>mantra</s>. [Having offered a tenth part] — having performed a fire-oblation (<s>homa</s>) of one-tenth of the <s>japa</s>, [having completed the concluding bath of that sacrifice] — having bathed at the conclusion (<s>avabhṛtha</s>) of that sacrifice, [on an auspicious day] — on a favorable day, [stationed at the site] — at the designated site, [or while wandering in pursuit of siddhi] — or wandering through [various] sites, [one should commence the rite] — one should begin the ritual work.
And he, though of the appearance of a mendicant —
should not bestow blessings upon anyone,
should not flatter, nor should he reproach;
he should not sit for long anywhere
except at the designated sacred site.
Commentary:

children.text:
bhikṣārthaṃ paryaṭan bhaikṣyalobhāt [na kaṃcidanugṛhṇīyād] āśīrvādaparo na bhavet| [na niṣeveta bhartsayed] nāpi praśaṃsāparo bhaved bhikṣāyā alābhād garhayedvā|
[vinā kṣetraparigrahād anyatra] sādhyamantrajapārthaṃ parigṛhītapavitrasthānādanyadeśe [ciraṃ nāsīta] bhikṣāṃ pratīkṣamāṇo bahukālaṃ na caret||
children.translated_text:
While wandering for alms, out of greed for alms [he should not bestow blessings upon anyone] — he should not be given to bestowing blessings. [Nor should he flatter or reproach] — nor should he be given to praising, nor should he reproach [anyone] upon not receiving alms.
[Except at the designated sacred site, elsewhere] — at a place other than the holy site taken up for the <s>japa</s> of the deity-<s>mantra</s>, [he should not sit for long] — while awaiting alms, he should not linger for a long time.
He should practice the <s>mādhūkarī</s> mode of begging,
for the day's sustenance, when the <s>savana</s> (pressing/offering time) has passed,
[reciting] the principal <s>mantra</s>, at an auspicious
[time], with the Supreme Lord as the presiding deity.
Commentary:
At the face of all mantras

children.text: sarveṣāṃ mantrāṇāṃ yanmukhamiva mukhaṃ sannidhisthānaṃ tasmin [puṇye] pāvane [parameśādhidaivate] śivadaivate [dinārthe] mādhyāhnikākhe savane [gate] nirvartite mādhūkarīm aniyatāṃ bhikṣāṃ caret| tathoktaṃ śrīmatpauṣkare---
children.translated_text: — at what is like the face, i.e. the station of proximity, of all <s>mantras</s>; [at the sacred] — purifying; [presided over by <s>Parameśa</s> (the Supreme Lord)] — whose deity is <s>Śiva</s>; [when the day-rite] — when the <s>savana</s> (pressing/oblation) known as the midday rite [is completed] — one should go begging for <s>mādhūkarī</s> (bee-like alms, collected from house to house). As stated in the holy <s>Pauṣkara</s>:

children.text: gṛhādgṛhaṃ paryaṭato bhaikṣaṃ mādhūkaraṃ smṛtam|| iti||
children.translated_text: 'Wandering from house to house — that begging is known as <s>mādhūkara</s> (bee-like).'
One who eats without completing
the <s>savana</s> (oblation) honored by the gods —
the <s>mantras</s> do not abide in him,
[even though they are] established on the <s>yogapīṭha</s> (yoga-seat).
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):

children.text:
tat [sūrapūjitaṃ] sarvāmarārcitaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ tadānīṃ mantrajapadevatārcanāgnihavanādi [anirvartya] avidhāya yo [aśnāti] bhuṅkte taṃ [yogapīṭhavyavasthitā mantrāḥ] yogapīṭha āvāhitamantrā nādhitiṣṭhanti nainamīpsitaphalena yojayantīti yāvat|
yogapīṭhaṃ nāmārcādhāraḥ saṃhitāntaroktalakṣaṇaḥ| tathā ca pauṣkare---
children.translated_text: That midday <s>savana</s>, [honored by the gods] — worshipped by all the gods; without completing the <s>mantra</s>-recitation, deity-worship, fire-oblation, and the like at that time — one who eats — the <s>mantras</s> established on the <s>yogapīṭha</s> — the <s>mantras</s> invoked on the <s>yogapīṭha</s> — do not abide in him, that is, they do not bestow the desired fruit upon him. The <s>yogapīṭha</s> is the base of worship, whose characteristics are stated elsewhere in the <s>Saṃhitā</s>. As also in the <s>Pauṣkara</s>:

children.text:
pīṭhaṃ teṣāṃ tu mantrāṇāṃ kāryaṃ padmāṅkitodaram|
śrīparṇikādidārūtthāṃ vṛttaṃ tu śubhalakṣaṇam|| iti||
children.translated_text: 'A seat should be made for those <s>mantras</s>, with a lotus-marked interior, made from <s>śrīparṇikā</s> and other woods, round, and of auspicious marks.'
While going about for alms,
one should not accept alms from a condemned [person],
nor from a <s>Śaiva</s> of the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> [sect],
nor from any <s>liṅgin</s> (wearer of insignia);
one should not accept alms rich in delicacies,
nor overly elaborate [food];
nor from where women skilled
in jest, flirtation, and the like [are present].
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):

children.text:
bhikṣāṃ [bhikṣāṃ carataḥ] bhikṣācarād [nādadyāt] na gṛhṇīyāt|
na ca śaivād vigarhitāt kṣudrācārāt| na ca [svāyambhuvādeḥ] svayaṃbhūpāsanopajīvinaḥ| ādigrahaṇānnānyasmādapi liṅgopajīvinaḥ pūjakādeśca| na ca [liṅginaḥ] mahāvrataśākyādicihnabhṛtaḥ sakāśād bhikṣāmādadīta|
[miṣṭānnapracurāṃ] svādvannabhūyiṣṭhām| [atisaṃskṛtām] atisaṃskārapuraḥsarām| parihāsakrīḍālāpapraṇayakuśalāśca yatra [nāryaḥ] yoṣitaḥ tato gṛhād bhikṣāṃ [nādadyād] nādadīteti pūrveṇa sambandhaḥ||
children.translated_text: While going about for alms — from the alms-round — one should not accept. Not from a condemned <s>Śaiva</s>, i.e. one of base conduct. Nor from one who lives by the worship of <s>Svayambhū</s>; by the word 'and the rest' (<s>ādi</s>), not from any other person who lives by [worshipping] a <s>liṅga</s>, or from a professional worshipper. Nor should one accept alms from a <s>liṅgin</s> — one bearing the insignia of the <s>Mahāvrata</s>, <s>Śākya</s> (Buddhist), and the like. [Rich in delicacies] — predominantly of savory foods. [Overly elaborate] — preceded by excessive preparation. And from a house where women skilled in jest, play, conversation, and coquetry are present — one should not accept alms — this connects with the previous [statement].
Having performed protective rites, remembering the weapon [-mantra],
one should wander about, observing silence;
not having obtained alms, one should not become angry,
nor should one remain detained for long.
Nor [should one react] when [people are] running on the roads,
nor when spoken to unpleasantly by someone.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
Observing silence

children.text:
saṃyatavāk sakalīkaraṇādinā kṛtarakṣaḥ [astraṃ smaran] astramantraṃ japan bhikṣāṃ paryaṭet| tāṃ ca alabdhvā tadarthaṃ vā ciraṃ vidhṛtaḥ san [no kopaṃ kuryāt] na kupyeta| na ca [adhvasu] mārgeṣu [pradhāvatsu] ye pradhāvanto janāḥ satsu teṣvanyeṣu ca|
[kenacid apriyam uktaḥ] apriyavādiṣu na kopaṃ kuryāt||
children.translated_text: — with restrained speech, having performed protective rites by means of <s>sakalīkaraṇa</s> (sanctification) and the like, [remembering the weapon-mantra] — reciting the weapon-<s>mantra</s>, one should wander about for alms. And not having obtained it, or having been detained for long for that purpose, [one should not become angry] — one should not get angry. Nor [should one react] when [people are] running on the roads — when there are people running and others [around]. [When spoken to unpleasantly by someone] — one should not get angry toward those who speak unpleasant words.
A portion for the <s>guru</s>, <s>Agni</s> (fire), <s>Śiva</s>, the <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge-deity),
and for the <s>Kṣetrapāla</s> (field-guardian),
having set aside and divided with one's companion,
one should eat, pure, [seated] on the ground.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
For the <s>guru</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, and the <s>Vidyā</s>; and for the <s>Kṣetrapāla</s>

children.text: gurvādibhyo [aṃśakaṃ samuddhṛtya] bhāgamuddhṛtya [sahāyena] `ātmārthabhāgamavasthāpya śiṣṭaṃ mahyaṃ sthāpayet' ityevamanuśāsitena sadyo vibhajya kṛtatattadvidhiḥ [kṣitau] bhūmau sthāpitapātraḥ [śuciḥ] samāhitaḥ san [adyād] bhuñjīta||
children.translated_text: — having set aside a portion for the <s>guru</s> and the others; [with one's companion] — 'having set aside one's own portion, let the rest be kept for me' — thus instructed, having divided at once and having performed the respective rites; [on the ground] — with the vessel placed on the ground; [pure] — being composed, one should eat.
Having rinsed the mouth, one should recite the <s>mantra</s>;
then at the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> time-period (evening),
when it has passed, one should give to the <s>Kṣetrapāla</s>
an offering preceded by <s>Oṃ</s> and <s>Svāhā</s>,
and a <s>bali</s> (offering) in the southwest direction,
accompanied by fragrance and incense.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
Having rinsed the mouth

children.text:
samyagācāntaḥ [mantraṃ] sādhyamantraṃ japan vaiṣṇave samaye sāyaṃsamaya āsīta|
[tato vyatīte] tasmiṃścātikrānte kṣetrapālāya svāheti [nairṛte] nirṛtidigbhāge baliṃ [gandhadhūpapuraḥsaraṃ] vilepanadhūpasrakpradhānaṃ dadyāt||
children.translated_text: — having properly rinsed the mouth; [reciting the <s>mantra</s>] — reciting the <s>mantra</s> being practiced, one should sit at the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> time-period, i.e. the evening time. [Then, when it has passed] — and when that has elapsed, one should give to the <s>Kṣetrapāla</s> a <s>bali</s> [with] <s>Svāhā</s>; [in the southwest direction] — in the quarter of <s>Nirṛti</s>; [accompanied by fragrance and incense] — principally with ointment, incense, and garlands.
Then, spreading out the [antelope] skin,
having assumed a [meditation] posture, untired,
the learned one should meditate and recite the <s>mantra</s>;
when weary, one should sleep lightly on that [skin].
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
Then

children.text:
paścāt [saccarma prasārya] mṛgājinamāstīrya [āsanam] ardhacandrapadmasvastikādyāsanaṃ baddhvā vidvān iti yogapādapradarśitadhyānādividhijño 'nalasaḥ san [mantraṃ dhyāyan japet] tattanmantrajapadhyānaṃ kuryāt|
[khinnaḥ] śrāntaśca tasmin tatra śayane [laghu] stokaṃ [svapet] śayīta||
children.translated_text: — afterward; [spreading out the skin] — spreading out the antelope skin; [a posture] — assuming a posture such as <s>ardhacandrā</s>, <s>padma</s>, <s>svastika</s>, and the like; the learned one — one who knows the method of meditation and the like as shown in the <s>Yogapāda</s> — being diligent; [meditating on and reciting the <s>mantra</s>] — one should perform the meditation and recitation of the respective <s>mantras</s>. [Weary] — and when fatigued, on that very sleeping-mat, one should sleep [lightly] — briefly.
Having risen at midnight,
one should perform worship, recitation, and the like.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):

children.text: ardharātre samutthāya iti samyag dakṣiṇapārśvena parameśvarasmaraṇapūrvakaṃ śayanādutthāya [pūjājapādikaṃ] japārcanādi kuryāt||
children.translated_text: Having risen at midnight — properly, lying on the right side, with the remembrance of <s>Parameśvara</s>, having risen from sleep — one should perform recitation, worship, and the like.
Then, at the <s>Brāhma</s> time-period (dawn),
one should fetch fuel-sticks and the like; then,
<s>Śaivas</s> who have arrived at one's dwelling —
one should worship them with supreme faith,
with well-furnished implements,
having ascertained them by their marks, as befitting.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
Then

children.text: paścād brāhme ca savane prabhāte [samidādi] samitkuśakusumāni āharet| tataśca [āvasathaprāptān] svāvasathaprāptān śaivān [liṅgaiḥ tāṃśca jñātvā] viśiṣṭaiścihnairācāryasādhakādīn brahmacārigṛhasthādīn brāhmaṇakṣatriyādīṃśca buddhvā [yathārhataḥ sampannaiḥ kārakaiḥ] yathocitāmatropakaraṇādisampattyā [parayā śraddhayā] utkṛṣṭayā bhaktyā [arcayet] sammānayet|
children.translated_text: — afterward, at the <s>Brāhma</s> time-period, i.e. at dawn, one should fetch fuel-sticks, <s>kuśa</s> grass, and flowers. And then, <s>Śaivas</s> who have arrived at one's own dwelling — having ascertained them by their distinctive marks — teachers, practitioners, celibates, householders, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, and the like — with appropriate provisions of food, implements, and the like — with supreme faith, i.e. excellent devotion — one should honor them.

children.text: Note here that amatra is a water-pot
liṅgāni cātra vratajātyādicihnāni vratiniyatapavitrakalājapamudrāpradarśanādīni śrīmatkāmikapauṣkarakiraṇādyāgamāmnātānīha na pradarśitāni granthavistaramātanvatīti tata eva jñeyāni||
children.translated_text: And here the marks are the insignia of vow, birth-class, and the like — [such as] the <s>vrata</s>-insignia, the fixed sacred mark, the <s>kalā</s>, the <s>japa</s>, the <s>mudrā</s>-display, and the like, as taught in the holy <s>Kāmika</s>, <s>Pauṣkara</s>, <s>Kiraṇa</s>, and other <s>Āgamas</s> — these are not displayed here so as not to extend the length of the text; they should be known from those [sources] themselves.

children.text: N.B. reference to Kāmika (!), Pauṣkara, and Kiraṇa
Note that Brunner diagnoses the text here to be partly corrupt (she
places a question mark after kalā, for instance); furthermore,
she finds no instructions in the South Indian Kāmika or Pauṣkara, but
for the Kiraṇa she refers to \Kir\ \CP\ 1 (for samayin and putraka),

children.translated_text: One should not bow to anyone [other than one's <s>guru</s>]; one should not tell
the <s>mantra</s> being practiced to anyone;
one should not disparage medicinal herbs, <s>mantras</s>,
cows, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and ascetics.
For these are the places of manifestation of <s>Śiva</s>;
since disparaging them is indeed disparaging <s>Śiva</s>.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
One should not bow to anyone

children.text:
guruvanna kaṃcinnamet| sādhyamantraṃ na [kasyacid brūyāt] prakāśayet| [oṣadhīḥ] oṣadhyādīn garhāṃ kurvan nākṣipet|
[yataḥ] yasmāt [śivasya] parameśvarasya ete [vyaktisthānaṃ] vyaktisthānāni| eṣu vyaktaḥ śivabhaṭṭārakastattatphalado bhavati| [sā] tannindā śivanindaiva iti garhaṇayā na tānākṣipet|
children.translated_text: — like the <s>guru</s>, one should not bow to anyone. The <s>mantra</s> being practiced should not be revealed to anyone. One should not disparage, i.e. censure, medicinal herbs and the like. Because these — medicinal herbs, <s>mantras</s>, cows, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and ascetics — are the places of manifestation of <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord). <s>Śiva Bhaṭṭāraka</s> manifests through them and bestows the respective fruits. That [their] censure is indeed the censure of <s>Śiva</s> — therefore one should not disparage them.
With distinguished offerings,
one should worship <s>Śaṅkara</s> on the <s>parvan</s> (juncture) days.
One should also [worship] the <s>Kṣetrapāla</s> and the <s>sādhya</s> soul (<s>aṇu</s>);
one should not give the <s>caru</s> (ritual oblation-food) to anyone;
having obtained permission, one should never
remain idle even for a single moment.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):

children.text:
parvasu aṣṭamīcaturdaśyādiṣu [viśiṣṭenopahāreṇa] saviśeṣeṇa balyādyupahāreṇa [śaṅkaraṃ] parameśvaraṃ [sādhyāṇuṃ] sādhyamantraṃ kṣetrapālaṃ ca [yajed] arcayet| sādhyamantrasaṃskṛtaniveditaṃ caruṃ na [kasyacid] anyasmai dadyāt|
kiṃ ca [labdhānujñaḥ] he bhagavan idamahaṃ karomi, anujānīhi māmiti prārthyājñāṃ labdhvā [mṛṣā] tāṃ tāmakurvan [jātu] yadā kadācit [ekamapi kṣaṇaṃ] kṣaṇamapi [na tiṣṭhet] nāsīta||
children.translated_text: On <s>parvan</s> days — the eighth, fourteenth, and the like — with distinguished offerings, i.e. with special <s>bali</s>-offerings and the like — one should worship <s>Parameśvara</s>, the <s>sādhya</s>-<s>mantra</s>, and the <s>Kṣetrapāla</s>. The <s>caru</s> consecrated and offered by the <s>sādhya</s>-<s>mantra</s> should not be given to anyone else. Furthermore, having obtained permission — 'O Lord, I shall do this; please grant me permission' — having prayed and obtained the command — one who fails to act [accordingly] should not remain idle even for a moment, at any time.
Rules for one wandering through <s>siddhi</s>-sites (<s>siddhikṣetra</s>)
Now he briefly states the specific [rules] for one wandering through <s>siddhi</s>-sites:
With concealed rosary and worship-accessories,
knowing the division of times for rites,
one gradually attains <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment)
while wandering through <s>siddhi</s>-sites.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
With concealed rosary and worship-accessories

children.text:
aprakāśitākṣasūtrapūjopakaraṇaḥ [kriyākālavibhāgavit] kriyākālavibhāgajñaśca [siddhikṣetrāṇi saṃcaran] siddhikṣetracārī sādhakaḥ [kramaśaḥ] kramāt siddhim [āpnoti] labhate|
yadyapi caitatsthāsnorapi sādhāraṇaviśeṣaṇaṃ, tathāpyasya pratyahaṃ deśāntarāṭane sati saviśeṣaṃ kriyākālajñatvam arcāliṅgākṣasūtrādiguptiśca sutarām upayogītyetadadhikaraṇe iyamuktiḥ||
children.translated_text: — with rosary and worship-implements not displayed; [knowing the division of times for rites] — knowing the division of times for rites; the <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner) wandering through <s>siddhi</s>-sites gradually attains <s>siddhi</s>. Although this qualification is common even to one who stays in one place, nevertheless, for one who daily travels to different regions, knowledge of the division of times for rites and the concealment of worship-<s>liṅga</s>, rosary, and the like is especially useful — hence this statement in this context.
Method of taking possession of a sacred site (<s>kṣetraparigraha</s>)
For the purpose of taking possession of a site, he says:
Or, having taken possession of a site
with a good <s>liṅga</s> and a qualified [guardian], one should dwell there.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
Or, with a good <s>liṅga</s> and qualified guardian
— or, having taken possession of a site sheltered by an excellent <s>liṅga</s> free from defects such as burning, breaking, cracking, and the like, one should dwell there.
And in that case —
[A site] occupied by <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, <s>Vṛṣabha</s> (the Bull), <s>Skanda</s>,
<s>Mātṛs</s> (Mothers), and <s>Lokeśas</s> (World-lords),
with doors to the south and north,
a <s>Śiva</s>-abode guarded by another,
crowded with many people, with fuel-sticks,
flowers, <s>kuśa</s> grass, and water far away,
and one with disturbances — abandoning [such sites],
one should take possession [of a suitable one].

children.text:
Vṛtti:
tataśca kṣetre parameśvarapratiṣṭhānāt pūrvakaṃ [gaṇeśavṛṣabhaskandamātṛlokeśakīlitaṃ] gaṇeśādyākrāntaṃ [dakṣiṇottaradigdvāraṃ] yāmyodaggatadvāraṃ śivadhāma [anyarakṣitam] anyasya sādhakasya rakṣitaṃ [mahājanākulaṃ] bahulokākīrṇaṃ [dūrasamitpuṣpakuśodakaṃ] viprakṛṣṭakuśakusumasamijjalaṃ [sopadravaṃ ca] hiṃsraprāṇicorādyupadravayutaṃ ca [saṃtyajya] tyaktvā [parigrahaṇamācared] etaddoṣarahitaṃ gṛhṇīyāt||
children.translated_text: Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>): And then, at the site, prior to the installation of <s>Parameśvara</s>, [one occupied by <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, <s>Vṛṣabha</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Mātṛs</s>, and <s>Lokeśas</s>] — one occupied by <s>Gaṇeśa</s> and the rest; [with doors to the south and north] — with doorways facing south and north; a <s>Śiva</s>-abode [guarded by another] — guarded by another practitioner; [crowded with many people] — thronged with many people; [with fuel-sticks, flowers, <s>kuśa</s> grass, and water far away] — where <s>kuśa</s> grass, flowers, fuel-sticks, and water are distant; [and with disturbances] — having disturbances from dangerous animals, thieves, and the like — [abandoning] — having abandoned [such sites]; [one should take possession] — one should take one free from these defects.
At a <s>Bāṇa</s>-<s>liṅga</s>, a self-manifested [<s>liṅga</s>],
[a site] frequented by sages and <s>Siddhas</s>,
by the method prescribed in one's own <s>kalpa</s> (manual),
or at one [personally] established,
on the fourteenth of the bright fortnight,
especially during the northern solstice (<s>uttarāyaṇa</s>),
the learned one should take possession, being composed,
or on the eighth.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
At a <s>Bāṇa</s>-<s>liṅga</s>

children.text: tripurīnarmadāpravāhādiparigṛhīte [svayaṃ vyakte] svayaṃbhūsthāne, tathā [munisiddhaniṣevite] munisiddhaparyupāsite [svakalpoktena vidhinā] svaśāstroktakrameṇa [svayaṃ vā parikalpite] svayaṃ vā vakṣyamāṇavatpratiṣṭhāpite|
children.translated_text: — one found in the currents of <s>Tripurī</s>, <s>Narmadā</s>, and the like; [self-manifested] — at a <s>Svayambhū</s> site; likewise [frequented by sages and <s>Siddhas</s>] — attended by sages and <s>Siddhas</s>; [by the method prescribed in one's own <s>kalpa</s>] — by the procedure stated in one's own scripture; [or at one personally established] — or at one installed by oneself as will be described.

children.text: This vakṣyamāṇavat indicates that there must have been something in the
text about liṅgapratiṣṭhāpana, perhaps attached to the fragment about
liṅgas given as an appendix that Bhatt holds to be from a later part of
the \CP. [Brunner says the same in her note 1985:393, n.3]
liṅga iti lakṣaṇayā rudrāśayasthānoktiḥ| eṣu sthāneṣu śuklapakṣacaturdaśyāmaṣṭamyāmuttarāyaṇakāle samāhitaḥ samāhitamatiḥ san tatkramajñaḥ kṣetraparigrahaṃ kuryāt||
children.translated_text: The word '<s>liṅga</s>' by extension indicates a <s>Rudrāśaya</s> (Rudra-site). At these sites, on the fourteenth of the bright fortnight or on the eighth, at the time of the northern solstice, being composed — with a collected mind, being one who knows the proper procedure — one should perform the taking possession of the site.
Having prepared the place of sacrifice, first,
one should worship the <s>Māheśvara</s> (belonging to the Great Lord) weapon [-<s>mantra</s>];
having recited ten thousand [times],
one should perform the <s>homa</s> (oblation) with one-tenth [of that].
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
First

children.text: prathamaṃ yāgadhāma [vidhāya] kṛtvā tatra vighopaśamanāya [māheśvaram astraṃ yajet] pārameśvaramastramiṣṭvā [daśasahasrāṇi japtvā] daśasahasrasaṃkhyayā taṃ japan [daśāṃśam anuhomayet] taddaśāṃśena ca homaṃ kuryāt||
children.translated_text: — initially, having prepared the place of sacrifice, for the pacification of obstacles, [one should worship the <s>Māheśvara</s> weapon] — having worshipped the weapon-[<s>mantra</s>] of <s>Parameśvara</s>; [having recited ten thousand] — having recited it ten thousand times; [one should perform the <s>homa</s> with one-tenth] — one should perform the oblation with one-tenth of that [number].
With abundant garlands, offerings, incense, and the like —
<s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva) [is established] in the chosen <s>liṅga</s>;
one should place the direction-guardians in the directions,
<s>Śakra</s> (Indra) and the rest, in the form of stakes;
with a thread that has become a channel (<s>nāḍī</s>),
connecting [them], one should draw on the outside
a rampart with ashes, blazing,
while reciting the <s>Māheśvara</s> weapon [-<s>mantra</s>];
within that, with all the seed [-<s>mantras</s>]
obtained from the armor [-<s>mantra</s>], reciting those,
one should make a protective armor of the rampart,
and likewise for one's own dwelling.
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
Vṛtti:

children.text:
prabhūtasraṅnaivedyadhūpagandhādibhiḥ [iṣṭaliṅgasthaśaṃkaraḥ] arcito liṅgāśrayaḥ śivo yasya tathāvidhaḥ sādhakaḥ kṣetraparigrahāya śakrādīn [digīśvarān] indrādidikpatīn [śaṅkuvigrahān] śaṅkuśarīrān [dikṣu] prācyādidikṣu nyaset|
tataśca [nāḍībhūtena] nāḍyātmanā sūtreṇa sandhāya digbandhanaṃ kuryāt| [bahiḥ] tadbāhye [dīptaṃ māheśvaramastraṃ] jvalatpārameśvamastraṃ japan [bhasmanā prākāram ālikhed] bhasmaprākāraṃ vilikhet|
[tadantaḥ] tasyāntaḥ [akhilaiḥ bījaiḥ] sarvabījaiḥ [varmālabdhaiḥ] kavacādyabhimantritaiḥ [taduccaran] tanmantramuccārayan [kavacaṃ prākāraṃ] kavacaprākāraṃ [kuryād] vidadhyāt| [evameva hi] itthameva nityaṃ [svadhāmno 'pi] svanivāse kurvīta||
[kṣetraparigrāhiṇo dharmāḥ]
tataśca
children.translated_text:
[With abundant garlands, offerings, incense, and the like] — with plentiful garlands, food-offerings, incense, fragrances, and the like. [Having worshipped Śaṃkara established in the chosen liṅga] — the practitioner (sādhaka) whose Śiva is worshipped residing in the liṅga, being of that nature, for the purpose of claiming the ritual field, should install [the guardians of the directions] — Indra and the other direction-lords — [in stake-form] in stake-bodies — [in the directions] in the eastern and other directions.
Then, [with a thread-form] by means of a thread in the form of a channel (nāḍī), joining [them], one should perform the binding of the directions. [Outside] on the exterior of that, [reciting the blazing Māheśvara weapon-mantra] chanting the blazing supreme Parameśvara weapon-mantra, [one should draw a boundary-wall with ashes] one should trace a boundary-wall of ashes.
[Within that] inside that, [with all seed-syllables] with all seed-syllables, [empowered as armor and the like] consecrated as armor and so forth, [uttering that mantra] chanting that mantra, [one should make the armor-boundary] one should create the armor-boundary. [In this very way] thus indeed one should always do [this] also [in one's own dwelling] at one's own residence.
[The dharmas for claiming the ritual field:]
Then —
At the dwelling-stakes, [one should worship] the world-guardians
at twilight, every day.
In the outer enclosure, their weapons;
within, the concealer of offerings (<s>kṣetrapāla</s>, field-protector),
one should worship in one's own directional quarter;
on festival days, the guardians of the field's perimeter.
Vṛtti:
At the dwelling-stakes

children.text:
nivāsaparicchadahetuṣu dikṣvaṣṭasu niviṣṭeṣu śaṅkuṣu [lokeśān] indrādilokapālān [pradoṣe] rātryārambhe [prativāsaraṃ] pratyahaṃ pūjayet| [bāhyāvṛtau] bāhyaprākāranimittaṃ ca śakrādidigaṣṭake śaṅkuṣu [tadastrāṇi] vajrādyāyudhāni antarghanacchadam iti kavacādyāvaraṇaṃ ca yajet| [svadigbhāge] prāgukte nairṛtasthāne kṣetrapālaṃ yajet|
parv asu caturdaśyaṣṭamyādiṣu kṣetranemigān indrādilokapālān yajet| tathā hyuktaṃ prāk---
children.translated_text:
— at the stakes installed in the eight directions that serve as supports for the dwelling equipment — [one should worship the world-guardians] <s>Indra</s> and the other world-protectors — [at twilight] at the onset of night — [every day] daily. [In the outer enclosure] — for the purpose of the outer boundary-wall, at the stakes in the eight directions of <s>Śakra</s> and the rest, [their weapons] — the thunderbolt and other weapons — and the concealer of offerings, the armor-covering, one should worship. [In one's own directional quarter] — in the previously mentioned southwestern location, one should worship the <s>kṣetrapāla</s> (field-protector).
On festival days — on the fourteenth, eighth, and other [tithi days], one should worship the field-perimeter guardians, namely <s>Indra</s> and the other world-protectors. For it was previously stated —
'One should install the direction-lords — <s>Śakra</s> and the rest — in the directions, in stake-form.'
What is not available in the [ritual] field, that from afar,
brought by a helper, one should use.
Vṛtti:

children.text: siddhyarthaṃ parigṛhīte kṣetre yat kuśakusumasamidādi nāsti, taddūrād viprakṛṣṭād [sahāyopahṛtaṃ bhajed] anyataḥ sahāyenānayet|
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>kuśa</s> grass, flowers, firewood, and the like are not available in the field claimed for accomplishment — that, from a distant [place], [brought by a helper, one should use] one should have it brought from elsewhere by a helper.
Objection: It was previously specified that a field lacking nearby firewood, flowers, kuśa grass, and water should not be taken.

children.text:
iha ca dūrātsahāyena tadānayanokteḥ prāgvyākṛtaparāmarśato virodhaḥ| naiṣa doṣaḥ| kuśakusumasalilasamidvarjitamanyatphalamūlatṛṇendhanamṛdādi dūrāt sahāyenānayeditīha pratipādyate| tanna kaścidvirodhaḥ|
yadvā dūrasamitpuṣpakuśodakakṣetraniṣedhasūtre sakalānyaguṇopapannaṃ kṣetraṃ yadi syāttadādnīṃ dūrasamitpuṣpakuśodakasyāpi tasyāpariharaṇamityeṣṭavyameva| tacca `kṣetre yannāsti taddūrātsahāyenopahṛtaṃ bhajed' ityetatsūtrārambhasāmarthyātsiddhyati| tadetaduktam---
children.translated_text:
And here, the statement about bringing those from afar with a helper contradicts the earlier-explained rule. This is not a fault. Here it is taught that other things — fruits, roots, grasses, fuel, clay, and the like — apart from kuśa, flowers, water, and firewood, should be brought from afar with a helper. So there is no contradiction.
Alternatively, in the sūtra prohibiting a field with distant firewood, flowers, kuśa, and water — if a field endowed with all other good qualities were available, then even [one] with distant firewood, flowers, kuśa, and water should not be rejected — this is what should be accepted. And this is established by the force of the commencement of this sūtra: 'What is not in the field, that from afar, brought by a helper, one should use.' This is what was stated —
'[This sūtra] serves to resolve the earlier-explained rule.'
One should not leave the accomplishment-field
and go even a step elsewhere.
The <s>mantra</s> [becomes accomplished] through recitation of lakhs [equal to the number of] syllables,
and through fire-offering (<s>homa</s>) of one-tenth [of that amount],
and by following the conduct prescribed
in one's own scripture — [the mantra] becomes accomplished.
Vṛtti:
Having not left the accomplishment-field

children.text: siddhikṣetrāvasthitaḥ sādhakastattyaktvā padamapi na anyato [vrajed] gacchet| [mantro varṇalakṣajapād] mantras ca sādhyasya yāvanto varṇāstāvallakṣajapāt [daśamāṃśato homācca] taddaśāṃśahomāt [svaśāstravihitāṃ vṛttimāsthitasya prasiddhyati] svaśāstrāmnātacaryācaraṇācca siddhiḥ||
children.translated_text: — the practitioner established in the accomplishment-field, having not abandoned it, should not go even a step elsewhere. [The mantra, through recitation of lakhs equal to the syllables] — the mantra [is accomplished] through recitation of as many lakhs as the mantra to be accomplished has syllables. [And through homa of one-tenth] — and through fire-offering of one-tenth of that [amount]. [By following the conduct prescribed in one's own scripture, it becomes accomplished] — and through practicing the conduct taught in one's own scripture, accomplishment [is attained].
Rules for expiation (prāyaścitta):
When a transgression has occurred, one should perform
the expiation established by rule.
If [done] unintentionally; but if intentionally, one should perform
that very [expiation] threefold — [says] the wise one.
Vṛtti:
Unintentionally

children.text: anicchātaḥ [saṃjātavyutkramaḥ] svaśāstrāmnātavidhyatikrame [vidhisthitaṃ] tacchāstropadiṣṭaṃ prāyaścittaṃ kuryāt| [kāmataḥ] icchātaḥ triguṇam| sudhīriti suṣṭhu śobhanā tadanuṣṭhāne pravaṇā dhīryasya saḥ||
children.translated_text: — without desire. [When a transgression has occurred] — when a transgression of the procedure taught in one's own scripture [has occurred], [established by rule] one should perform the expiation taught in that scripture. [Intentionally] — with desire — threefold. 'Wise' (sudhī) means one whose intelligence is well-inclined, beautiful, directed toward the performance of that [expiation].
Thus —
When the daily observance of the practitioner is interrupted,
one should recite <s>Sadyojāta</s> ten thousand times,
or one hundred times with controlled breath (<s>prāṇāyāma</s>),
for one day, subsisting on air alone.
Vṛtti:
When the daily observance of the practitioner is interrupted

children.text:
ahnā nirvartyaḥ āhnikaḥ pratyahaṃ kāryo vidhiḥ sādhakasādhyaḥ prāgukto vidhiḥ, tasyecchāto vicchede tallope [sadyojātāyutaṃ] daśasahasrāṇi sadyojātasya japet|
yadvā [vāsaraṃ mārutāśanaḥ] ekāhopoṣitaḥ [saṃyataprāṇaḥ] prāṇāyāmaśatena tameva [śataṃ] śataśo japet|
atra ca dūrasthādapi yathāyogaṃ prāktanamakāmakṛta ekaguṇatvaṃ kāmakṛte tu traiguṇyamabhisambandhanīyam||
children.translated_text:
— the daily observance (āhnika) is the procedure to be completed daily — the previously stated procedure that is the practitioner's duty. When it is interrupted intentionally, when it lapses — [one should recite Sadyojāta ten thousand times] one should recite the Sadyojāta [mantra] ten thousand times.
Alternatively, [for one day, subsisting on air alone] — having fasted for one day — [with controlled breath] with one hundred prāṇāyāmas, one should recite that very [mantra] [one hundred times] a hundred-fold.
And here, even for one who is far away, the previously [stated rule of] single measure for unintentional [transgression] should be connected as appropriate, and triple for intentional [transgression].
For a food-transgression, [one should recite] the <s>Vāma</s> [mantra];
for violence, [one should recite] the <s>Bahurūpin</s> [mantra];
for nocturnal emission,
one should recite the face [mantra] (<s>Vaktra</s>/<s>Tatpuruṣa</s>); by day, double that.
Vṛtti:

children.text:
saṃmyataprāṇo nirāhārī śataṃ [vāmasya] vāmadevasya anicchākṛte [annavyatikare] abhojyānnabhojane japet|
evaṃ hiṃsāyāṃ kṛtāyāṃ [bahurūpiṇaḥ] bahurūpaśatam| icchayā tattriguṇam|
rātrau [syandane] vīryotsarge [vaktrasya] tatpuruṣamantraṃ śataśo 'bhijapet| divā tu taddviguṇaṃ prāyaścittamācaret| atra cecchākṛtatvaṃ na sambhavatītyanicchaiva mukhyā||
children.translated_text:
With controlled breath, fasting, one should recite one hundred [times] [the Vāma mantra] the <s>Vāmadeva</s> [mantra] for an unintentional [transgression of] food — [for eating forbidden food] when eating food that should not be eaten.
Likewise, when violence has been committed, [the Bahurūpin mantra] one hundred [times] of the Bahurūpa [mantra]. If intentional, triple that.
For nocturnal [emission] — seminal discharge — one should recite the <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> mantra (<s>Vaktra</s>, face-mantra) a hundred-fold. By day, one should perform double the expiation. Here, since intentionality is not possible [in nocturnal emission], only the unintentional [case] is primary.
In the case of contact with food-remnants of a Brāhmaṇa and the rest,
one [should worship] with one of the face [mantras] and the rest, [with appropriate] quality,
by means of worship in the center of a four-petaled lotus;
in the [regular] place of that [mantra], one should worship the fifth [mantra, Īśāna].
Vṛtti:
In the case of contact with food-remnants of a Brāhmaṇa and the rest

children.text:
adīkṣitabrāhmaṇādyucchiṣṭasaṅkare
puruṣāghoravāmājā jātīśā brāhmaṇāditaḥ iti%
\quote{puruṣāghoravāmājā jātīśā brāhmaṇāditaḥ
${\rm \Kir\ 46:6cd.}$}
children.translated_text: — in the case of contamination by the food-remnants of an uninitiated Brāhmaṇa and the rest. 'The lords of the castes, beginning from Brāhmaṇas, are [born] from Puruṣa, Aghora, Vāma, and Aja [mantras respectively]' —

children.text:
śrīkiraṇoktatajjātyadhipatayaḥ kramād [vaktrādyanyatamaṃ guṇaṃ] tatpuruṣabahurūpavāmadevasadyojātamantrāḥ [daturdalābjamadhyeṣṭyā] caturdalapadmamadhyayogena pūjyāḥ|
evaṃ jātyanusāreṇa madhye 'rcya tatsthāne [pañcamam] īśānabhaṭṭārakaṃ [yajed] arcayet|
children.translated_text:
The lords of those castes as stated in the Śrī Kiraṇa [Āgama], in order — [one of the face mantras and the rest, with quality] the <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>, <s>Bahurūpa</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, and <s>Sadyojāta</s> mantras — [by means of worship in the center of a four-petaled lotus] should be worshipped using the method of a four-petaled lotus center.
Thus, having worshipped in the center according to caste-correspondence, in the [regular] place of that [mantra], [the fifth] — the <s>Īśāna Bhaṭṭāraka</s> — [should be worshipped] should be worshipped.

children.text:
evaṃ ca yadi brāhmaṇasyādīkṣitabrāhmaṇocchiṣṭasaṅkaro jātastadā tatpuruṣamantraṃ madhyadale 'bhyarcya pūrvadale īśānaḥ pūjanīyaḥ|
anye tu svashtāneṣveva| tasyaiva kṣatriyavaiśyaśūdrocchiṣṭasparśe bahurūpādimantrā madhye 'bhyarcyāḥ| tadīyasthāne tvīśsanamantraḥ|
evaṃ kṣatriyasyādīkṣitakṣatriyavaiśyocchiṣṭasparśe sati bahurūpādayaḥ prāguktakramādeva madhye, tatsthāne punarīśānabhaṭṭārakamantrakramaḥ||
children.translated_text:
Thus, if a Brāhmaṇa has had contamination by the food-remnants of an uninitiated Brāhmaṇa, then having worshipped the <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> mantra in the central petal, <s>Īśāna</s> should be worshipped in the eastern petal.
The others [are placed] in their own locations. For that same [Brāhmaṇa], in the case of touching food-remnants of a Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, or Śūdra, the <s>Bahurūpa</s> and other mantras should be worshipped in the center; and in their [regular] place, the <s>Īśāna</s> mantra.
Likewise, for a Kṣatriya — in the case of contact with food-remnants of an uninitiated Kṣatriya or Vaiśya — <s>Bahurūpa</s> and the rest in the center by the previously stated order, and in that place again the sequence of the <s>Īśāna Bhaṭṭāraka</s> mantra.
He states [the rules] for recitation and fire-offering —
Having fasted for six days, one should recite a lakh [of the mantra];
or while eating forest [food];
one should offer ten thousand oblations, if knowing;
double, for the purpose of purification.
Vṛtti:

children.text:
tasminyāge pūrvaṃ [śuddhikāraṇāt] śuddhihetoḥ dvijādyucchiṣṭasparśaśāntyai [ṣaḍahopoṣitaḥ] kramādekāhadvyahatryahaṣaḍahopoṣito [vanyāśano 'pi vā] vanyaiḥ nīvārādibhiḥ kṛtavṛttirvā yaṣṭavyamantraṃ lakṣaṃ japet|
yadi vājānataḥ sthito 'pyatikramastadā ayutaṃ juhuyāt| anyathā [dviguṇaṃ] taddviguṇam| japasya cāyameva kramaḥ| yathā homastathā japaḥ iti śruteḥ||
children.translated_text:
In that worship, first, [for the purpose of purification] for the sake of purification, for the pacification of contamination by food-remnants of Brāhmaṇas and the rest — [having fasted for six days] having fasted progressively for one, two, three, and six days — [or while eating forest food] or subsisting on wild grains (nīvāra) and the like — one should recite a lakh of the mantra to be worshipped.
If, however, one commits the transgression while knowingly established [in the rules], then one should offer ten thousand oblations. Otherwise, [double] double that. And the procedure for recitation is this very same. Because of the teaching: 'As the fire-offering, so the recitation.'
When there is contact with discarded offerings (<s>nirmālya</s>),
one should recite all the <s>Brahma</s> [mantras], a lakh each.
When eating discarded offerings,
one should recite a lakh of the entire collected scripture (<s>saṃhitā</s>).
Vṛtti:
When there is contact with nirmālya

children.text:
nirmālyasāṅkarye sati [sarvabrahmāṇi lakṣaśo japed] brahmamantrāḥ pratyekaṃ lakṣaśo japyāḥ|
[nirmālyabhojane] sākṣāttu tadbhojane [samagrasaṃhitālakṣaṃ japet] sādhyamantrasaṃhitāyāḥ śivaikādaśinyā ekaikamantralakṣaṃ japet||
children.translated_text:
— when contamination by discarded offerings occurs — [one should recite all the Brahma mantras, a lakh each] the Brahma mantras should each be recited a lakh times.
[When eating nirmālya] — but when actually eating that [discarded offering] — [one should recite a lakh of the entire collected scripture] one should recite a lakh of each mantra of the Śiva-ekādaśinī (eleven [mantras] of Śiva) of the mantra-saṃhitā to be accomplished.
<s>Vāma</s> and the rest are the lords of the <s>Śākyas</s> (Buddhists),
<s>Pādārthikas</s> (Jainas), and <s>Kāpālikas</s>;
<s>Ajāta</s> (<s>Sadyojāta</s>) is proclaimed as the lord
of those devoted to the threefold Veda and those bearing [sectarian] marks.
Purification for eating their food
is like purification for caste-contamination.
But for eating the food of a <s>Kāpālika</s>,
it is held [to require] the end of a lunar observance (<s>aindava-vrata</s>).
Vṛtti:
Of the Śākyas, Pādārthikas, and Kāpālikas

children.text:
saugatārhatamahāvratānāṃ [vāmādyāḥ] vāmadevāghoratatpuruṣāḥ patayaḥ|
[trayīnaiṣṭhikaliṅgināṃ] trayīnaiṣṭhikāḥ saṃnyāsāśramiṇaḥ anye ca liṅgino anyadarśanāmnātavratadhāriṇaḥ, teṣām [ajāto 'dhipatiḥ] sadyojātaḥ patiḥ| tadannabhojane [śuddhiḥ] prāyaścittaṃ [jātisamparkaśuddhivat] tadadhipatiścaturdalābjamadhye tatsthāne ca īśānabhaṭṭārakaḥ|
children.translated_text:
— of the Buddhists, Jainas, and Mahāvratins — [Vāma and the rest] <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Aghora</s>, and <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> are the lords.
[Of those devoted to the threefold Veda and those bearing marks] — those devoted to the threefold Veda are the renunciants (saṃnyāsins); and others bearing marks are those who observe vows taught in other doctrines. Of these, [Ajāta is the lord] <s>Sadyojāta</s> is the lord. For eating their food, [purification] the expiation [is] like purification for caste-contamination — that lord in the center of a four-petaled lotus, and in that place <s>Īśāna Bhaṭṭāraka</s>.

However, [for eating the food of a Kāpālika] when eating the food of a Mahāvratin — [it is held to require the end of a lunar observance] purification is achieved by performing such a worship at the completion of the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> vow.
But if their food has not been eaten, then he states —
One should recite a lakh of <s>Īśāna</s>
for purification from that contamination.
In the case of contamination with a <s>Kāpālika</s>,
three lakhs, with observance of self-restraint.
Vṛtti:
For purification from that contamination

children.text: sāṅkaryamātre jāte tu tacchuddhyai lakṣam īśānasya japet| [kāpālikasaṃkrame] kāpālikasaṅkare tu [kṛtasaṃyamaḥ] triṣavaṇasnāto nirāhāraḥ trīṇi lakṣāṇi||
children.translated_text: — when mere contamination has occurred, for its purification one should recite a lakh of <s>Īśāna</s>. [In the case of Kāpālika contamination] — in the case of contamination with a <s>Kāpālika</s> — [with observance of self-restraint] bathing three times daily and fasting — three lakhs.
When the <s>liṅga</s> is lost through carelessness,
or when the rosary (<s>akṣasūtra</s>) falls,
one should recite a lakh of <s>Maheśa</s> (the Great Lord),
and then re-acquire [new ones].
Vṛtti:
When the liṅga or rosary is lost through carelessness or falls

children.text: daivānmānuṣādvā prabalālliṅgākṣasūtrayorhāritayorbhraṣṭayorvā [maheśasya lakṣaṃ japet] parameśvaramantralakṣajapaṃ kṛtvā [punaḥ parigrahaṃ kuryāt] punarguṇotkṛṣṭayoranyayoḥ saṃgrahaṃ kuryāt||
children.translated_text: — when the liṅga and rosary, whether through divine [cause], human [cause], or superior force, are lost or fallen — [one should recite a lakh of Maheśa] having performed a lakh of recitation of the <s>Parameśvara</s> mantra — [one should then re-acquire] one should then acquire other ones of superior quality.
When there is a fall or a break [of the liṅga],
one-tenth is prescribed, O sage.
For other [cases], half the base amount,
or a thousand for the most minor [case].
Vṛtti:

children.text:
janite bhaṅge bhraṃśe vā prāgukto vidhiḥ| yadi tu [tadanyatra] pūjāvisraṃsananirmālyamadhyapātādyādvā janite bhraṃśe adhaḥpāte liṅgasya akṣasūtrasya vā tadā [daśāṃśaḥ] taddaśāṃśo vihitaḥ| ayutaṃ japedityarthaḥ|
tāvanapi vyājo yatra notpātaḥ tathāvidhe bhadrapīṭhād āsanādvā bhraṃśe jāte [ardhamūlaṃ] tato 'pyardhaṃ pañca sahasrāṇi|
[sulaghīyasi] suṣṭhu laghīyasi alpe karacalane skhalane bhadrapīṭhe vā āsane vā karādvicyāve sahasraṃ japaḥ||
children.translated_text:
When a break or fall has occurred, the previously stated rule [applies]. But if [it is] for other [reasons] — such as a fall during worship, falling among discarded offerings, and the like — when a break or downward fall of the liṅga or rosary [occurs], then [one-tenth] one-tenth of that is prescribed — one should recite ten thousand, is the meaning.
Even that much, where there is no [such] cause — in a fall from a pedestal or seat of that nature — [half the base amount] half of that again, five thousand.
[For the most minor case] — for something extremely minor — a movement of the hand, a slip, or [a fall] from a pedestal or seat, or a slipping from the hand — a thousand recitations.
And likewise, when [the liṅga is] seen by a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>, uninitiated person),
when touched, one should recite tenfold.
For a break of the counting-thread [of the rosary], half of the 'lost' [amount]
removes the fault.
And abandonment [is required] when [the liṅga/rosary is] touched
by phlegm, feces, or urine — except for metal [ones].
Vṛtti:

children.text:
iṣṭaliṅge akṣasūtre vā [paśunā] adīkṣiteṇa dṛṣṭe sahasraṃ japet|
spṛṣṭe tu [daśaguṇaṃ japed] ayutaṃ japyam| saṃkhyāsūtrasya ityakṣasūtrasya akasmād [guṇacchede] sūtrasya cchede hāritārthaṃ lakṣārdhaṃ doṣanut|
[kaphaviṇmūtraspṛṣṭasya kaphādispṛṣṭasya tyāgaḥ kāryaḥ| anyatra taijasād iti hemādilohasya duṣṭasya tenaiva dravyeṇa punarghaṭanaṃ na tu tyāga iti| ayaṃ ca liṅgākṣasūtravidhiḥ sādhakādanyatrāpi vijñeyaḥ||
children.translated_text:
When the chosen liṅga or rosary [is] seen by a paśu (uninitiated person) — one should recite a thousand.
When touched — [one should recite tenfold] ten thousand should be recited. For the counting-thread — that is, the rosary — when the thread breaks unexpectedly, [half of the lost amount] half a lakh removes the fault.
[Abandonment is required when touched by phlegm and the rest] — when touched by phlegm and the like, abandonment should be made. [Except for metal] — but for [objects made of] gold and other metals, the contaminated [item] can be refashioned from that very material, not abandoned. And this rule regarding liṅga and rosary should be understood as applying to others besides the practitioner as well.
If through carelessness one approaches a woman,
one should practice ten thousand <s>prāṇāyāmas</s>.
Fivefold doubled, for purification —
preceded by the utterance of <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ).
[Vṛtti:]
Through inadvertence, having gone to a woman

children.text: anicchayā nikhilāni balīvardanyāyena pramādāt pramadayā kṛtapariṣvaṅgasya tadupabhoge [praṇavoccārasaṃśritaṃ] praṇavoccārapuraḥsaraṃ [prāṇāyāmāyutaṃ bhajet] prāṇāmāyadaśasahasraṃ kuryāt|
children.translated_text: — for one who, without intention, like the bull forced [to work], through inadvertence has embraced a woman and enjoyed her — [preceded by the utterance of <s>Praṇava</s>] preceded by the utterance of <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ), [one should perform <s>prāṇāyāma</s> ten thousand times] one should perform ten thousand <s>prāṇāyāmas</s>.

children.text: Brunner (1985:406, n.2) acknowledges that the above appears to be
corrupt and advocates punctuating after balīvardanyāyena. But
icchayā tu [dvipañcaguṇitaṃ] taddaśaguṇaṃ japet| lakṣaṃ vidadhyād ityarthaḥ||
children.translated_text: But with intention, [double five-fold] — tenfold that amount should be recited. The meaning is: one should perform one hundred thousand.
When connected with a great sin (<s>mahāpātaka</s>),
ten thousand [recitations of] the <s>Śivaikādaśikā</s> —
one should recite tenfold, controlling the breath,
subsisting on fruits and roots.
For [sins] equal to those, the same [applies],
except without the breath-control.
[Vṛtti:]
When connected with a great sin

children.text: `brahmahatyā surāpānaṃ steyaṃ gurvaṅganāgamaḥ| tatsamparkaśca' iti mahāpātakāni|
children.translated_text: — 'Killing a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, drinking liquor, theft, going to the teacher's wife, and association with [those who have committed] those' — these are the great sins.

children.text:
ebhiranicchātaḥ saṃyoge [śivaikādaśikāyutaṃ] śivaikādaśikāyāḥ saṃhitāyā ayutaṃ japet| icchayā tu [prāṇasaṃyamī] saṃyataprāṇaḥ [phalamūlabhuk] phalamūlāśanaḥ tadeva daśaguṇaṃ japet|
[tatsameṣu] etatsameṣūpapātakeṣu [prāṇāyatiṃ vinā] prāṇāyāmavarjyam [evameva syād] eṣa eva vidhiḥ||
children.translated_text:
When connected with these unintentionally — [ten thousand of the <s>Śivaikādaśikā</s>] one should recite ten thousand [repetitions] of the <s>Śivaikādaśikā</s> hymn. But with intention — [controlling the breath] with breath controlled, [subsisting on fruits and roots] eating fruits and roots, one should recite tenfold that very amount.
[For those equal to those] — for the secondary sins (<s>upapātakas</s>) equal to these — [without the breath-control] excluding <s>prāṇāyāma</s> — [the same should apply] this very rule applies.
For sins other than those,
and for lapses in ritual practice,
one should recite the eleven [mantras of <s>Śiva's</s> faces] with their limbs,
or one [mantra of] <s>Brahman</s> in the middle.

children.text: Brunner (1985:407) suggests that the sense is
japedekādaśajātam, `he should recite the group of
eleven [brahma and aṅga mantras]', and that the long ā (which
confusingly suggests sadyojāta) is metrically required.

children.translated_text: [Vṛtti:]
For sins

children.text: tebhyo mahāpātakopapātakebhyo yānyanyāni pātakāni tattaddravyāpaharaṇaniṣiddhānnabhakṣaṇādīni teṣu teṣvapi [tadanyeṣu kriyāvyatikareṣu] anyeṣu ca kriyācchidreṣu [ekādaśa] śivavaktrāṇyaṅgasahitāni japet| yadvā tattadanusāreṇa bahurūpanāthamevāvartayet||
children.translated_text: — those sins other than those great sins and secondary sins — such as stealing various articles, eating forbidden food, and the like — in those too, and [for other lapses in ritual practice] in other deficiencies of ritual — [eleven] one should recite the [mantras of <s>Śiva's</s>] faces together with their limbs. Or one should repeat only <s>Bahurūpanātha</s> in accordance with each [case].

children.text: The edition inserts [ajātam ekaṃ] before bahurūpanātham,
as though the text meant `sadyojāta with aghora'; but, as Brunner
points out, what is probably rather intended is that jātam means
group and construes with pāda c; pāda d means then `the one [mantra]
that is in the centre of the brahmamantras [viz. aghora]'.

children.translated_text: Nothing should be accepted — any material
procured by one connected with sin through friendship.
One who takes [something] through ignorance
should perform half of what was previously stated.
[Vṛtti:]
By a follower of one connected with the previously stated great sins and the like,

children.text: Thus correction of \Brunner; \Bhatt\ reads: [jātāṃhasaḥ sakhyā] pūrvoktamahāpātakādiyogino 'nucareṇa [hṛtaṃ] [kārakaṃ]

yathoktāmatropakaraṇādi [na kiñcid grāhyaṃ] na kiṃcid gṛhṇīyāt|
kiṃcid [aparijñānād] ajñānād [ādadānaḥ] gṛhṇan [pūrvoktād ardham] tattanmahāpātakayoginaḥ prāyaścittaṃ yatpūrvamuktaṃ tadardham ācaret||
children.translated_text:
[nothing should be accepted] — one should not accept any of the materials, implements, and the like stated above.
If one [through ignorance] unknowingly [takes] accepts something — [half of what was previously stated] one should perform half the expiation stated previously for one connected with that particular great sin.
When [the sin-]connection extends over many days,
[the expiation is] equal, because of acquiring the same nature [through association].
Knowing this, the wise practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>)
should choose a companion of good qualities —
one endowed with same caste and noble birth,
younger, superior in qualities;
a <s>putraka</s> (son-initiate), or one observing the vows (<s>samayastha</s>),
or, failing that, another who is very affectionate.
[Vṛtti:]
When the sin-connection extends over many days

children.text: sañjātapātakena sakhyānekāhike samparke sati [tulyaṃ] tatsamameva sādhakasya prāyaścittam|
children.translated_text: — when there is association for more than one day with one who has committed sin — [equal] the expiation of the practitioner is equal to that [of the sinner himself].
Because of acquiring the same nature

children.text: tatsādharmyaprāpteḥ| evaṃ buddhvā tadvidā sādhakena sadguṇaḥ satkuśalaḥ tadalābhe samānajātiḥ kanīyān guṇajyeṣṭhaḥ putrakaḥ samayī vā tayorabhāve anyaḥ kaścit susnigdhaḥ sahāyo yojanīyaḥ||
children.translated_text: — because of attaining the same nature as that [sinner]. Having understood this thus, the practitioner knowing this should employ a companion of good qualities — of excellent wholesomeness; failing that, one of the same caste, younger, superior in qualities; a <s>putraka</s> (son-initiate) or one observing vows; or failing those two, some other very affectionate companion.
The <s>sādhaka</s>-prescribed vow should be performed
by the teacher who is a non-vow-holder and not under his own control.
Double [should be performed by] one under his own control; for as long
[should] a vow-holder not under his own control perform.
[Vṛtti:]

children.text:
deśiko mantravṛttiśca putrakaḥ samayī ca yaḥ|
catvāra ete śaivāḥ syurvratino 'vratino 'pi vā|| iti pūrvamuktatvāt
children.translated_text: 'The <s>deśika</s> (preceptor), the mantra-practitioner (<s>mantravṛtti</s>), the <s>putraka</s>, and the <s>samayī</s> — these four are <s>Śaiva</s>, whether vow-holders or non-vow-holders.' Since this was stated previously,

children.text:
avratī yo guruḥ asvavaśa ityanicchuḥ kṛtapātakaḥ sa prāguktānāṃ pātakānāṃ nivṛttyai sādhakoktam uditaṃ vrataṃ kuryāt|
dviguṇaṃ svavaśa iti, kāmataḥ kṛtapātako guruḥ sādhakoktaṃ vrataṃ dviguṇamācaret| tāvaccaredasvavaśo vratīti, yadi punaranicchākṛtapāpo vratī sa dviguṇamevācaret||
children.translated_text:
a non-vow-holder teacher who is 'not under his own control' — meaning unwilling, having committed sin [inadvertently] — he should perform the vow stated for the <s>sādhaka</s> for the removal of the previously stated sins.
'Double, under his own control' — a teacher who has committed sin intentionally should perform double the vow stated for the <s>sādhaka</s>. 'For as long should a vow-holder not under his own control perform' — but if a vow-holder has committed sin without intention, he should perform exactly double.
One under his own control — triple; one-third less
without that — a <s>putraka</s> should perform.
Half of the <s>putraka's</s> [expiation] — for a <s>samayī</s>,
for the previously stated and unstated sins.
[Vṛtti:]

children.text:
sa eva guruḥ svavaśa icchākṛtapātakaścet [triguṇaṃ] vratamanutiṣṭhet|
itthaṃ sakāmākāmatvena vratitvāvratitvabhedena ca guroścaturdhā prāyaścittamuktam| adhunā putrakaṃ pratyucyate| tryaṃśaṃ vinā tatputrakaścaret| svavaśastadicchāvān putrakaḥ sādhakoktāt tribhāgaṃ prāyaścittaṃ caret|
sa evānicchāvān vratī tryaṃśaṃ vineti dvibhāgamevānutiṣṭhet prathamasamayinaḥ| putrakārdhaṃ tu iti, putrakoktād vratādardhaṃ samayī pūrvoktānuktapāpmanāṃ prāguktānāmanuktānāṃ ca pāpānāṃ śāntaye vrataṃ kuryāt||
children.translated_text:
That same teacher, if under his own control — one who has committed sin intentionally — [triple] should observe the vow.
Thus, through the distinctions of intentional/unintentional and vow-holder/non-vow-holder, fourfold expiation for the teacher has been stated. Now it is stated for the <s>putraka</s>: 'One-third less without that — a <s>putraka</s> should perform.' An intentional <s>putraka</s> should perform one-third of the <s>sādhaka</s>-prescribed expiation.
That same one, if unintentional and a vow-holder — 'one-third less' — should observe only two-thirds, [like] the first <s>samayī</s>. 'Half of the <s>putraka's</s>' — the <s>samayī</s> should perform half the vow stated for the <s>putraka</s>, for the pacification of the previously stated and unstated sins.
Or, every six months a <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance),
or every year a <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar fast),
a <s>parāka</s> (twelve-day fast), or a <s>taptakṛcchra</s> (hot penance) —
the mantra-practitioner with his companion should perform;
desiring unobstructed success;
the other three — for the purpose of liberation.
[Vṛtti:]

children.text:
asaṃviditapātakavicchittyai [nirvighnasiddhimanvicchan] nirvighnasiddhiprepsuḥ [sānucaraḥ] sasahāyaḥ [mantrī] sādhakaḥ [itare trayaḥ] tadanye ca deśikaputrakasamayinastrayaḥ [muktyarthaṃ] vighnavarjitamuktyarthaṃ pratiṣaṇmāsaṃ kṛcchramācareyuḥ|
[athavā] yadvā [pratyabdaṃ] prativarṣam [aindavaṃ] cāndrāyaṇaṃ parākaṃ taptakṛcchraṃ vā kuryuḥ| kṛcchracāndrāyaṇādilakṣaṇaṃ tantrāntarājjñeyam| yathoktaṃ śrīmatkiraṇe---
children.translated_text:
For the cessation of sins not known [to have been committed] — [desiring unobstructed success] one who desires success without obstacles — [with his companion] with his helper — [the mantra-practitioner] the <s>sādhaka</s> — [the other three] and the three others — preceptor, <s>putraka</s>, and <s>samayī</s> — [for the purpose of liberation] for liberation free from obstacles — should perform a <s>kṛcchra</s> every six months.
[Or] alternatively, [every year] each year, [a <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>] a lunar fast, or a <s>parāka</s>, or a <s>taptakṛcchra</s>. The definition of <s>kṛcchra</s>, <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>, and the like is to be known from other tantras. As stated in the blessed <s>Kiraṇa</s>:

children.text:
ekabhuktaṃ tryahaṃ kuryāttryahaṃ tu yadayācitam|
tryahaṃ syānnaktabhojī tu tryahaṃ syānmārutāśanaḥ||
eṣa kṛcchraḥ samākhyātaḥ prājāpatya iti smṛtaḥ|
māsārdhaṃ grāsavṛddhiḥ syācchukle kṛṣṇe tu hrāsayet||
cāndrāyaṇavidhiḥ proktaḥ iti
children.translated_text:
'One should eat once a day for three days, [then] three days what is unasked-for, three days eating at night, and three days subsisting on air.
This is called the <s>kṛcchra</s>, known as <s>Prājāpatya</s>.
For half a month, increase [food] by one morsel [daily] in the bright [fortnight]; in the dark, decrease [it].
This is declared to be the rule of <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>.'
Similarly:

children.text: dvādaśāhaṃ nirāhāraḥ parāka iti saṃsmṛtaḥ| iti|
children.translated_text: 'Twelve days without food is known as <s>parāka</s>.'
Similarly:

children.text:
tryahamuṣṇaṃ pibedvāri tryahaṃ kṣīraṃ tathā pibet|
tryahamuṣṇaṃ ghṛtaṃ pītvā tryahaṃ vai kevalaṃ tataḥ||
taptakṛcchro 'yamākhyātaḥ iti
children.translated_text:
'For three days one should drink hot water, for three days drink milk, for three days drink hot ghee, and then three days with nothing at all.
This is declared to be the <s>taptakṛcchra</s>.'
Now the <s>Pavitra</s> (purificatory) ceremony
Another rite for these [practitioners] is stated,
which removes all deficiencies.
Which was obtained by the gods from <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>)
through austerity, for the strengthening of their own rites.
[Vṛtti:]

children.text: eṣāṃ sādhakādīnāṃ [sarvacchidrāpahaḥ] samayalopādijasakalacchidrāpahaḥ [anyo] yaḥ pavitrākhyo vidhiḥ prāg devaiḥ [harāt] parameśvarāt tapasā [prāptaḥ] labdhaḥ sa eveṣāmeva [svavidhipuṣṭaye] svavidhipuṣṭyarthaṃ [nigadyate] ucyate||
children.translated_text: For these practitioners and the rest — [removing all deficiencies] removing all deficiencies arising from breaches of observance and the like — [another] the rite called <s>Pavitra</s>, which was formerly [obtained] received by the gods from [<s>Hara</s>] <s>Parameśvara</s> through austerity — that very same is [stated] said for these same [practitioners], [for the strengthening of their own rites] for the purpose of strengthening their own rites.
In [the month of] <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, or at its end,
or in <s>Nabhasya</s> (Bhādrapada), in the manner to be described —
having produced the <s>Pavitra</s> of <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),
one should complete the annual rite.
[Vṛtti:]

children.text:
śrāvaṇe māsi [tadupānte vā] saḥ śrāvaṇa upānto yasya kālasya sa tadupānaḥ kālaḥ| āṣāḍhapaurṇamāsī vā caturdaśī vā tasmin| yathoktaṃ śrīmanmaye---`āṣāḍhyāścādime 'hani' iti|
nabhasye vā iti bhādrapade|
children.translated_text:
In the month of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>; [or at its end] — that time at whose end <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> is, is 'its end' (<s>tadupānta</s>); either the full moon of <s>Āṣāḍha</s> or the fourteenth [day] — on that [day]. As stated in the blessed <s>Maya</s> [tantra]: 'On the first day of <s>Āṣāḍhī</s>.'
Or in <s>Nabhasya</s> — meaning in <s>Bhādrapada</s>.

children.text: eteṣvanyatame kāle ucyamānavat vakṣyamāṇarītyā śambhoḥ pavitramāpādya maheśvaramūrdhni pavitrāṇyāropya vārṣikaṃ vidhiṃ pūrayet pratyabdamanuṣṭheyaṃ nityāṅgabhūtaṃ prāyaścittātmakaṃ vidhiṃ samāpayet
children.translated_text: On one of these times, in the manner to be described — having produced the <s>Pavitra</s> of <s>Śambhu</s>, having placed the purificatory threads upon <s>Maheśvara's</s> head, one should complete the annual rite — should accomplish the rite that is to be performed annually, that is an essential permanent observance, that is of the nature of expiation.

children.text: The above bracketed portion is presumably an addition of the editor;
what follows below is a fragment transmitted `au début du Yogapāda'
of a single MS: GOML D5470 (Bhatt's \msC). It appears to be a fragment
of instructions about liṅgapratiṣṭhā, to which a forward reference
was made by \Narayana\ earlier in his commentary on the caryāpāda,
and which therefore probably also belonged to the caryāpāda:
